articles.title: 3D Terrain
articles.summary: See the satellite map on the real shape of the land in Ride Mode and Map Mode, with contour lines and peak heights in feet, and tilt and turn it.
articles.text:
---
title: 3D Terrain
summary: See the satellite map on the real shape of the land in Ride Mode and Map Mode, with contour lines and peak heights in feet, and tilt and turn it.
category: routes-maps
order: 52
release: "2.1"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/components/mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/mapbox-map.web.tsx
  - app/src/components/group-mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/nav-mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/trail-map-overlay.tsx
  - app/src/core/terrain.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-trail-map.ts
  - app/src/lib/terrain.ts
  - app/src/lib/terrain-offline.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-panel-fold.ts
related: [map-layers, offline-maps, ride-mode, navigation-mode]
keywords: [3d, 3d map, terrain, elevation, contour, contour lines, topo, peaks, mountains, tilt, pitch, mapbox, hills, ridges, tablet]
---

3D Terrain shows the satellite map draped over the real shape of the land, so you can see ridges, canyons and climbs before you ride them. Contour lines and peak heights are drawn on top, along with every trail layer.

## Turn On 3D Terrain

1. Open Ride Mode or Map Mode.
2. Tap the round **Map Settings** button (two sliders) in the top-left corner of the map.
3. Under **Map Style**, tap **3D Terrain**.

The map tilts to show the land in 3D. To lay it flat again, tap **Satellite** or **Topo** under **Map Style**.

Your choice is remembered and used in Ride Mode and Map Mode. Other maps, like the route builder and Find a Ride, show plain satellite while 3D Terrain is picked.

3D Terrain is a map style, so like the other map styles it's a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Move Around in 3D

- **Tilt**: drag up or down with two fingers. The further you tilt, the steeper the land is drawn: looking straight down it's true to life, and at the steepest tilt hills and canyons stand up to three times their real height, so a ridge reads at a glance. Tilt back and it settles down again.
- **Turn**: twist with two fingers. The compass in the corner shows north; tap it to face north again.
- **Zoom and pan**: pinch and drag, as on any map.

On the website, right-drag or hold Ctrl and drag to tilt and turn (two fingers on a touch screen), or use the zoom, compass and tilt buttons in the bottom-left corner. Tilting further raises the land there too.

## What's on the Map

- **Contour lines**: thin white lines, with every fifth line heavier and labeled in feet when you zoom in.
- **Peaks**: mountain names with their height in feet.
- **Trails and roads**: the same public trail, road, closure and rider trail lines as the flat maps. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).
- **Your ride**: rider dots, the route, waypoints, planned stops and the regroup pin in Ride Mode; your recording, followed trail, Track Line and the distance finder in Map Mode.

Follow Me and Center on Me work the same as on the flat map.

## With No Signal

3D Terrain needs a signal, or an area saved for it ahead of time. In [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps), add **3D Terrain** to a download. With no signal, the 3D map shows over saved areas; anywhere else the app shows the flat downloaded map instead, so you always have a map.

## On iPhone, iPad, Android and the Website

3D Terrain works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and tablets, and on the website in Ride Mode and Map Mode. Every map in the app is drawn by Mapbox from 2.1, so the other maps look the same as this one, just flat. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).

articles.title: Make Your Location Accurate
articles.summary: If a rider shows up a mile or more from where they really are, turn on Precise Location and, on Android, Google Location Accuracy, then calibrate.
articles.text:
---
title: Make Your Location Accurate
summary: If a rider shows up a mile or more from where they really are, turn on Precise Location and, on Android, Google Location Accuracy, then calibrate.
category: troubleshooting
order: 15
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/core/precise-location.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-precise-location.ts
  - app/src/lib/location.ts
  - app/src/core/bubble.ts
related: [troubleshooting, location-sharing, ride-mode, ride-bubble]
keywords: [wrong location, miles away, approximate, precise location, google location accuracy, calibrate, compass, gps, accuracy, android, dot in wrong place]
---

OnMyLead shows each rider where their phone says they are. If a rider sitting right next to you shows up a mile or two away, their phone is giving every app a rough location, not just OnMyLead. Open Google Maps or Apple Maps on that phone: if its blue dot is in the same wrong spot, follow the steps below on that phone.

## On Android

1. **Turn on precise location for OnMyLead.** Open **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Permissions > Location** and turn on **Use precise location**.
2. **Turn on Google Location Accuracy.** Open **Settings > Location > Location Services > Google Location Accuracy** and turn on **Improve Location Accuracy**. With it off, the phone has only GPS, and indoors or under trees the dot can land miles away.
3. **Calibrate.** Open Google Maps, tap your blue dot and choose **Calibrate**, then follow the steps (it may ask you to point the phone at buildings, or move it in a figure 8).

Menu names differ a little between phone makers. Search Settings for "precise" or "location accuracy" if you can't find them.

## On iPhone and iPad

1. Open **Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > OnMyLead** and turn on **Precise Location**.
2. If the dot still wanders, open **Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services** and turn on **Compass Calibration**.

## Everywhere

Go outside or near a window with a clear view of the sky for a minute. Then open Ride Mode again: the dot moves to where the rider really is with the next update.

:::release 2.0
## What OnMyLead Does for You

- **When you start sharing on Android**, OnMyLead asks once to change to a precise location if you allowed only an approximate one, and shows Android's prompt to turn on Google Location Accuracy if it's off.
- **Ride Mode shows a yellow banner** when your own location isn't sharp: **Precise Location Is Off**, **Google Location Accuracy Is Off**, or **Your Phone Has a Rough Location Right Now**. Tap it to fix it: Android asks or opens Location settings, iPhone and iPad open Settings, and a rough location shows the steps above.
- **Other riders see Approximate Location** in the riders list under a rider whose phone shares only a rough spot, so nobody goes looking for them a mile away.
- **[Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble)** leaves out the distance a rough location could be off by, so a rider beside you isn't called separated.
:::

articles.title: Change the Look (Light Mode, Themes and Color Blind Mode)
articles.summary: Switch between Dark, Light and Match Phone, pick one of four themes, and turn on Color Blind Mode.
articles.text:
---
title: Change the Look (Light Mode, Themes and Color Blind Mode)
summary: Switch between Dark, Light and Match Phone, pick one of four themes, and turn on Color Blind Mode.
category: account
order: 75
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-04
sources:
  - app/src/app/appearance.tsx
  - app/src/core/appearance.ts
  - app/src/core/color.ts
  - app/src/core/ink.ts
  - app/src/lib/appearance.ts
  - app/src/lib/appearance-sync.ts
  - app/src/constants/theme.ts
related: [sync-across-devices, ride-bubble, navigation-mode, battery-saver]
keywords: [appearance, theme, themes, skin, light mode, dark mode, match phone, color blind, colour blind, colorblind, accessibility, carbon, desert, forest, night navy, black]
---

OnMyLead starts in the dark Night Navy look. Go to **You** > **Appearance** to change it. The app redraws as soon as you tap, and it opens the same way next time.

:::release 2.0
Light mode, Match Phone and the themes are Pro features. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Dark mode, the Navy theme and Color Blind Mode stay free. If you picked a look before version 2.0, the app keeps it.
:::

## Mode

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Dark** | The dark look OnMyLead has always had. The default. |
| **Light** | Light backgrounds with dark text. Easier to read in bright sun. |
| **Match Phone** | Follows your phone's own Dark Mode setting and switches when your phone does. |

## Themes

Each theme comes in a dark and a light version. Buttons stay logo red and links stay logo blue in every theme.

- **Night Navy**: the classic OnMyLead look.
- **Carbon**: true black. On phones with an OLED screen it uses a little less battery.
- **Desert**: warm sand and dust tones.
- **Forest**: deep pine green.

The maps look the same in every theme, and so do the name tags on the map, so riders always read them the same way.

## Color Blind Mode

Turn on **Color Blind Mode** if red and green (or blue and yellow) are hard to tell apart. It changes:

- Rider status colors: OK is sky blue, falling behind is yellow and separated is orange-red, and Ride Mode adds a symbol (✓, ! or ✕) next to a rider who needs a look.
- Trail ratings, trail spots (obstacles, hazards, water crossings and viewpoints) and your Track Line days.

The Appearance screen shows a preview of these colors as you switch.

:::tip
Changing the look only changes how OnMyLead looks on your screen. Other riders don't see your choice.
:::

## On Your Other Devices

Your choice follows your account to every device you sign in on. A change from another device shows the next time you open the app (or right away if you just opened it), so the screen never changes in the middle of a ride. See [Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device](/help/sync-across-devices).

## On a Tablet

On iPad and Android tablets the four themes sit side by side in one row. Everything else works the same as on a phone.

summary: How join requests work on rides where the organizer approves riders, and how the waitlist fills open spots on a full ride.

related: [join-a-ride, create-a-ride, organizer-controls, invite-riders, notification-settings]
keywords: [approve, approval, request to join, pending, waiting, decline, waitlist, wait list, full ride, max riders, max vehicles, spots, tablet]
---

Organizers can choose to approve each rider on a public ride, and can cap how many riders or vehicles come along. Here's what happens on both sides.

## Rides That Need Approval

When creating a public ride, the organizer picks **I Approve Riders** under **Joining**. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).

### If You're Asking to Join

1. Open the ride page.
2. Tap **Request to Join**.

The page shows "Your request is waiting for the organizer." You get a notification when you're approved. Until then you don't see the exact meeting point or the group.

This is the same whether you found the ride on **Find** or opened it with its link, QR code or invite code. Only riders the organizer invited through a riding group skip approval. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders).

### If You're the Organizer

You get a notification when someone asks to join. Then:

1. Open the ride page. The **Riders** section shows a red count of requests waiting.
2. Tap **Riders**.
3. Under **Waiting for You**, tap **Approve** or **Decline** next to each rider.

If you set **Max Riders** or **Max Vehicles** and the ride is already full, a rider you approve goes on the waitlist instead. They move up automatically when a spot opens.

## The Waitlist

If the organizer set **Max Riders** or **Max Vehicles** and the ride is full, new riders go on the waitlist. That includes riders the organizer approves and riders invited through a riding group. The page shows "You're on the waitlist. You'll move up automatically if a spot opens."

When a rider leaves, riders on the waitlist move up in the order they joined, as long as they fit. You get a notification when you have a spot.

The **Spots** line on the ride page shows how full the ride is, like "8 of 10 vehicles". Riders on the ride can see how many are on the waitlist under the **Going** list.

## Leaving the Waitlist or a Request

:::until 2.0
Open the ride page and tap **Leave Ride**, or swipe left on the ride on the **Rides** tab and tap **Leave**.
:::

:::release 2.0
Open the ride page and tap **Withdraw** at the bottom, then confirm. Or swipe left on the ride on the **Rides** tab and tap **Leave**. You can ask again later with the ride's link or code.
:::

:::note
If the ride is cancelled, riders who asked to join or are on the waitlist get a notification and an email too.
:::

articles.title: See the Badge Leaderboard
articles.summary: See where you rank against other riders by badges earned, everywhere or in your country and state, and choose whether you're listed.
articles.text:
---
title: See the Badge Leaderboard
summary: See where you rank against other riders by badges earned, everywhere or in your country and state, and choose whether you're listed.
category: account
order: 26
release: "2.1"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/app/leaderboard.tsx
  - app/src/app/leaderboard-area.tsx
  - app/src/core/leaderboard.ts
  - app/src/core/areas.ts
  - app/src/lib/leaderboard.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261104050000_badge_leaderboard.sql
related: [badges-and-ranks, privacy, home-screen]
keywords: [leaderboard, leader board, ranking, top riders, compare, state, country, province, where you ride]
---

The **Leaderboard** ranks riders by the badges they earned by riding. Look at everyone, or narrow it to a country and then a state or province.

## Open the Leaderboard

- On **Badges**, tap **Leaderboard** under your rank.
- On **Home**, tap **Leaderboard** beside **Your Badges**.

You need to be signed in. It opens on the state or country you ride from, if you picked one.

## How Riders Are Ranked

- Each badge level you earn by riding counts once, the same as your rank: Bronze is 1, Silver 2, Gold 3, for up to 21 levels. See [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks).
- Ties go to the rider with more Gold, then more Silver, then whoever reached that total first.
- **OnMyLead Founder** and **Brand Ambassador** don't count, but they still show beside the rider's name.

Each row shows the place, the rider's picture and name with their top badge, their rank, where they ride from, their total levels and how many Gold, Silver and Bronze they hold. Tap a rider to open their profile.

Your own row is highlighted. If you're further down than the list goes, your place shows at the bottom.

## Filter by Country and State

1. Under **Country**, tap **Everywhere** or a country.
2. For the United States, Canada, Mexico and Australia, a **State** (or **Province**) row appears. Tap one, or **All of** the country.

Only places with riders on the board are listed, plus your own.

## Pick Where You Ride

Riders show on a country or state board only after they pick where they ride from.

1. On the Leaderboard, tap **Where You Ride**.
2. On iPhone, iPad and Android, tap **Use My Location** to fill it in. Your phone works out the country and state itself, and only those two are saved, never where you are.
3. Or pick your country (type to search) and then your state or province.
4. Tap **Save**.

To take it off, open **Where You Ride** and tap **Remove My Area**. On the website, pick it from the list (there's no **Use My Location** there).

## Leave the Leaderboard

Turn off **Show Me on the Leaderboard**. You disappear from every board right away, and you can still look at it. Turn it back on any time.

If **Who Sees Your Activity** in your Feed settings is **Nobody**, you start off the leaderboard until you turn **Show Me** on.

Riders you've blocked, or who blocked you, never see each other on the leaderboard. See [What Other Riders Can See](/help/privacy).

## On a Tablet

On an iPad or Android tablet, and on a wide window on the website, your place, **Where You Ride**, **Show Me** and the filters sit in a column beside the board.

articles.text:
---
title: Earn Badges and Ranks
summary: Earn Bronze, Silver and Gold badges for leading, riding, miles and trails, see your rank on the You tab, and spot other riders' top badge.
category: account
order: 25
release: "1.0.3"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

  - supabase/migrations/20261103900000_founder_badge.sql

related: [badge-leaderboard, ride-name-and-profile, leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner, ride-summary-and-ride-again, notification-settings]
keywords: [badges, leaderboard, brand ambassador, ambassador, founder, rank, ranking, achievements, levels, trail boss, tail gunner, crew rider, mile eater, trailblazer, mapmaker, trail scout, expert leader, legend]
---

Badges show what you have done on OnMyLead. Each badge has three levels, **Bronze**, **Silver** and **Gold**, and the levels you earn add up to your rank.

## The Badges

| Badge | What earns it | Bronze | Silver | Gold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Trail Boss** | Lead group rides | 1 ride | 10 rides | 25 rides |
| **Tail Gunner** | Ride at the rear as tail gunner | 1 ride | 10 rides | 25 rides |
| **Crew Rider** | Ride with a group | 1 ride | 10 rides | 50 rides |
| **Mile Eater** | Miles on your rides | 100 miles | 1,000 miles | 5,000 miles |
| **Trailblazer** | Share trails you mapped with every rider | 1 trail | 5 trails | 20 trails |
| **Mapmaker** | Your shared trails rated accurate by other riders | 1 trail | 5 trails | 20 trails |
| **Trail Scout** | Rate trails for accuracy | 5 trails | 25 trails | 100 trails |

Leading counts when you are the ride's leader as it ends: the organizer, or the rider the organizer made **Leader** or handed the lead to. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

## How a Ride Counts

- A ride counts once it ends.
- It counts for you when your own location track on that ride covers at least half a mile, so share your location in **Ride Mode** while you ride.
- **Trail Boss**, **Tail Gunner** and **Crew Rider** also need at least two riders with a track, so a ride you end on your own doesn't count toward them. Your miles on it still do.
- Miles come from your own track, with GPS jumps and time stopped left out, the same way as the ride summary.

:::release 2.0
Rough locations, GPS bounces and time with your location off are left out of your miles too, the same as the ride summary.
:::
- No signal on the trail? Your track uploads when your phone gets service again, and the ride counts then.

Badges are worked out by OnMyLead's server from what you really ride, so nobody can add one by hand. Once you earn a badge, you keep it.

:::release 2.0
## Brand Ambassador and OnMyLead Founder

OnMyLead gives two special badges. They have no Bronze, Silver or Gold, you can't earn them by riding, and they don't count toward your rank.

| Badge | Who has it | Looks like |
|---|---|---|
| **OnMyLead Founder** | The rider who started OnMyLead | A red patch with a flag planted on a summit |
| **Brand Ambassador** | Riders who represent OnMyLead | A blue patch with the OnMyLead mountains and red arrow |

If OnMyLead gives you one:

- You get a notification, for example **You're an OnMyLead Brand Ambassador**.
- It shows at the top of **Badges** and first in the badge row on the **You** tab.
- It shows beside your name instead of your top riding badge, and on the Feed and your profile.
:::

## Your Rank

Every level you earn counts once toward your rank. There are 21 levels in all.

| Rank | Levels earned |
|---|---|
| **Rookie** | 0 |
| **Rider** | 1 |
| **Veteran** | 4 |
| **Expert** | 9 |
| **Legend** | 15 |

## See Your Badges

1. Go to the **You** tab. Under your name you see your rank and a row of all seven badges. Earned badges are in their Bronze, Silver or Gold color; the rest are outlines.
2. Tap the row to open **Badges**.
3. Each badge shows its level, what earns it and how far you are from the next level, for example **4 of 10 rides led for Silver**.

A badge you just earned is marked **New** until you open **Badges**.

On a tablet, **Badges** shows two columns in portrait and three in landscape.

## When You Earn a Badge

You get a notification, for example **New Badge: Trail Boss Silver**. Tap it to open **Badges**. To turn these off, switch off **Badges and Pro Trial** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Other Riders' Badges

Each rider's top badge shows as a small patch beside their name in the ride's **Going** list, the **Riders** list in **Ride Mode** and the riders list beside the map on a tablet. Other riders see your badges and rank level, never your exact ride count or miles.

:::release 2.1
## The Leaderboard

See how your badge levels compare with other riders, everywhere or in your country and state, from **Leaderboard** on **Badges**. See [See the Badge Leaderboard](/help/badge-leaderboard).
:::

articles.title: Use Battery Saver
articles.summary: Choose how often your phone sends your location while you share, to make the battery last longer on long days.
articles.text:
---
title: Use Battery Saver
summary: Choose how often your phone sends your location while you share, to make the battery last longer on long days.
category: safety-privacy
order: 15
release: "1.0.1"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/app/battery.tsx
  - app/src/core/battery.ts
  - app/src/lib/battery.ts
  - app/src/lib/location.ts
related: [location-sharing, ride-mode, troubleshooting]
keywords: [battery, battery saver, battery life, power, gps, update rate, accuracy, low power, drain]
---

Sharing your location keeps the GPS on and sends your position to your group. Battery Saver lets you trade how often your group sees you move for a longer-lasting battery. It starts on **Best Accuracy**, which is what we recommend whenever you can charge your phone.

## The Three Settings

| Setting | Your dot updates about every | What your group notices |
|---|---|---|
| **Best Accuracy** (Recommended) | 15 seconds or 25 m (80 ft) | Your dot follows you closely. Best for following the leader and for finding someone who stopped. |
| **Balanced** | 30 seconds or 75 m (250 ft) | Your dot can trail up to 30 seconds behind you. |
| **Max Battery Saver** | 45 seconds or 200 m (650 ft) | Your dot can trail up to 45 seconds behind you and be off by up to about 100 m (330 ft). For multi-day trips with no way to charge. |

On every setting, a phone that is parked still checks in often enough that your group sees you as live, not as **No Signal**. Taps like **Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** always send right away.

Battery Saver also slows Ride Mode's own work on your phone: your blue dot on the route moves in bigger steps, and the backup check for other riders runs less often. Other riders still appear the moment their phones send.

## Change the Setting

1. Go to the **You** tab and tap **Battery Saver**. You can also tap **Change** next to **Battery Saver** at the bottom of **Share My Location**.
2. Tap the setting you want.
3. If you picked **Balanced** or **Max Battery Saver**, the app tells you what your group loses and asks you to confirm. Tap **Use Balanced** or **Use Max Battery Saver**, or **Keep Current** to leave it.

The change takes effect right away, even in the middle of a share. While you're on Balanced or Max Battery Saver, the sharing banner in Ride Mode shows the setting's name, and **Switch Back to Best Accuracy** is at the top of the Battery Saver screen.

:::note
Battery Saver is set on each phone or tablet separately, and other riders aren't told which setting you picked.
:::

## Other Ways to Save Battery

- Download an [offline map](/help/offline-maps) before you lose service, so the phone isn't searching for map tiles.
- Stop sharing when you don't need to. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
- Keep the phone on a charger or a 12V outlet on long rides.

articles.title: Share With Nearby Riders With No Service
articles.summary: With no cell service, riders on the same ride pass spots, status taps and messages to each other over Bluetooth, and phones pass them along the group.
articles.text:
---
title: Share With Nearby Riders With No Service
summary: With no cell service, riders on the same ride pass spots, status taps and messages to each other over Bluetooth, and phones pass them along the group.
category: ride-mode
order: 25
release: "2.1"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/core/nearby.ts
  - app/src/lib/nearby.ts
  - app/modules/onmylead-nearby/**
  - app/src/lib/outbox.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-broadcast.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-ride-chat.ts

  - app/src/components/ride-chat.tsx

  - supabase/migrations/20261104060000_bluetooth_sharing.sql
  - supabase/migrations/20261104100000_bluetooth_mesh.sql
related: [ride-mode, ride-chat, location-sharing, emergency-and-safety, status-buttons, offline-maps, battery-saver, privacy]
keywords: [bluetooth, no service, no signal, offline, dead zone, mesh, relay, nearby, out of range, no cell, message, talk, seen by, got it]
---

When there's no cell service, OnMyLead phones on the same ride talk to each other over Bluetooth. Riders close to you keep moving on your map, and your status taps, quick replies and typed messages reach them, with no service at all. Each phone passes on what it hears, so the rider at the back can reach the front through the riders in between. It works on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets, and they all work with each other.

Seeing nearby riders, sharing your spot, and sending messages over Bluetooth are part of OnMyLead Pro, including the free Pro Trial. On every plan, your phone passes everything along for the group, and status taps go out and come in over Bluetooth, so EMERGENCY, Need Help and Crash Alerts always get through, and so does the **I'm OK** that ends one. On Free, the switch shows the **Pro** tag. With service, everything works as always on every plan. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## What It Does

- **Spots.** If you're sharing your location with the ride, nearby riders on the ride see your dot move. Their details say **Via Bluetooth** when the spot came phone to phone. When one phone gets a newer spot for any rider, from Bluetooth or from the internet, it passes that on too, so everyone in range sees the freshest spot the group has.
- **Status taps and EMERGENCY.** A status you tap goes to nearby riders at once over Bluetooth, with or without service, and still sends over the internet when you have signal. An EMERGENCY alerts nearby riders just like it does with service, and always goes out first.

:::release 2.1
- **The Emergency Siren over Bluetooth.** An EMERGENCY from a nearby rider sounds the siren on your phone with no service, and a notification with the siren if OnMyLead is in the background. See [Hear the Emergency Siren](/help/emergency-siren).
:::
- **Quick replies and messages.** Your quick replies and the messages you type in Ride Mode reach nearby riders too. Their phones read them out loud, and they show in Ride Chat marked **Via Bluetooth**. Every Ride Mode message goes over Bluetooth whole, in any language.
- **Got it, seen it.** The card under your tap says who has it: **Reached (name) over Bluetooth** when their phone got it, and **Seen by (name)** once it showed on their screen. While your tap is **Waiting for Signal**, the card still names the nearby riders who got it over Bluetooth.
- **Passed along.** Each phone passes on what it hears, up to six phones down the line, so a strung-out group can still hear each other when the riders in between are in range.
- **A phone with service helps the rest.** Any phone on the ride that has signal puts what OnMyLead knows about the group, the other riders' spots, status taps and messages, on the air for the riders near it with none.
- **Uploaded when anyone gets signal.** When any phone on the ride gets service, it passes what it heard to OnMyLead, including messages and who has seen what, so riders elsewhere and people at home see the group too.

When it's working, the no-service banner in Ride Mode says **No Service. Sharing With 2 Nearby Phones Over Bluetooth.**

## Range

Bluetooth reaches about 30 to 100 meters (100 to 300 feet) between phones in the open, and less through trees, hills, bodies and steel. It works best when the group is bunched up, at a regroup, or riding close. Riders a half mile apart are usually out of range of each other unless riders in between pass it along.

Riders farther away than that show where they were last seen, as before. See [Use Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

## Before You Lose Service

- **Open Ride Mode once with service.** Your phone gets the ride's Bluetooth keys from OnMyLead then and keeps them for that ride. Joining a ride needs service.
- **Allow Bluetooth.** The first time, iPhone and iPad ask to use Bluetooth, and Android asks for **Nearby devices**. Say yes.
- **Keep Bluetooth on.** If Bluetooth is off in the phone's settings, nothing goes out.
- **Download the ride's map.** See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

## Turn It On or Off

Bluetooth Sharing is on by default. Turn it off or back on in either place:

- **You:** switch **Bluetooth Sharing** off or on.
- **Ride Mode:** when you have no service, the no-service banner has a **Bluetooth On** button. Tap it to turn Bluetooth Sharing off (it then says **Bluetooth Off**), and tap again to turn it back on. It starts again right away.

With it off, your phone doesn't use Bluetooth for OnMyLead at all. Your status taps, messages and location still go over the internet whenever you have service.

## Privacy

- Only riders who joined the ride can read what's sent. Everything is encrypted with a key that only the ride's joined riders get, and the key changes for every ride.
- Phones near you that aren't on your ride see only that an OnMyLead phone is nearby. They can't see your name, your ride or where you are.
- Your spot goes out only while you're sharing with the ride. Stop sharing and it stops.
- Each spot, tap, message and receipt carries a code that only your phone and OnMyLead can make, so nobody can upload a fake spot, put words in your mouth or mark your message seen for you.
- It runs only in Ride Mode, and ends when the ride ends.

## Battery

Bluetooth uses far less battery than GPS, but it adds a little to Ride Mode's battery use. The radio works hardest when you have no service or there are phones in range, which is when it matters. With service and nobody in range it idles, and with [Max Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver) on it slows down too. Phones that come into range are picked up either way.

## On Each Device

- **iPhone and iPad:** keeps working with the screen locked while you share with the ride. A locked iPhone can be a little slower to find other phones.
- **Android phones and tablets:** keeps working with the screen off while Ride Mode shows its sharing notification. An Android phone may not find a locked iPhone on its own; the iPhone finds the Android phone instead, and they then talk both ways.

## Good to Know

- Phones on Free still pass everything along, so a Free rider in the middle of the group never breaks the chain. A phone with Bluetooth Sharing switched off doesn't pass anything along.
- It isn't a satellite messenger. It doesn't reach 911 or anyone outside Bluetooth range. See [Emergency and Safety](/help/emergency-and-safety).
- Photos, polls, announcements and leader-only messages still need service.
- With no service, a message you get over Bluetooth shows in Ride Chat with **Via Bluetooth** until OnMyLead has it; then it looks like any other message.

articles.summary: During a ride, OnMyLead shows on your car's CarPlay screen with one-tap status buttons, your group, EMERGENCY and alerts when a rider falls behind.
articles.text:
---
title: Use OnMyLead on CarPlay
summary: During a ride, OnMyLead shows on your car's CarPlay screen with one-tap status buttons, your group, EMERGENCY and alerts when a rider falls behind.
category: ride-mode
order: 46

related: [ride-mode, status-buttons, emergency-and-safety, ride-bubble, leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner, music-controls]
keywords: [carplay, car play, car screen, dashboard, truck, jeep, car, apple carplay, android auto, head unit, infotainment]
---

If your truck, Jeep or car has Apple CarPlay, OnMyLead shows on the car's screen during a ride. You get big buttons for the status taps you use most, your group, and EMERGENCY, so you can keep your phone in the mount and your eyes on the trail.

CarPlay works with iPhone. iPad, Android phones and Android tablets don't have it, and OnMyLead doesn't support Android Auto.

CarPlay is part of OnMyLead Pro, including the Pro Trial. On a Free account the car screen says **CarPlay Is Part of OnMyLead Pro**, and Ride Mode, status taps and EMERGENCY keep working on your phone. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Start CarPlay

1. Connect your iPhone to the car, with a cable or wirelessly, the way you usually start CarPlay.
2. Tap **OnMyLead** on the car screen. If you don't see it, swipe across the car's home screen, or add it in your iPhone's **Settings** > **General** > **CarPlay** > your car > **Customize**.
3. Open **Ride Mode** for your ride on your phone. The car screen follows it.

Until Ride Mode is open on your phone, the car screen says **No Ride Running**.

## What's on the Car Screen

The top of the screen shows the ride's name and how the group is doing: **Group Together**, how many riders are separated, or the latest status another rider tapped.

The buttons:

- **Group** lists every rider on the ride, with the leader and tail gunner marked.
- **OK**, **Stopped**, **Need Fuel**, **Mechanical Issue** and **Need Help** send that status to the group, the same as tapping it in Ride Mode on your phone.
- **Regroup Here** shows for the organizer and leader. Other riders get **Running Late** in its place.
- **EMERGENCY** asks once, **Send EMERGENCY with your location to everyone on the ride?**, and tap **Alert My Group** to send it. **Cancel** sends nothing.

Typed messages, your own quick replies and the map stay on your phone. CarPlay only allows a few buttons, and typing while driving isn't safe.

## Alerts on the Car Screen

- When another rider taps a status, like **Need Fuel**, **Mechanical Issue**, **Need Help** or **EMERGENCY**, it pops up as an alert with their name. Tap **OK** to close it. **OK** taps don't alert anyone.
- The leader and the tail gunner also get an alert when a rider falls out of the [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble), the same alert the phone speaks.

## Language

The car screen uses the language you picked in OnMyLead. See [Language](/help/language).

## Troubleshooting

- **OnMyLead isn't on the car screen.** Update OnMyLead from the App Store, then reconnect your iPhone to the car.
- **The car screen says No Ride Running.** Open Ride Mode for your ride on your phone.
- **The car screen says CarPlay Is Part of OnMyLead Pro.** Your account is on Free. Check **You** > **Subscription** on your phone.
- **A button did nothing.** Status taps need the same signal as on your phone. With no service, they wait and send when you're back in range, just like in Ride Mode.

title: Check In

---

Checking in tells the organizer and the rest of the group that you're at the meeting spot and ready to ride.

## Check In

1. Open the ride page.
2. Tap **I'm Here and Ready**.

The button changes to "Checked in at" and the time you tapped it.

You can check in once you've joined the ride, until the ride ends. Checking in doesn't use your location. It does need a connection, so if the trailhead has no signal, check in before you lose it.

## See Who's Here

On the ride page, tap **Riders**. Riders who checked in show **Here** under their name in the **Going** list. Organizers use this to see who's made it before starting Ride Mode.

:::note
Once you've checked in, you can't undo it.
:::

:::tip
Need help getting to the meeting spot? Directions are on the ride page once you've joined. See [Directions](/help/directions).
:::

articles.text:

title: Contact Us
summary: Send the OnMyLead team a message from the app or the website about a problem, an idea, billing, your account or safety.
category: troubleshooting
order: 30
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06

related: [troubleshooting, faq, report-and-block, emergency-and-safety, manage-subscription, delete-account]
keywords: [contact, support, help, email, bug, problem, feedback, feature request, billing question, refund, customer service]
---

Questions, problems or ideas for OnMyLead go straight to the team at RUS Offroad. A real person reads every message.

:::warning
OnMyLead is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 911 or your local emergency number first.
:::

## Send a Message From the App

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Help**, tap **Contact Us**.
3. Under **What's It About?**, pick a topic:
   - **Something Isn't Working**
   - **Feature Request**
   - **Billing and Pro**
   - **Account and Sign-In**
   - **Safety or a Rider**
   - **General Feedback**
   - **Something Else**
4. Check **Your Name** (optional) and **Your Email**. If you're signed in, they're filled in for you.
5. Write **Your Message**. The hint under the box suggests what to include for your topic.
6. Tap **Send Message**.

You'll see **Message Sent**. We reply to the email you gave, usually within a day.

:::release 1.0.1
## Report a Bug

If something in the app isn't working, tell us with a screenshot so we can fix it fast.

1. Take a screenshot of the problem:
   - **iPhone**: press the side button and volume up together.
   - **iPad**: press the top button and a volume button together.
   - **Android phone or tablet**: press the power and volume down buttons together.
2. Go to the **You** tab. Under **Help**, tap **Report a Bug**. The form opens with **Something Isn't Working** already picked.
3. Tap **Add a Screenshot** and pick your screenshot. Tap **Change Screenshot** or **Remove** if you picked the wrong one.
4. Write what you tapped, what happened and what you expected, then tap **Send Message**.

Your report also includes your phone model, your OnMyLead version, the screen you were on before you opened the form, and a short log of what the app just did (the screens you opened, errors and requests that failed). The log never includes your location, your messages or anything you typed, and it's kept only in memory: it's gone when you close the app.

On onmylead.com/contact, pick **Something Isn't Working** to add a screenshot the same way. Your browser goes with the report instead of a phone model.
:::

## Send a Message From the Website

Go to onmylead.com/contact. The same form works there, and you don't need to sign in.

## Email Us

You can also email support@rusoffroad.com.

## Tips for a Quick Answer

- **Something Isn't Working**: tell us what you tapped, what happened and what you expected. The ride name helps if it's about a ride.
- **Billing and Pro**: purchases are billed by Apple, and refunds go through reportaproblem.apple.com. We're still glad to help.

On Android, the hint says purchases are billed by Google Play, with refunds through your Google Play order history.
- **Account and Sign-In**: if you sign in with a different email than the one on the form, tell us which.
- **Safety or a Rider**: to report a rider, you can also press and hold their message in a ride. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## Help and Support Page

:::until 2.0
Under **Help** on the **You** tab, **Help and Support** has short answers to common questions about joining rides, location and battery, Pro, blocking and deleting your account.
:::

:::release 2.0
Under **Help** on the **You** tab, **Help and Support** has short answers to common questions about joining rides, location and battery, Pro, blocking and deleting your account. Under each answer, **Read the Guide** opens the full guide for that topic.

## Open These Guides From the App

The step-by-step guides you're reading now (onmylead.com/help) are one tap away in the app:

- On the **You** tab, under **Help**, tap **Help Center: How-To Guides**.
- Or tap **Help & Support** on the **Home** tab, or **Help and Support** on the **You** tab, then tap **Help Center: How-To Guides** at the top.

The guides open inside OnMyLead. Tap **Done** (iPhone and iPad) or the close button at the top (Android phones and tablets) to go back to the app. On onmylead.com, the link opens the Help Center in the same tab.
:::

In the Android app, those answers give the Android steps where they differ, such as allowing location **While Using the App**.

---

You can plan a ride on the big screen at onmylead.com. It's the same ride as one made in the app: the ride, its route and its stops show up in the OnMyLead app on your phone or tablet as soon as you save. Ride Mode and live tracking stay in the app.

![Drawing a route on onmylead.com](/help/img/web-route.webp)

:::release 2.0
Using OnMyLead on the website is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, the website still lets you join a ride, open your rides and follow the leader in Ride Mode.
:::

## Create a Ride on the Web

1. Go to onmylead.com and click **Create a Ride on the Web**.
2. Sign in with your OnMyLead account if you aren't already. You go straight to Create a Ride after signing in.
3. Pick **Public** or **Private** under **What Kind of Ride?**
4. Fill in the **Ride Name**, the day under **When**, and the **Meet At** time. Click **Calendar**, then type the date (such as 06/12/2027) in **Type a Date** or click it on the calendar. Click the month's name to jump to another year and month. Any day from today up to three years out works. For **Meet At**, click the time, then click **AM** or **PM**, the hour and the minute; no typing needed. You can also press Tab to move between them and Enter to pick.
5. Set the **Meeting Point**: type a park, trailhead, town or address in **Search a Place or Address** (just above the map) and pick it, or click the satellite map to drop the pin, then drag the pin to fine-tune it. You can also use your location or type coordinates, and the pin moves there.
:::release 2.1
   From 2.1 the meeting-point map is Mapbox's satellite map, the same one the app uses, and it opens near where you are if the browser shares your location. Clicking and dragging work the same.
:::
6. Under **The Route**, pick **Mapped** or **Freeride**.
7. Fill in anything else you want, then click **Create Public Ride** or **Create Private Ride**.

The rest of the form works the same as in the app. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride) for every option.

## Draw the Route on the Web

If you picked **Mapped**, the route builder opens after you create the ride. Click along the trail and the route follows it. Drawing a route is free. Importing a GPX file is a Pro feature. See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

To find a trailhead or park by name while you draw, click **Search** at the top of the map and pick a result. The map jumps there.

You can also add numbered planned stops for fuel, lunch or camp. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

:::release 1.0.1
The waypoints map has the same **Search**, so you can jump to a place before you click to drop a stop.
:::

:::release 2.1
## Change It Later

Open the ride on onmylead.com and click **Edit Ride Details** in the **You're Organizing** card to change the name, day, time, meeting point (click the map to move the pin) and the rest. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).
:::

## Share It

After saving, your ride page shows the invite code, a QR code and share buttons, the same as in the app. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders).

:::note
Free accounts create one ride each month, whether on the website or in the app. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

:::tip
When someone opens a ride link on a computer, the page shows the ride's QR code. They can scan it with their phone's camera to open the ride on their phone.
:::

:::note
Stuck while planning? Click **Help** at the top of onmylead.com to open these guides.
:::

articles.title: Create a Ride
articles.summary: Pick public or private, set the day, time and meeting point, choose a mapped route or freeride, and share your new ride.
articles.text:
---
title: Create a Ride
summary: Pick public or private, set the day, time and meeting point, choose a mapped route or freeride, and share your new ride.
category: rides
order: 10
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/components/meet-point-mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/meet-point-map.tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/new.tsx
  - app/src/components/events/event-or-ride.tsx
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx
  - app/src/components/invite-card.tsx
  - app/src/core/entitlements.ts
  - app/src/core/pro.ts
  - app/src/components/pro-gate.tsx
  - app/src/core/time.ts
  - app/src/core/calendar.ts
  - app/src/components/ride-date-picker.tsx
  - app/src/components/date-calendar.tsx
  - app/src/components/time-picker.tsx
  - app/src/lib/api.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261018000000_pro_entitlements.sql
related: [create-a-ride-on-the-website, invite-riders, route-builder, approvals-and-waitlist, edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride, free-vs-pro]
keywords: [new ride, plan a ride, start a ride, organize, host, meeting point, meet up, public ride, private ride, freeride, tablet]
screenshots:
  - file: create.webp
    shows: app/src/app/ride/new.tsx
---

You lead. Create a ride, tell everyone where and when to meet, and OnMyLead gives you a link, a code and a QR code to share. Public rides show up for riders nearby. Private rides are only for the people you invite.

![The Create a Ride screen](/help/img/create.webp)

## Create Your Ride

1. On the **Rides** tab, tap **Create a Ride**.
2. Under **What Kind of Ride?**, tap **Public** (open to anyone, found by riders near you or in your state) or **Private** (only friends you invite by link, text or email).
3. Type a **Ride Name**.
4. Under **When**, pick the day (see [Pick the Day](#pick-the-day) below).
5. Set the time in **Meet At** (see [Pick the Time](#pick-the-time) below).
6. Set the **Meeting Point**. You can search in **Search a Place or Address**, tap **Use My Current Location**, or paste **Coordinates** like "38.57, -109.55".
7. Add a **Place Name** if you like, such as "Gas station on Main St".
8. Under **The Route**, tap **Mapped** (you draw the route or import a GPX file next) or **Freeride** (no set route, everyone follows the leader).
9. Under **Who's Riding**, pick the **Vehicles Welcome**.
10. Tap **Create Public Ride** or **Create Private Ride**.

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 a satellite map sits under **Search a Place or Address**, on every device. It opens near where you are. Tap it to drop the meeting point there, then drag the pin to fine-tune the spot. Searching a place, **Use My Current Location** and typed **Coordinates** move the pin too. (The map needs a signal; without one, set the point by search, location or coordinates as before.)
:::

:::release 2.1
Found a park in [Scout](/help/scout)? Tap **Create a Ride Here** on its page: Create a Ride opens as a public ride with the meeting point and **Place Name** already set to the park. Move the pin if your group meets somewhere else, such as the park's gate or a gas station nearby.
:::

:::release 2.0
Planning a rally or a ride weekend with several rides? That's an event, not one ride. Tap **Event or Public Ride?** at the top of Create a Ride to see the difference, or see [Events](/help/events).
:::

If you picked **Mapped**, the route builder opens right away so you can draw the trail. See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder). Once the ride is saved you land on its page, ready to invite riders.

:::release 1.0.3
### Ride One of Your Trails

This is a Pro feature. Open a trail in [Navigate](/help/navigation-mode) and tap **Plan a Group Ride on This Trail**. The new ride starts with the trail's name, the trail as its route and its start as the meeting point, under a **Riding** banner. Pick the day, change anything you like and create it.

:::release 2.0
If the trail has a width limit, the **Riding** banner shows it (and whether your Garage machines fit), and the ride's **Instructions for Joined Riders** start with a line like "Trail width limit: 50". Wider machines won't fit." so everyone who joins sees it. Edit or delete that line like any other.
:::
:::

:::tip
Only riders who have joined see the exact meeting spot. Public pages show the general area, within about a mile.
:::

:::release 2.0
A **Mapped** ride, where you draw the route, is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, **Mapped** carries a **Pro** tag; pick **Freeride** to create the ride for free.
:::

## Pick the Day

:::until 1.0.1
Under **When**, tap **Today**, **Tomorrow** or any day in the next two weeks.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
Under **When**, tap **Today**, **Tomorrow**, **Sat** or **Sun** for the coming weekend. For any other day, tap **Calendar**.

:::until 1.0.2
Pick the day from the month calendar. Use the arrows to go to another month. You can schedule a ride for any day from today up to a year out.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
Then either type the date or pick it on the calendar:

- **Type a Date:** tap the box and type the month, day and year, such as 06/12/2027. The number pad is enough; the slashes go in for you. The calendar jumps to that day.
- **Tap a day:** use the arrows to go to another month, or tap the month's name (such as "November 2026") to choose a year and month, then tap the day.

You can schedule a ride for any day from today up to three years out, so rides next year and the year after are fine. Past days and days further out are greyed out.
:::

The day you picked shows under **When**, with how far away it is, such as "In 8 Weeks". Tap **Done** to fold the calendar away.

On a tablet, the calendar sits in the same form, with bigger day buttons.

## Pick the Time

:::until 1.0.3
Type the time in **Meet At**, for example "8:00 am" or "2:30 pm".
:::

:::release 1.0.3
No typing needed. **Meet At** starts at 8:00 AM. To change it, tap the time, then:

1. Tap **AM** or **PM**.
2. Tap the hour, **1** to **12**.
3. Tap the minute, from **:00** to **:55** in 5-minute steps.

The time shows in big letters as you tap. Tap **Done** to fold the picker away.

**Departure Time** and **Expected Finish** (under **Add Route, Difficulty and More**) work the same way. They start as **Not Set**: tap **Add** and the app suggests a time (30 minutes after you meet for departure, 8 hours after for the finish), then tap to adjust. Tap **Clear** to leave one empty.

On a tablet or a computer, all 12 hours and all 12 minutes fit in one row each.
:::
:::

## Public Ride Options

A public ride is listed in its state so riders can find it. The **State** fills in from the meeting point. If it's wrong (it can happen near a border), tap **Change State** and pick the right one.

Public rides also have a **Joining** choice:

- **Anyone Can Join**
- **I Approve Riders**

See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist) for how requests work. Private rides don't have this choice: anyone holding your invite link or code can join.

## Limit Who Can Come

Under **Who's Riding**, set **Max Vehicles**, **Max Riders** or both. Leave them empty for no limit. When the ride is full, new riders go on a waitlist. See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist).

:::release 1.0.3
**Pick your own invite code.** Under **Invite Code**, leave **Your Own Code (Optional)** empty and OnMyLead makes a code for you. Or type your own, like MOAB-2026: 6 to 20 letters and numbers, with dashes between words. A green **Available** means no other ride uses it. See [Choose Your Own Code](/help/custom-codes).
:::

## Invite a Riding Group

If you're in a riding group, an **Invite a Group** section shows up. Pick one or more groups under **Your Riding Groups**. Everyone in them gets a notification and sees the ride on their Rides tab, and they join with one tap. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups).

## Add More Details

Tap **Add Route, Difficulty and More** to fill in any of these:

- **Description**
- **Departure Time** and **Expected Finish** (used to check your ride against sunset, see [Ride Day and Weather](/help/ride-day-and-weather))
- **Destination**, which anyone who can see the ride sees, with directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
- **Route Length (Miles)**, used to warn riders whose fuel range is too short (see [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range))
- **Difficulty**: Easy, Moderate, Hard or Extreme
- **Experience**: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced or Expert
- **What to Bring**, **Required Equipment** and **Fuel**
- **Instructions for Joined Riders**, which only riders on the ride see
- **Ride Bubble**: Standard, Tight Trail, Desert or Highway (see [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble))

## After You Create It

Your ride page opens with a card that has the invite code, a QR code and buttons to share it. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders). You're also the ride's organizer and leader. See [Organizer Controls](/help/organizer-controls).

## How Many Rides You Can Create

Free accounts create one ride each month. Joining rides is always free and unlimited. On Free, the top of the Create a Ride screen shows **Rides Created This Month** so you know where you stand. When you've used this month's free ride, the app tells you the date your next one opens (the first of the month, UTC). Creating more rides than that is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

:::note
A ride counts toward the month you create it, even if you later cancel or delete it. Copying a ride or using **Ride Again** also creates a new ride.
:::

Pro bought on Android through Google Play lifts the monthly limit the same way, on every device you sign in to.

:::release 2.0
On Home, the **Create a Ride** card shows where you stand: **1 Left This Month** or **None Left This Month** on Free, and **Unlimited** on Pro or the trial. On Free, tap the label to see what Pro adds.
:::

:::release 2.0
## Create a Ride for an Event

On an event you host, **Group Rides > Add > Create a New Ride for This Event** opens Create a Ride with a **For Your Event** note at the top. Once you create the ride, it shows under the event's Group Rides. See [Events](/help/events).
:::

articles.title: Choose Your Own Code
articles.summary: Give your ride, riding group or friend link a code that's easy to say, like MOAB-2026, instead of the one OnMyLead made.
articles.text:
---
title: Choose Your Own Code
summary: Give your ride, riding group or friend link a code that's easy to say, like MOAB-2026, instead of the one OnMyLead made.
category: joining
order: 32
release: "1.0.3"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

related: [invite-riders, create-a-ride, riding-groups, friends, join-a-ride, qr-codes]
keywords: [custom code, own code, invite code, ride code, group code, friend code, vanity code, change code, pick code, link]
---

Every ride, riding group and friend link has a code: it's the end of the link (onmylead.com/r/MOAB-2026) and what riders type to open it. OnMyLead makes one for you, like 7F3A9C21. You can type your own instead, so it's easy to say out loud at the trailhead.

:::release 2.0
Choosing your own code is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, every ride, group and friend link still gets its own code that works, and the code box shows a **Pro** tag.
:::

## What a Code Can Be

- 6 to 20 letters and numbers
- Dashes between words, like SATURDAY-CREW (a space turns into a dash as you type)
- Capital or small letters both work: moab-2026 opens the same ride as MOAB-2026

Codes that pass for OnMyLead itself (like ONMYLEAD or SUPPORT) and rude words aren't allowed.

As you type, OnMyLead checks the code. A green **Available** means you can use it. **Another ride already uses this code** means someone got there first, so try another.

## A Ride's Code

- **When you create it:** under **Invite Code**, type it in **Your Own Code (Optional)**. Leave it empty to get one made for you. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).
- **Later:** on the ride's invite card, tap **Choose Your Own Code**, type the new code and tap **Save Code**. Only the ride's organizers see this, and only before the ride ends.

On a private ride, anyone with the code can join, so pick one that's hard to guess.

## A Riding Group's Code

- **When you create it:** type it in **Group Code (Optional)**.
- **Later:** open the group, scroll to **Invite by Link** and tap **Choose Your Own Code**. Only the rider who runs the group sees this.

## Your Friend Link

On the Friends screen, under **Your Friend Link**, tap **Choose Your Own Code**. See [Add Friends](/help/friends).

## What Happens to the Old Code

When you change a code, the old link, QR code and code stop working, the same as **Make a New Link**. Riders already on the ride or in the group stay in, and your friends stay friends. Send the new link to anyone who still needs it.

It works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones, Android tablets and onmylead.com.

articles.text:
---
title: Delete Your Account
summary: Permanently delete your OnMyLead account and its data from the You tab, and what to do about a Pro subscription first.
category: account
order: 80
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

  - app/src/lib/api.ts
  - supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts

related: [manage-subscription, sign-in, privacy, contact-support]
keywords: [delete account, remove account, close account, erase data, delete my data, cancel account]
---

You can delete your OnMyLead account yourself, right in the app. It happens straight away and can't be undone.

## Before You Delete

If you pay for OnMyLead Pro, cancel it with Apple too. Apple bills the subscription, so deleting your account doesn't stop it. See [Manage Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).

## Delete Your Account

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Scroll to the bottom and tap **Delete Account**.
3. Read the message, then tap **Delete Account** to confirm.

You're signed out and taken back to the start.

## What Gets Deleted

- Your account and profile.
- Rides you organize. They're removed for everyone on them.
- Your Garage, trips and riding groups.
- Your messages and location history.

This can't be undone. To ride with OnMyLead again later, you'd make a new account.

:::release 2.0
One thing is kept: the record that you agreed to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement, because it's a legal record. See [The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement](/help/rider-safety-agreement#what-gets-saved).
:::

## If You See Deletion Requested

Sometimes the app shows **Deletion Requested** instead of signing you out. That means your request was sent and your account and its data will be deleted within 7 days. If you pay for Pro, cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again.

## Need Help?

If the delete doesn't go through, [Contact Us](/help/contact-support) and pick **Account and Sign-In**.

articles.title: Get Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
articles.summary: Hand off to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions to the meeting point, along the route, to the destination, or to a rider.
articles.text:
---
title: Get Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
summary: Hand off to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions to the meeting point, along the route, to the destination, or to a rider.
category: routes-maps
order: 70
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/components/directions.tsx
  - app/src/core/directions.ts
  - app/src/lib/directions.ts
  - app/src/app/r/[code].tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/live.tsx
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx
  - app/src/components/rider-list.tsx
related: [ride-mode, ride-day-and-weather, waypoints-and-planned-stops, privacy]
keywords: [navigate, navigation, turn by turn, apple maps, google maps, meeting point, driving directions, how to get there, tablet]
---

OnMyLead hands you over to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions on the road. Off road, follow the leader and the route on the OnMyLead map.

On Android, directions open in Google Maps, since Android phones and tablets don't have Apple Maps.

Only the place you want to go is sent to the maps app, nothing about you.

:::release 2.0
Directions are a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, the **Directions** buttons carry a **Pro** tag. Directions to a rider who taps Need Help, EMERGENCY or Mechanical Issue, or who falls behind the group, always stay free.
:::

## Get Directions to the Meeting Point

1. Open the ride from the **Rides** tab.
2. On the **Details** section, find the **Directions** card.
3. Tap a row:
   - **Meeting Point:** the exact meeting spot.
   - **Along the Route:** follows the ride's route through stops on the way, ending at the end of the route.
   - **Destination:** the ride's destination, if the organizer added one.
4. Pick **Apple Maps** or **Google Maps**, unless you've already chosen one (below).

The **Directions** card shows while the ride is scheduled or live. **Meeting Point** and **Along the Route** only show for riders who have joined the ride, because the exact meeting spot and the route are private to them. See [Privacy](/help/privacy).

## Get Directions in Ride Mode

1. In Ride Mode, tap **Directions** just above the bottom panel, on the left.
2. Tap a row:
   - **Regroup Point:** where the leader asked everyone to meet up, when one is set.
   - **Meeting Point**
   - **Continue Along the Route:** picks up from where you are on the route.
   - **Destination**
3. Pick your maps app, if asked.

You can also get directions from other places in Ride Mode:

- Tap the **Regroup point set. Tap to navigate** banner.
- Tap **Navigate** on a rider's alert card.
- Open the **Riders** list and tap **Navigate**, or **Go to Last Seen** for a rider whose position is old.
- Tap a waypoint on the map. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

:::note
Directions along the route pass through up to 8 stops picked from the route, and the maps app keeps to roads it knows between them. Off-road parts of the route may differ, so follow the OnMyLead map there.
:::

## Choose Your Maps App

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **Settings**, tap **Directions**.
3. Pick **Ask Each Time**, **Apple Maps** or **Google Maps**.
4. Tap **Done**.

Every **Navigate** and **Directions** button in the app uses this choice. With **Ask Each Time**, the app asks which one to open every time.

:::tip
Google Maps opens in its app if you have it installed, and in your browser if you don't.
:::

---

Plans change. As the organizer (or a co-organizer) you can update the ride's details, change the route and stops, cancel the ride so everyone knows it's off, or delete it entirely.

:::until 2.1
## What You Can Change

On your ride page, you can change:

- **The route.** Open the **Map** section and tap **Edit Route** (or **Build the Route** if there isn't one yet, or **Map a Route Anyway** on a freeride). See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder).
- **Planned stops.** In the **Map** section, tap **Add a Planned Stop**. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).
- **Who leads and who rides at the rear.** See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

:::note
The ride's name, day, meeting time and meeting point can't be changed after the ride is created. To move a ride, tap **Copy This Ride** on its page to start a new one with the same details and route, pick the new day, then cancel the old one. The copy counts as a new ride toward your monthly allowance on Free.
:::
:::

:::release 2.1
## Edit Ride Details

1. Open the ride page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card on **Details**, tap **Edit Ride Details**.
3. Change what you need and tap **Save Changes**. **Cancel** leaves everything as it was.

You can change the name, the day and meeting time, the departure and expected finish times, the meeting point (search a place, use your location, type coordinates, or tap the map on onmylead.com), the place name, the state a public ride is listed in, the description, destination, route length, difficulty, experience, the vehicles welcome, whether you approve riders, the vehicle and rider limits, what to bring, required equipment, fuel notes and the instructions joined riders see (on a ride whose meeting point never saved, the instructions box appears once you pick the point, and stays while it holds text).

The box above **Save Changes** says what the save will do before you tap it, or **Not Ready to Save** with the reason while something stops it (a blank name, a time that doesn't read, a half-typed meeting point, instructions before a meeting point):

- **A new time or meeting point** sends everyone on the ride (including riders waiting for approval or on the waitlist) a notification, and the ride page shows **Updated** with what changed for a week, so nobody turns up at the old spot. Ride reminders move to the new time.
- **Other details** (the description, limits, what to bring and so on) just update on the ride page, marked Updated. No notification.

Lowering a vehicle or rider limit never removes anyone who already joined. A private ride stays open to anyone with its code.

Co-organizers can edit the ride too. Riders can't.

:::note
Once the ride is **live**, the day, times and meeting point are locked, because everyone is already out riding. The name and the other details can still change. A ride that has ended or been cancelled can't be edited: tap **Ride Again** or **Copy This Ride** to plan the next one.
:::

The same **Edit Ride Details** button is on the ride page at onmylead.com, so you can make changes on a big screen. On an iPad or Android tablet turned sideways, the day, times and meeting point sit on the left and the rest of the details on the right.

## The Route, Stops and Roles

- **The route.** Open the **Map** section and tap **Edit Route** (or **Build the Route** if there isn't one yet, or **Map a Route Anyway** on a freeride). See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder).
- **Planned stops.** In the **Map** section, tap **Add a Planned Stop**. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).
- **Who leads and who rides at the rear.** See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).
:::

## Cancel a Ride

Cancel when the ride is off but you want everyone to see that it was called off. The ride stays in their list as Cancelled.

1. Open the ride page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card on **Details**, tap **Cancel Ride**.
3. Read the message. It tells you how many riders will hear about it.
4. Tap **Cancel Ride** to confirm, or **Keep Ride** to go back.

Everyone who joined, asked to join or is on the waitlist gets a notification and an email saying the ride is cancelled. Cancelling can't be undone.

You can cancel a ride that hasn't started yet or one that's live. A ride that has already ended can't be cancelled.

## Delete a Ride

Delete removes the ride for everyone, along with its chat and route. Only the ride's organizer can delete it.

1. Open the ride page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card, tap **Delete Ride**.
3. Tap **Delete Ride** to confirm.

If the ride hadn't ended yet, everyone on it gets a notification and an email saying it's cancelled. Deleting can't be undone.

:::tip
You can also delete a ride from the **Rides** tab. Swipe left on the ride under **Your Rides** or **Past Rides** and tap **Delete**.

On onmylead.com there's nothing to swipe: each ride on the **Rides** page has its own button at the end of the row. Click the trash can (**Delete**) on a ride you organize, then confirm. On a ride someone else organizes the button is **Leave** (or **Decline** for an invite).
:::

## Cancel or Delete: Which One?

- **Cancel** keeps the ride in everyone's list, marked Cancelled.
- **Delete** removes it, its chat and its route for everyone.

Either way, riders on an upcoming ride are told it's off.

:::note
Cancelling or deleting doesn't give back a ride on a Free account. A ride counts toward the month you created it. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

articles.title: Emergencies and Staying Safe
articles.summary: What the EMERGENCY button does and doesn't do, how Need Help works, and how to ride safer with OnMyLead. OnMyLead is not an emergency service.
articles.text:
---
title: Emergencies and Staying Safe
summary: What the EMERGENCY button does and doesn't do, how Need Help works, and how to ride safer with OnMyLead. OnMyLead is not an emergency service.
category: safety-privacy
order: 50
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/live.tsx
  - app/src/components/hold-button.tsx
  - app/src/core/hold-to-send.ts
  - app/src/core/breakdown.ts
  - app/src/core/blocks.ts
  - app/src/lib/outbox.ts

  - app/src/app/support.tsx

  - app/src/app/terms.tsx

related: [emergency-siren, tilt-and-crash-alert, status-buttons, ride-mode, location-sharing, family-link, notification-settings, offline-maps]
keywords: [emergency, sos, 911, help, need help, accident, injury, hurt, crash, safety, rescue, tablet]
---

:::warning
OnMyLead is not an emergency service. It does not contact 911, search and rescue, or anyone outside your ride. If anyone is hurt, call 911 or your local emergency number first.
:::

OnMyLead helps your group keep track of each other. Phones lose signal, batteries die, and positions can be late or wrong, so use it alongside your own plan, not instead of one.

:::release 2.0
Every rider agrees to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement before using the app: you ride at your own risk, never use the phone while moving, and only ride where it's allowed. See [The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement](/help/rider-safety-agreement).
:::

Everything on this page is free on every plan. None of it needs Pro.

## What EMERGENCY Does

The **EMERGENCY** button in Ride Mode alerts everyone on your ride at once.

1. In Ride Mode, tap **EMERGENCY**. It stays on screen even when the bottom panel is folded.
2. Read the **Emergency** screen. If you're sharing your location, it shows your coordinates in large type, so you can read them out on a call.
:::until 1.0.3
3. Press and hold **Alert My Group** until it sends. A quick tap won't send it.
:::

:::release 1.0.3
3. Press and hold **Alert My Group** for 1.5 seconds. A bar fills across the button and it says **Keep Holding**. When the bar is full, your phone buzzes, the screen closes and the alert goes out. If you let go early, it says **Not sent** and nothing goes to the group. With VoiceOver or TalkBack, double tap and hold, or use the **Send** action.
:::
4. If anyone is hurt, tap **Call 911** to open your phone's dialer.

Tap **Cancel** to close the screen without sending anything.

:::release 1.0.3
In [Full Map](/help/ride-mode), **EMERGENCY** stays in the slim bar at the bottom of the screen, so it's still one tap away.
:::

When the alert goes out:

- Every rider on the ride gets a notification, "EMERGENCY: your name needs help now", with "Tap to see where they are."
- It shows in red on their Ride Mode screen. If you're sharing your location, they see you on the map and can tap **Navigate** to get directions to you.
- Help and EMERGENCY notifications are always on for every rider, even in quiet hours, and they come through even from a rider someone has blocked.

:::release 2.1
- Their phones sound a loud **Emergency Siren** until they silence it, unless they turned it off. See [Hear the Emergency Siren](/help/emergency-siren).
:::

You see a card showing whose phones have the alert. If you sent it by mistake, tap **Cancel** on the card and the group is told to ignore it. See [Send a Status or Quick Reply](/help/status-buttons).

:::release 2.0
**Crash Alert** can also send it for you: if your phone detects a hard hit or a rollover in Ride Mode and you don't tap **I'm OK** within 30 seconds, your group gets the EMERGENCY alert with your location. See [Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert](/help/tilt-and-crash-alert).
:::

## What EMERGENCY Doesn't Do

- It doesn't call or text 911, emergency services, or anyone else.
- It doesn't reach anyone who isn't on the ride.
:::until 2.1
- It can't send without a connection. With no service, the alert waits on your phone and sends by itself when you get signal. Riders also need service to receive it.
:::

:::release 2.1
- With no service, it reaches only riders on the ride within Bluetooth range (about 30 to 100 meters, passed along by up to six phones), and it waits on your phone and sends by itself when you get signal. If any nearby rider's phone gets signal first, it sends the alert for you. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
:::

## Need Help

**Need Help** is for when you need the group but it isn't an emergency. It sends with one tap, shows in red for the group, and notifies everyone on the ride the same way, including during quiet hours.

When things are sorted, tap **Resolved, I'm OK** so the group knows.

## Ride Safer

- **Call 911 first** in an emergency, then alert your group.
- **Share your location for the whole ride**, so Ride Bubble and the group can see you, and so riders can find you if you call for help. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
- **Send a family link** to someone at home, and tell them when you expect to be back. See [Share a Family Link](/help/family-link).
- **Download the ride's map** before you lose signal. The map keeps working offline, but positions only update with a connection. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).
- **Allow notifications** so you hear when someone needs help. See [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).
- **Allow location Always**, so your group can see you with your phone locked.

On Android, allow location **While Using the App**: the **Sharing Your Location** notification keeps your group seeing you with the phone locked. **Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** arrive in the **Rider Alerts** notification category, which Android shows at the highest priority.
- **Never type or read the screen while driving or riding.** Pull over first. Ride Mode is built for one-tap use when you're stopped.
- **Carry what you need to get yourself home**, and ride within your skill and your machine's limits.
