articles.title: Hear the Emergency Siren
articles.summary: When a rider in your group sends EMERGENCY or a Crash Alert goes out, your phone sounds a loud siren until you silence it. Here's how it works and how to turn it off.
articles.text:
---
title: Hear the Emergency Siren
summary: When a rider in your group sends EMERGENCY or a Crash Alert goes out, your phone sounds a loud siren until you silence it. Here's how it works and how to turn it off.
category: safety-privacy
order: 51
release: "2.1"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/core/siren.ts
  - app/src/lib/siren.ts
  - app/src/components/emergency-siren.tsx
  - app/src/app/notifications.tsx
  - app/src/lib/push.ts
  - supabase/functions/notify-ride-message/index.ts
  - supabase/functions/_shared/fcm.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261105070000_emergency_siren.sql
related: [emergency-and-safety, tilt-and-crash-alert, notification-settings, bluetooth-sharing, status-buttons]
keywords: [siren, alarm, emergency, sos, crash, accident, loud, sound, alert sound, silent mode, wake up]
---

:::warning
OnMyLead is not an emergency service. The siren only reaches riders on your ride. If anyone is hurt, call 911 or your local emergency number first.
:::

When another rider on your ride sends **EMERGENCY**, your phone sounds a loud siren so you notice it over wind, engines and helmets. It keeps going until you silence it. It's free on every plan and it starts on.

## What Sounds the Siren

- A rider presses and holds **Alert My Group** on the Emergency screen in Ride Mode, or sends EMERGENCY from CarPlay.
- A rider's **Crash Alert** countdown runs out, or they tap **Alert My Group Now** on it. See [Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert](/help/tilt-and-crash-alert).

**Need Help** and the other status buttons don't sound the siren; they come with the usual notification sound. Your own EMERGENCY never sounds the siren on your phone.

## With OnMyLead Open

The siren takes over the whole screen, on any screen in the app, and it says who needs help. Your phone buzzes with it, it plays even with the ring/silent switch on silent, and any music you're playing turns down under it.

On Android, with OnMyLead open, the siren plays at your phone's media volume, so keep media volume up on a ride.

- Tap **Show Me Where** to silence it and open Ride Mode with their location, so you can tap **Navigate** to them.
- Tap **Silence Siren** to silence it and stay where you are.

If you lock your phone or switch to another app before silencing it (say, to call 911), the siren stops and a quiet notification stays on your lock screen; tap it to see where they are.

If more than one rider needs help, the newest shows first, with how many more riders need help. **Silence Siren** silences all of them; **Show Me Where** silences only that rider's, and the next rider who needs help shows right after.

The siren stops by itself if the rider cancels their EMERGENCY or taps another status like **I'm OK** (with no service, a cancel doesn't travel over Bluetooth, so ask them to tap **I'm OK**). If they take back that I'm OK, the siren doesn't come back; a rider who still needs help taps **EMERGENCY** again. An EMERGENCY you've silenced never sounds again on that phone, and one older than 10 minutes doesn't sound when you open Ride Mode later; it still shows in red there. One that reaches you late while Ride Mode is open (say the rider had no service when they sent it) still sounds when it arrives.

## With OnMyLead Closed or in the Background

The EMERGENCY notification plays the siren as its sound, for about 27 seconds. Tap the notification to open Ride Mode at their location; the siren doesn't start again in the app.

- **iPhone and iPad:** the siren follows your ring/silent switch, like any notification. It's a Time Sensitive notification, so it comes through a Focus if you allow Time Sensitive notifications for OnMyLead in **Settings > Notifications > OnMyLead**.
- **Android phones and tablets:** the siren has its own notification channel, **Emergency Siren**, and plays as an alarm, so you hear it with the ringer on silent. Do Not Disturb can still hold it back; to let it through, open **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Notifications > Emergency Siren** and allow it to override Do Not Disturb. If you turn the **Emergency Siren** channel off there, EMERGENCY notifications come with the usual ride alert sound instead.

## With No Service

With [Bluetooth Sharing](/help/bluetooth-sharing) (on every plan for EMERGENCY), an EMERGENCY from a rider within Bluetooth range sounds the siren in Ride Mode too. If OnMyLead is in the background, you get a notification with the siren that says it was sent over Bluetooth.

## On the Website

Ride Mode on onmylead.com sounds the siren while the page is open. Your browser may only play it after you've tapped or clicked the page once. The website doesn't send notifications.

## Hear It or Turn It Off

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Settings**, tap **Notifications**.
3. Tap **Play Siren** to hear it for three seconds.
4. Switch **Emergency Siren** off if you'd rather not hear it. EMERGENCY notifications still come through, with the normal notification sound.

With [Sync Across Devices](/help/sync-across-devices) (Pro), your choice follows your account to your other devices.

articles.title: Events
articles.summary: Find rallies, poker runs and ride weekends, see the agenda and join the group rides. Pro riders post events with photos, co-hosts and Ride Managers.
articles.text:
---
title: Events
summary: Find rallies, poker runs and ride weekends, see the agenda and join the group rides. Pro riders post events with photos, co-hosts and Ride Managers.
category: joining
order: 60
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/components/meet-point-mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/meet-point-map.tsx
  - supabase/migrations/20261104130000_event_presenter.sql

  - supabase/migrations/20261102950000_events.sql
related: [home-screen, join-a-ride, create-a-ride, organizer-controls, free-vs-pro, report-and-block]
keywords: [presented by, sponsor, sponsored event, event or public ride, difference, event vs ride, event, events, rally, poker run, concert, raffle, show, meetup, ride weekend, agenda, schedule, co-host, ride manager, going, interested, rsvp, event link]
---

Events are the big days: a rally, a poker run, a club weekend or a meetup. An event has its dates, a place, photos, an **Agenda** of what's happening and when (group rides, poker runs, concerts, raffles, shows, food), and the **Group Rides** you can join. Anyone can see events. Pro riders create them.

## Event or Public Ride?

They're different things, and an event can hold public rides.

- A **Public Ride** is one ride on one day: a leader, a meeting point and a time. Anyone nearby finds it in **Find a Ride**, joins it, and you ride together in Ride Mode. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride) and [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).
- An **Event** is a bigger gathering, like a rally, poker run or ride weekend. It has dates, a place, photos, an agenda and **Going** or **Interested**, and it can hold several group rides that you join one by one.

Just riding? Create a Public Ride. Running a rally or a weekend? Create an Event and add its rides to it.

In the app, **Event or Public Ride?** on Events, Find a Ride, Create a Ride and Create an Event opens the same explanation. Tap **What's the Difference?** to open it and **Hide** to close it. It's the same on iPhone, iPad, Android and the website.

## Find an Event

1. On the **Rides** tab, tap the gold **Events** card (under Create a Ride, Find a Ride and Map Mode).
2. **Coming Up** lists public events, soonest first. With location allowed, it shows the ones within your distance (the same distance as Public Rides Near You); tap the distance chip to change it.
3. Tap an event to open it.

**Yours** lists the events you host, co-host, or said you're going or interested in, including ones from the last 30 days.

Event links look like **onmylead.com/e/** followed by a code. Anyone can open one, even without the app; on the website, names of riders only show once you sign in. On Android the link opens in the app. On iPhone and iPad it opens on onmylead.com for now.

## On an Event's Page

- **Going** and **Interested** tell the hosts you're coming (tap again to take it back). The count is public; the names of riders going show only to signed-in riders.
- **Share** sends the event's link.
- **Directions** opens the place in Apple Maps or Google Maps.
- **Agenda** shows each day in time order. Group rides and poker runs are marked red, raffles, contests and shows gold, everything else blue.
- **Group Rides** lists the event's rides, with their label (like **Day 1: Easy Group**), time, area, how many are going and the **Ride Manager**. Tap **See Ride and Join** to open the ride and join it as usual. A private ride shows **Invite Only: Ask a Host** unless you're already on it.

A ride that's part of an event shows **Part of** and the event's name at the top of its page.

:::release 2.1
## Presented By

Some events are presented (sponsored) by a company. Those show **Presented by** and the name in gold on their card in Events and near the top of their page. When RUS Offroad presents an event, the page also has **Shop RUS Offroad**, which opens the RUS Offroad store. Hosts can't add this themselves: the OnMyLead team sets it for a sponsor. Interested in presenting an event? Use Contact Us.
:::

## Create an Event (Pro)

1. Open **Events** and tap **Create an Event**. On Free, the button carries a small gold **Pro** tag and opens the Pro prompt.
2. Give it a name and details, and pick **Public** (shows in Events for everyone) or **Link Only** (only people with the link).
3. Under **When**, pick the first day and the start time. For more than one day, tap **Several Days** and pick the last day (up to 31 days).
4. Under **Where**, search a place or tap the map, and check the **Place Name**. Everyone who sees the event sees this place, so pick a public spot like a venue, park, campground or trailhead.
5. Add a website or ticket link if there is one, and tap **Create Event**.

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 the map under **Where** is on every device, not only the website, and opens near where you are: tap it to drop the place, and drag the pin to fine-tune it.
:::

The event opens, ready for the rest.

## Add Photos, the Agenda and Group Rides

Hosts see extra buttons on the event's page:

- **Add Photos** picks up to 12 photos (on iPhone, iPad and Android you can also **Take a Photo**). The app shrinks each one before it uploads. The first photo is the cover; tap a photo to **Make It the Cover** or **Remove Photo**.
- **Agenda > Add**: pick what it is (Group Ride, Poker Run, Concert, Raffle, Show, Contest, Food, Vendors, Meetup or Other), its name, the day, the start time and, if you like, an end time, where and details. Tap an item to change or remove it.
- **Group Rides > Add**: tap **Create a New Ride for This Event**, or add a ride you already organize (with an optional label). A ride can be in one event at a time. Removing a ride from the event doesn't cancel the ride.
- **Edit Details** changes the name, dates, place and the rest.

## Ride Managers

Each group ride can have a Ride Manager, someone who runs that ride for you. On the ride's card, tap the person button and pick a rider from your friends, the event's hosts and riders you've ridden with.

- The Ride Manager becomes a **Co-Organizer** of the ride: they can approve riders, set roles and run the ride like any co-organizer. See [Organizer Controls](/help/organizer-controls).
- If they aren't on the ride yet, they get a ride invite first, and become Co-Organizer when they join.
- Picking someone else, or **No Ride Manager**, puts the old manager back to Rider.
- Only a host who organizes (or co-organizes) the ride can pick its manager.

## Co-Hosts

The person who created the event can **Add Co-Host** (up to 10). Co-hosts edit the event, its photos and agenda, and add the rides they organize. They can't delete the event or add other co-hosts. A co-host can **Step Down** at any time. Co-hosting is free on every plan.

## Cancel or Delete

- **Cancel Event** keeps the event on its link marked **Cancelled**, and nobody can say they're going. Its group rides aren't cancelled; cancel them on their own pages if needed. **Bring the Event Back** undoes it.
- **Delete Event** (the creator only) deletes the event, its photos and agenda for good. Its group rides stay.

## Report an Event

Signed-in riders can tap **Report This Event** at the bottom of the page. See [Report and Block](/help/report-and-block). If the OnMyLead team hides an event, only its hosts can still see it, with the reason.

## On a Tablet

On iPad and Android tablets (and wide browser windows), Events shows two or three events per row, and an event's page puts the details on the left and the agenda, group rides and who's going on the right.

A family link is a web link you can text to someone at home. They open it in any web browser, with no app and no account, and see your last known location and when sharing ends. It's free on every plan.

## Send a Family Link

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **On the Trail**, tap **Share My Location**.
3. Turn on **Family Link**.
:::until 1.0.2
4. Under **For How Long**, pick how long to share. If you pick **Until I Turn It Off (Max 24 Hours)**, tap **Share** to confirm.
5. Your iPhone's share sheet opens with a message like "Follow my location until 5:30 PM" and the link. Pick Messages, or any app, and send it.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
4. Under **For How Long**, pick how long to share, or tap **Pick an End Date** to choose a day and time. If you pick **Until I Turn It Off**, tap **Share** to confirm.
5. Your phone's share sheet opens with a message like "Follow my location until 5:30 PM" (or just "Follow my location" when you picked **Until I Turn It Off**) and the link. Pick Messages, or any app, and send it.
:::

You can pick riders under **Who Can See You** at the same time, or send just the family link.

## What They See

The link opens a simple page with:

- Your ride name.
- **Last update:** when your phone last sent its location.
- **Sharing ends:** when the link stops working, with the date for a share that runs past today.

:::release 1.0.2
- For a share set to **Until I Turn It Off**, **Sharing ends** says **When they turn it off**.
:::
- **Open in Maps:** opens your last location in Google Maps.

The page checks for a new location every 30 seconds. If your phone hasn't sent a location yet, it says **No location received yet.**

:::warning
The page shows your last update, not a guaranteed live position. With no service on the trail, **Last update** stays at the last time your phone got through. Tell your family what time you expect to be back, and what to do if they don't hear from you.
:::

## Stop or Extend the Link

The family link lasts exactly as long as the share it belongs to.

1. Tap the **You** tab, then **Share My Location**.
2. Find the card that says **Includes a family link**.
:::until 1.0.2
3. Tap **Add 1 Hour** to keep it going, or **Stop** to end it now.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
3. Tap **Add 1 Hour** to keep it going, or **Stop Sharing** to end it now.
:::

Once the share ends, the link shows **No Longer Shared** and **This location link has ended.** Your location can't be seen from it again.

:::note
Anyone who has the link can see your location until the share ends, so only send it to people you trust.
:::

## Is OnMyLead Free?

Yes. Free accounts create one ride each calendar month and can join as many rides as they like, and the safety features are always free. [OnMyLead Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) adds unlimited rides and more.

:::release 2.0
From version 2.0, Free also includes 8 hours of Map Mode a month, and joining a ride and following the leader stay free and unlimited on every device. Using OnMyLead on an iPad, an Android tablet or the website, and extras like map layers, drawing routes, waypoints and directions, are part of Pro.
:::

## I Deleted the Ride I Made This Month. Can I Make Another on Free?

No. A ride counts when it's created, so cancelling or deleting it doesn't give it back, and copying a ride or using **Ride Again** counts as a new ride. Your next free ride opens on the 1st of next month (UTC).

## Will I Be Charged When My Pro Trial Ends?

No. The [Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial) needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription. Your account moves to Free, and your rides, routes, groups and maps stay.

## My Pro Trial Ended Mid-Month and I Can't Create a Ride. Why?

Rides you created during the trial count toward that month's one free ride.

## Can I Buy Pro or Use a Promo Code on the Website?

No. Subscribing, **Restore Purchases** and promo codes work only in the app on your phone or tablet. Pro bought in the app also works when you sign in on the website.

## Does Deleting My Account Cancel My Pro Subscription?

No. Apple bills Pro, so also cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again. See [Manage Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).

If you bought Pro on Android, Google Play bills it: cancel it in Google Play too.

## Can I Change My Ride's Time or Meeting Point?

:::until 2.1
Not after it's created. Tap **Copy This Ride** to make a new ride with the same details and route, pick the new day, then cancel the old ride. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).
:::
:::release 2.1
Yes, until the ride goes live. On the ride page, tap **Edit Ride Details** in the **You're Organizing** card, change the day, time or meeting point and save. Everyone on the ride gets a notification, and the ride page shows what changed. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).
:::

## My Ride Still Says Live. How Do I End It?

Rides don't end on their own. The organizer taps **End Ride for Everyone** on the ride page. Ending a ride stops everyone's location sharing for that ride.

## Why Can't I See the Exact Meeting Spot?

Only riders who have joined see it. Before you join, you see the general area, within about a mile. See [Privacy](/help/privacy).

## Why Isn't My Ride Showing on Find?

Find lists only public rides that are upcoming or live. Private rides never appear there, and rides drop off a few hours after their meeting time. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).

## Why Do Other Riders See Me as "Rider"?

You haven't picked a ride name yet. Tap **Pick Your Ride Name** on the Rides tab, or your name at the top of **You**. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

## Does "Until I Turn It Off" Sharing Ever End?

:::until 1.0.2
Yes. Personal shares stop by themselves after 24 hours. A ride share set to **Until I Leave the Ride** ends when the ride ends or you leave it. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
:::

:::release 1.0.2
Only when you stop it. Sharing with chosen riders or a family link set to **Until I Turn It Off** has no time limit: tap the **You** tab, then **Share My Location**, then **Stop Sharing**. A ride share set to **Until I Turn It Off** also ends when the ride ends or you leave it. If you'd rather it end on its own, tap **Pick an End Date** instead. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
:::

## Does Live Tracking Work With No Cell Service?

:::until 2.1
No. Positions only update when a phone has a connection. [Offline maps](/help/offline-maps) keep the map and route on your screen, and riders without service show where they were last seen.
:::

:::release 2.1
Yes, for riders close to you. With no service, OnMyLead phones on the same ride pass spots, status taps, EMERGENCY and Ride Mode messages to each other over Bluetooth, about 100 to 300 feet between phones in the open, and each phone passes them along the group, up to six phones down the line. Riders out of Bluetooth range show where they were last seen, and the first phone to get signal sends everything it heard to OnMyLead. Seeing riders, sharing your spot and messages over Bluetooth are part of OnMyLead Pro (every new account gets 30 days free); on every plan your phone passes things along and EMERGENCY goes out over Bluetooth. It's on by default. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing), and download the ride's [offline map](/help/offline-maps) before you go.
:::

:::release 2.0
## Why Does the App Ask Me to Agree to a Safety Agreement?

Riding is risky, and OnMyLead can't keep you safe on its own. Before you use the app, you agree that you ride at your own risk, won't use your phone while moving, and only ride where it's allowed. You're asked once, and again only if the agreement changes. See [The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement](/help/rider-safety-agreement).
:::

## Can I Use OnMyLead on an iPad or Android Phone?

Yes. OnMyLead is in the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and on Google Play for Android phones and tablets. On a tablet the map fills the screen, see [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet). You can also plan a ride on the website at onmylead.com, see [Create a Ride on the Website](/help/create-a-ride-on-the-website).

 iPhone and Android riders can join the same ride, see each other on the map and chat together.

:::release 2.1
## Does OnMyLead Work With CarPlay?

Yes, on iPhone. Open Ride Mode on your phone, connect to your car and tap **OnMyLead** on the car screen. See [Use OnMyLead on CarPlay](/help/carplay). OnMyLead doesn't support Android Auto.
:::

## How Do I See What Changed in an Update?

Every version's changes are listed in the [Release Notes](/help/release-notes), newest first, with when it reached the App Store and Google Play. To get the latest version, update OnMyLead from the App Store or Google Play.

:::release 1.0.3
## The App Says "Please Update OnMyLead". What Do I Do?

We show this when your version has a problem that's fixed in a newer one. Tap **Update Now** to open the App Store (iPhone and iPad) or Google Play (Android), then update OnMyLead. Your rides, groups and settings stay as they are.

On a ride with no signal? Tap **Not Now**. Ride Mode, Help and SOS and everything else keep working, and the app asks again the next time you open it.

You might also see:

- **Update Available** at the top of the home screen when a newer version is out. Tap **Update**, or close the card with the X.
- **About This Version**, an amber card at the top of the home screen, when we know about a problem in your version. It says what's wrong and what to do until the fix arrives.
:::

:::release 2.0
## How Do I Know When There's a New Version?

OnMyLead checks the App Store (iPhone and iPad) or Google Play (Android) for you. When a newer version is out, an **Update Available** card shows at the top of the home screen. Tap **Update** to go straight to OnMyLead in the store, or close the card with the X and it won't show again for that version. The check needs a signal and runs at most twice a day, so the card can take a few hours to appear after an update comes out.
:::

:::release 2.1
## Which Version of OnMyLead Do I Have?

Scroll to the very bottom of the home screen. It shows something like **Version 2.1 (10)**: the version, then the build number in brackets. It also shows at the bottom of the logo screen for a moment when you open the app. To get the newest version, update OnMyLead from the App Store or Google Play.
:::

## How Many Waypoints Can I Add?

Each rider can add up to 100 waypoints to a ride. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

Looking for people to ride with? The **Find** tab shows public rides near you or anywhere in a state. Private rides never show here. You need an invite link or code for those. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

![Find a Ride, near you or by state](/help/img/find.webp)

:::release 2.1
Looking for somewhere to ride instead of a group? Tap **Places to Ride** at the top of the **Find** tab to open Scout: off-road parks, OHV areas, trail systems and trailheads near you. See [Find Places to Ride With Scout](/help/scout).
:::

## Find Rides Near You

1. Tap the **Find** tab (or **Find a Ride** on the **Rides** tab).
2. Make sure **Near Me** is selected at the top.
3. Allow location if asked. If location is off, tap **Use My Location**, or pick your state instead.
4. Under **How Far Will You Go?**, pick **25 Miles**, **50 Miles**, **100 Miles** or **250 Miles**.

Rides show on the map and in a list under it, nearest first, with how far away each one is.

:::release 2.0
### Public Rides Near You on Home

Home also shows **Public Rides Near You** as cards you swipe sideways, nearest first. Tap the distance chip (**Within 500 mi** at first) to pick **50 mi**, **100 mi**, **250 mi**, **500 mi**, **1,000 mi** or **Anywhere**. Home never asks for your location: if you haven't allowed it, it shows every upcoming public ride. The **Find a Ride** card shows how many there are. See [Your Home Screen](/help/home-screen).
:::

## Find Rides Near a Place

Planning a trip somewhere else? Search a park, trailhead or town.

1. On the **Find** tab, tap **Search Near a Place**.
2. Type the place and pick it from the results.

The list shows **Rides Near** that place. Tap **Back to Near Me** to go back to rides around you.

## Find Rides in a State

1. On the **Find** tab, tap **By State**.
2. Pick a state.

Rides in that state show soonest first. To switch states, tap the state's name in the corner of the map.

## Use the Map

- Each dot is a ride. Blue dots are upcoming rides. Red, glowing dots are live now.
- Tap a dot to see the ride's name, time and distance, then tap **Open Ride**.
:::release 2.1
- Tap the map away from a dot to close the ride's card. The map is drawn by Mapbox, the same on the phone and the website.
:::
- Move or zoom the map, then tap **Search This Area** to see rides there. To return, tap the button under the map that starts with **Back to**, such as **Back to Rides Near Me**.
- Use the **+** and **-** buttons to zoom, and the location button to recenter the map.

:::release 2.0
- Tap the **Full Map** button above the zoom buttons to make the map fill the screen (on a tablet or a wide screen, the list tucks away). Tap it again (**Exit Full Map**) to bring the list back. See [Full Map](/help/full-map).
:::
- On a wide screen, such as the website on a computer, the search and the list of rides sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen.

:::note
Dots sit on the ride's general meeting area, within about a mile. The exact meeting spot is shown only to riders who join.
:::

## What You'll See

Find shows public rides that are coming up or live right now. Each ride in the list shows its date, time, general area, difficulty, distance and the vehicles welcome. Tap a ride to open its page and join. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

If there are no rides yet, tap **Create a Public Ride** to start one. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).

:::release 2.0
Looking for a rally or a ride weekend? Those are events. Tap **Event or Public Ride?** under the search to see the difference and **See Events** to browse them. See [Events](/help/events).
:::

:::tip
The **Rides** tab also lists a few upcoming **Public Rides**. Tap **Find Rides on the Map** (or **See All on the Map**, which shows how many there are) to see them all.
:::

Liked a ride? Follow the rider who organized or led it, and you'll hear when they post their next public ride. Following is free.

## Follow a Leader

1. Open the ride's page. If you've joined the ride, go to **Riders**.
2. Find the organizer or ride leader. Each one is labeled **Organizer** or **Ride Leader**.
3. Tap **Follow**. The button changes to **Following**.

To stop, tap **Following** on a ride page, or use **Unfollow** on the Groups tab (see below).

You can't follow yourself, so your own name doesn't get a Follow button.

## What You Get

- A notification when a leader you follow posts a new public ride. Private and unlisted rides are never announced to followers.
- On the **Groups** tab, under **Leaders You Follow**, a list of the leaders you follow, and under **Their Upcoming Rides**, their upcoming public rides.

To turn these notifications off, switch off **Leaders You Follow** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Unfollow a Leader

1. Tap the **Groups** tab.
2. Under **Leaders You Follow**, tap **Unfollow** next to the leader.

## Who Sees a Follow

Only you and the leader can see that you follow them. If riders follow you, the Groups tab shows how many.

keywords: [zoom in at intersections, intersection zoom, junction, auto zoom, zoom out, keep dot on screen, compass, follow me, follow, map follows me, keep me centered, auto center, recenter, map moves with me, tracking mode, my arrow, heading, direction arrow, which way am i going, my dot, blue dot]
---

With **Follow Me** on, the map in [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode) and [Navigate](/help/navigation-mode) moves with you as you ride, so your dot stays in view and you never have to drag the map to find yourself.

:::until 2.1
The map keeps your zoom and doesn't turn; it slides so you stay in the open part of the map, clear of the panels.

## Your Own Arrow

While you're moving faster than a walk (about 4 mph), a small white arrow on the edge of your own blue dot points the way you're heading, the same arrow every other rider's dot gets. It stays true when you turn the map. When you stop, the arrow goes away, because a phone can only tell direction while it moves.
:::

:::release 2.1
## How the Map Keeps Up With You

Your dot moves freely through the middle of the map. The first time it gets within about a tenth of the screen of an edge of the open part of the map (clear of the panels), the map zooms out one step. The next time your dot reaches an edge, the map centers on your dot and from then on moves with you, keeping your dot in the middle so it's always on screen. The map never turns.

Tapping **Center on Me**, or picking Follow Me back up after a pause, starts fresh: the map may zoom out one step again the next time you near an edge.

## Zoom In at Intersections

While the map is following you and you're moving, it zooms in as you come up on a junction of roads or trails, about 9 seconds before you reach it, so you can see the turn up close. Once you're through, it zooms back out to where it was. It works with any road, track or trail drawn on the map, including on a downloaded map with no signal.

**Zoom In at Intersections** is on until you turn it off, either in [Map Settings](/help/map-layers) under **Following** or in the **You** tab under **On the Trail**. Your choice follows your account to your other devices.

## Your Dot

Your own dot has an arrow built into it and a soft beam ahead of it (Red, White and Blue unless you pick another **Dot Style** in [Map Settings](/help/map-layers), a Pro feature). The arrow always shows which way you're facing: the direction you're riding while you move, and your phone's compass when you're stopped, so it turns as you turn. The beam is long while you ride and shorter when you stop. The dot takes its stopped look as soon as your phone reports you've stopped, or after a short while with no new location (about 8 seconds; in Ride Mode on Android phones and tablets using the basic map instead of Mapbox, about 25 seconds with Balanced and about 37 seconds with Max Battery Saver, which update less often). It stays true when you turn the map. On the Mapbox map in the iPhone, iPad and Android apps, if your device has no compass reading while you're stopped, the dot shows a round centre with no arrow instead of guessing a direction; the basic map and the website keep pointing the last way you were heading.
:::

## The Follow Me Button

**Follow Me** sits on the map just left of the round **Center on Me** button.

| What you see | What it means |
|---|---|
| Blue **Following** | The map is moving with you. Tap it to turn Follow Me off. |
| Blue outline, **Paused** | You dragged or pinched the map, so it stopped following to let you look around. Tap it, or **Center on Me**, to follow you again. |
| Plain **Follow Me** | Follow Me is off. The map stays where you put it. Tap it to turn Follow Me on. |

Follow Me is on until you turn it off. Your phone remembers the choice for Ride Mode and Navigate alike, and you can also switch it in the **You** tab under **On the Trail**: **Follow Me on Maps**.

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 these switches are also under **Following** in **Map Settings** (the round **Map Settings** button on Ride Mode's and Map Mode's map): **Follow Me**, **Zoom Out at the Edge** and **Zoom In at Intersections**. Turn **Zoom Out at the Edge** off and the map centers on your dot and moves with you the first time you near an edge, without zooming out first; it's also on the **You** tab under **On the Trail**. The zoom switches work while Follow Me is on.
:::

With Follow Me off, **Center on Me** still centers the map on you once, and Navigate doesn't move the map by itself, even while you record or follow a trail.

In Navigate the map holds still while the **Measure** tab is open, and when you jump to a place with search.

## In Full Map

In [Full Map](/help/full-map), **Follow Me** stays on the map as a round arrow button next to **Center on Me**, so the map stays as big as it can be.

## On Each Device

- **iPhone and Android phones:** **Follow Me** and **Center on Me** sit on the right, just above the bottom panel. If the panel fills the screen, fold it to see them.
- **iPad and Android tablets:** both sit at the bottom of the map, just left of the buttons panel in Ride Mode, and in the bottom corner in Navigate.
- **Website:** Navigate has **Follow Me** too, and shows your arrow when your browser reports your direction (most phones do while you move; computers usually don't). Ride Mode on the website shows the route instead of a live map, so it has no Follow Me button.

:::release 2.1
The website has no compass, so on onmylead.com your dot keeps pointing the last way you were heading when you stop.
:::

OnMyLead is free to download and use. Free accounts can join as many rides as they like, and every safety feature is free on every plan. OnMyLead Pro is for riders who lead a lot of rides and want extras like offline maps and GPX import.

Pro is $4.99 a month or $29.99 a year in the US. Other countries see the price in local currency. Every new account starts with a [free 30-day Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial).

## What's Included

This is the same comparison as the **Free and Pro** table on the Pro screen.

:::until 2.0

| Create Rides | 1 a Month | Unlimited |
| Join Rides | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Live Tracking, SOS and Ride Bubble | Yes | Yes |

| Navigate (Map Mode From 2.0): Offroad Map, Draw and Measure, Rate Trails | Yes | Yes |

| Group Rides on Your Trails | No | Yes |

| Create Ride Polls | No | Yes |
| Ride History | Last 5 | All |
| Advanced Trip Planning | No | Yes |
| Advanced Ride Statistics | No | Yes |
| Premium Ride Cards | No | Yes |
:::

:::until 2.1

## Always Free

:::until 2.0
Safety never depends on your plan. On every plan you get Ride Mode, live tracking, Need Help, EMERGENCY, Mechanical Issue alerts, Ride Bubble, location sharing, family links, ride chat and joining rides.
:::

:::release 2.0
Joining a ride and following the leader are free and unlimited, on every device. Safety never depends on your plan. On every plan you get Ride Mode, live tracking, Need Help, EMERGENCY, Mechanical Issue alerts, Crash Alert, Ride Bubble, location sharing, family links, ride chat, the status buttons and the leader's route and waypoints on the ride map. Directions to a rider who needs help are free too.
:::

## The Free Monthly Ride

Free accounts create one ride each calendar month.

- The month follows UTC time, so a new month can start a few hours earlier or later than midnight where you live.
- A ride counts when you create it. Deleting or cancelling it doesn't give the ride back.
- Using **Ride Again** to copy a ride counts as creating a ride.
- Rides you create on the website count too.
- Joining other riders' rides is always unlimited.

When you create a ride on a Free account, the Create a Ride screen shows how many you've created this month, like **Rides Created This Month: 0 of 1**. If you've used it, the app tells you the date your next free ride opens, and you can tap **See OnMyLead Pro** or **Not Now**.

:::release 2.0
## Free Map Mode Time

Free accounts get 8 hours of Map Mode every calendar month (UTC time). Pro has no limit.

- The clock only runs while Map Mode is open on your screen. It stops when you leave Map Mode or put the app in the background.
- It never runs while you're sharing your location on a group ride, so riding with a group and following the leader stay unlimited.
- Your time is counted on your OnMyLead account, so it's the same on every device and doesn't reset if you reinstall the app.
- Map Mode shows the time you have left, like **Free Map Mode: 5 h 20 m Left This Month**.
- When the time is used up, Map Mode tells you and offers **See OnMyLead Pro**. It opens again at the start of the next month.
:::

## What Each Pro Feature Does

:::until 2.0
- **Create More Rides:** Pro creates as many rides as you lead.
- **Import GPX Routes:** bring in a track from Gaia, onX or any GPX file. See [Import a GPX Route](/help/import-gpx). Drawing a route on the map stays free, and a route you already imported stays editable.
- **Offline Maps:** download satellite, topo and trail maps so the map keeps working with no signal. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps). Maps already on your phone keep working on Free.
- **Saved Riding Groups:** save your crew, add riders and invite everyone in one tap. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups). Joining a group, its chat and its ride invites stay free.
- **Record and Share Your Trails:** record a trail in Navigate, and share your trails on the public map. The offroad map, following a trail, measuring and rating other riders' trails stay free, and a trail you already shared stays editable. See [Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails](/help/navigation-mode).
- **Group Rides on Your Trails:** turn one of your trails into a group ride's route. Drawing a route on the map stays free.
- **Create Ride Polls:** ask the group a quick question in ride chat. Everyone can still vote on polls for free. See [Ride Polls](/help/ride-polls).
- **Full Ride History:** Free shows your last 5 past rides. Pro shows every ride you've been on. Nothing is ever deleted, so older rides come back if you upgrade.
- **Advanced Trip Planning:** plan several trips at once, start from packing lists, copy trips and link them to rides. One active trip and the fuel check stay free. See [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner).
- **Advanced Ride Statistics:** moving time, average and top speed, climbing and the group's totals after every ride. Distance and time out stay free.
- **Premium Ride Cards:** share your ride with the Full Stats and Big Number layouts. The standard card stays free.
:::

:::release 2.0
- **Create More Rides:** Pro creates as many rides as you lead.
- **Draw Ride Routes:** draw the route for your ride on the map, snapped to trails and roads. Freeride rides and following the leader's route stay free. See [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).
- **Waypoints and Planned Stops:** drop waypoints and plan stops with symbols for fuel, camp, hazards and more. Seeing the leader's waypoints on a ride stays free. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).
- **Directions:** hand any spot to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions. Directions to a rider who needs help stay free. See [Get Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps](/help/directions).
- **Map Layers:** switch between satellite, topo and the trails layer with trail names and closures. The standard map stays free. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).
- **Unlimited Map Mode:** Free includes 8 hours of Map Mode a month. Pro has no limit.
- **Map a Custom Trail:** draw a trail on the map and measure distances along it. Following trails stays free.
- **Record, Save, Rate and Share Trails:** record your line, keep your trails in My Trails, rate trails and share yours on the public map. Seeing and following other riders' trails stays free. See [Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails](/help/navigation-mode).
- **Track Line:** see where you've been on the map for the last 7 days. Your dot on the map stays free.
- **Named Spots:** mark obstacles, hazards, water crossings and viewpoints on your trails. Seeing spots on shared trails stays free.
- **Group Rides on Your Trails:** turn one of your trails into a group ride's route.
- **Import GPX Routes:** bring in a track from Gaia, onX or any GPX file. See [Import a GPX Route](/help/import-gpx).
- **Offline Maps:** download satellite, topo and trail maps so the map keeps working with no signal. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps). Maps already on your phone keep working on Free.
- **Post, Comment and Share:** post ride reports with a photo on your profile, comment on your friends' rides, badges, trails and posts, and share to Facebook, Instagram or X. Seeing Social, reading comments and liking (posts and comments) stay free; replying to a comment is commenting, so it's Pro. Pro riders show a gold **PRO** tag next to their name. See [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social).
- **Create Events:** post a rally, poker run or ride weekend with photos, an agenda and its group rides. Seeing events, saying you're going and being a co-host or Ride Manager stay free. See [Events](/help/events).
- **Saved Riding Groups:** save your crew, add riders and invite everyone in one tap. Joining a group, its chat and its ride invites stay free. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups).
- **Custom Share Codes:** pick your own easy code for a ride, group or friend link. Every ride and group still gets a free code that works. See [Choose Your Own Code](/help/custom-codes).
- **Ride Polls:** create polls and vote on them in ride chat. Reading a poll and its results stays free. See [Ride Polls](/help/ride-polls).
- **Your Own Messages:** type your own one-line message to the group in Ride Mode and save your quick replies. The status buttons, Need Help and EMERGENCY stay free. See [Send a Status or Quick Reply](/help/status-buttons).
- **Music Controls:** play, pause, skip and change the volume from Ride Mode and Map Mode. See [Control Your Music While You Ride](/help/music-controls).
- **Full Ride History:** Free shows your last 5 past rides. Pro shows every ride you've been on. Nothing is ever deleted, so older rides come back if you upgrade.
- **Advanced Ride Statistics:** moving time, average and top speed, climbing and the group's totals after every ride. Distance and time out stay free.
- **Premium Ride Cards:** share your ride with the Full Stats and Big Number layouts. The standard card stays free.
- **Advanced Trip Planning:** plan several trips at once, start from packing lists, copy trips and link them to rides. One active trip and the fuel check stay free. See [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner).
- **Garage Build Sheet:** track parts and extras with costs, build totals, the Build Sheet and CSV export. Your machines, specs and fuel range stay free. See [Your Garage](/help/garage).
- **Themes and Light Mode:** pick Light, Match Phone or one of the themes. Dark mode and Color Blind Mode stay free. See [Change the Look](/help/appearance).
- **Natural Voices:** pick a voice for spoken alerts. Alerts are still read out loud with the Automatic voice on Free. See [Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts](/help/voice).
- **Sync Across Devices:** your settings and Map Mode trails follow you to every device. Your account and rides are on every device for free. See [Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device](/help/sync-across-devices).
- **iPad, Android Tablets and the Website:** use OnMyLead on a big screen. On a Free account, a tablet or the website still lets you join a ride, open your rides, follow the leader in Ride Mode and manage your account. See [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet).

If you were already using a theme or a voice before 2.0, the app keeps it.
:::

:::release 2.1
New in Pro with 2.1:

- **Bluetooth Sharing With No Service:** with no cell service, see nearby riders on your map and pass your spot, status taps and messages to them over Bluetooth, and phones pass them along the group. On every plan, your phone passes everything along for the group, and status taps go out and come in over Bluetooth, so EMERGENCY, Need Help and Crash Alerts always get through, and so does the I'm OK that ends one. On Free, the switch shows the Pro tag. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
- **CarPlay:** see your group and send status taps from your car's screen. On Free, the car screen says **CarPlay Is Part of OnMyLead Pro**, and Ride Mode, status taps and EMERGENCY keep working on your phone. See [Use OnMyLead in CarPlay](/help/carplay).
- **Customize Your Dot:** pick your Dot Style and Dot Size. On Free your dot is the Red, White and Blue dot at Medium. If you picked another one during a trial, it comes back when you have Pro again.
- **Group Photos:** give a riding group you made a photo. Everyone can still see group photos for free. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups).

When 2.1 arrives, every rider without Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial first, so nothing changes for you right away. Home shows the date your trial ends. See [Your Free 30-Day Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial).
:::

When you tap something that needs Pro, a short prompt explains it. Tap **See OnMyLead Pro** to see the plans, or **Not Now** to close it.

:::release 2.0
On a Free account, a small gold **Pro** tag sits beside each button that needs Pro, so you know before you tap. You'll see it on buttons like **Import GPX**, **Record a Trail**, **Download** for offline maps, **New Group**, **Create an Event**, **Directions**, **Add Waypoint**, **Message** in Ride Mode, the music button, **Map Style**, **Track Line**, **Mark a Spot**, poll voting, the theme and voice choices, and **Sync**. Tapping one opens the same prompt. During your Pro Trial and on Pro the tags are gone. Create a Ride doesn't carry a tag, because Free includes a ride a month; it shows how many you have left instead.
:::

## See Your Plan

:::release 2.0
Pro Annual is half price for the first year when you invite a new rider who finishes their first ride, or when a friend invites you. See [Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro](/help/refer-a-friend).
:::


On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**. **Your Plan** shows Free, Pro Trial or Pro. On Free it also shows how many rides you've created this month.

Your plan is saved on your phone, so the app knows it even with no signal.

:::note
Pro is bought in the app on iPhone or iPad through the App Store. Pro you buy there also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.
:::

On Android, Pro is bought through Google Play. Pro belongs to your OnMyLead account, so it works on iPhone, iPad, Android and the website, whichever store you bought it from.

articles.summary: Add riders as friends so you see each other when you're out riding nearby and can message any time.
articles.text:
---
title: Add Friends
summary: Add riders as friends so you see each other when you're out riding nearby and can message any time.

---

Add the riders you ride with as **friends**. Friends see each other in [Out Riding](/help/out-riding) when they're out near each other, and can message each other any time.

Being friends never shares where you are. In Out Riding, friends see your ride name and roughly how far away you are, in whole miles, the same as any rider you know.

## Open Friends

Go to the **Groups** tab and tap **Friends** near the top. The row shows how many friends you have, how many are out riding, and any friend requests waiting for you.

:::release 2.0
Tap a friend's picture to see it full size, or their name in **Social** to see their profile, rides, badges and posts. See [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social).
:::

## Add a Friend

There's no search by name, so nobody can look you up. You can add a rider in any of these ways:

- **Riders you know**: on the Friends screen, **Riders You Know** lists riders you've been on a ride with or share a riding group with. Tap **Add**.
- **On a ride**: on the ride's page, tap a rider in the **Going** list, then **Add Friend**. You can also tap **Message** there.
- **In Out Riding**: tap **•••** next to a rider, then **Add Friend**.
- **In a conversation**: tap **•••** at the top, then **Add Friend**.
- **With your friend link**: anyone else, like a buddy you met at the trailhead, can add you with your friend link (below).

They get a notification and see your request at the top of their Friends screen. You're friends once they tap **Accept**. If they had already asked you, adding them makes you friends straight away.

## Share Your Friend Link

1. On the Friends screen, find **Your Friend Link**. It shows your friend code. Want one that's easy to say, like MOAB-RIDER? Tap **Choose Your Own Code**. See [Choose Your Own Code](/help/custom-codes).
2. Tap **Share Friend Link**, or **Text**, **Email** or **Copy**.
3. When your buddy opens the link (or types your code under **Got a Friend Code?** and taps **Look Up**), they see your name and tap **Add Friend**. They need to be signed in to OnMyLead.
4. Accept their request on your Friends screen.

To stop an old link working, tap **Make a New Link**. Your friends stay friends.

:::release 2.0
If your buddy is new to OnMyLead and creates their account with your link, it also counts as an invite: when they finish their first ride, you both get 50% off Pro Annual. See [Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro](/help/refer-a-friend).
:::

## Answer a Friend Request

Requests waiting for you are at the top of the Friends screen under **Friend Requests**. Tap **Accept** or **Decline**. Declining just removes the request; the other rider isn't told.

## See Friends Out Riding

On the Friends screen, friends who are out near you are listed first, in green, with roughly how far away they are, like **Out Riding, About 3 Miles**. You only see this while you're Out Riding yourself, and only for friends within 50 miles. Tap a friend, or the blue message button, to message them.

In Out Riding, friends show up when you've both switched it on with **Riders I Know** (or **Everyone Nearby**). They're listed first and marked **Friend**.

## Message a Friend

Tap the blue message button next to a friend. You can message a friend any time, Out Riding or not. See [See Who's Out Riding Nearby](/help/out-riding) for muting, reporting and deleting conversations.

## Cancel a Request or Remove a Friend

- Under **Requests You Sent**, tap **Cancel**.
- Next to a friend, tap **✕**, then **Remove**. They aren't told.

## Limits

To keep requests friendly, you can send up to 30 friend requests a day, and ask the same rider at most twice a week.

## Blocking

If you block a rider, you stop being friends and any request between you is removed. Neither of you can send a new one. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## Notifications

Friend requests, and requests someone accepted, come as notifications. Tapping one opens **Friends**. Turn them off under **Friend Requests** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## On a Tablet

On a tablet in landscape, or a wide window, your friend link and **Got a Friend Code?** are on the left, and your requests, friends and riders you know are on the right.

Trail miles burn more fuel than you think. OnMyLead compares a ride's miles with your machine's range from your garage and tells you, in plain words, whether you have enough.

![Fuel range on a machine page](/help/img/vehicle.webp)

## How Range Is Worked Out

Your range is your fuel (tank plus any extra fuel you carry) times your miles per gallon. The check uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back and a third in reserve.

- **Enough Range**: the ride is within two thirds of your full range, so you keep a reserve.
- **Range Is Tight**: the ride eats into your reserve. Bring extra fuel or plan a fill-up.
- **Not Enough Range**: the ride is longer than your full range. The check says about how many miles short you are.

When you have enough, it also says roughly how much fuel you'll have left at the end.

## Set Up Your Machine

The check needs your machine's tank size and mileage.

1. Open your machine in the Garage and edit it.
2. Under **Fuel and Mileage**, enter **Tank (gal)**.
3. If you carry spare fuel, enter **Extra Fuel (gal)**.
4. Enter **Miles per Gallon**. Use your real-world trail mpg, not the sticker number.
5. Save.

Your machine's page then shows its **Full Range**, **Safe Turnaround** and **Safe Trip** miles. See [Your Garage](/help/garage).

## Where the Ride's Miles Come From

- If the ride has a mapped route, its miles come from the route. See [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).
- If not, the organizer can enter **Route Length (Miles)** when creating the ride, under **Add Route, Difficulty and More**.

A ride with neither has no miles to check against.

## Check Before the Ride

1. Join the ride, open it and tap the **Details** tab.
2. Find the fuel card. Until there's a result, it's called **Your Machine**.
3. Under **Bringing**, pick the machine you're taking, or **None / Riding Along**.
4. Read the result: **Enough Range**, **Range Is Tight** or **Not Enough Range**, with one line of advice.

If you have only one machine with a tank size and mpg, it's checked until you pick one.

You can change your machine while the ride is scheduled or live.

If the card says to add tank size and mpg, tap **Edit Machine**. If your garage is empty, tap **Add Your Machine to the Garage**.

## In Ride Mode

When the ride has a mapped route, Ride Mode shows your range check with the route progress, colored green, yellow or red. It uses the route's length and the machine you picked for the ride. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

:::tip
Running low on the trail? Use the **Need Fuel** status button to let the group know. See [Status Buttons](/help/status-buttons).
:::

## Good to Know

- The check is worked out for you from your own garage.
- It's a planning guide, not a gauge. Hills, sand, mud, load and speed all change real fuel use.
- The Trip Planner has a fuel check too. See [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner).

articles.summary: Hide the bars and panels on any map so the map fills your screen, and bring them back with one tap.
articles.text:
---
title: Full Map
summary: Hide the bars and panels on any map so the map fills your screen, and bring them back with one tap.
category: routes-maps
order: 12
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:

related: [follow-me, ride-mode, navigation-mode, route-builder, waypoints-and-planned-stops, find-a-ride, map-layers]
keywords: [full map, full screen, bigger map, more map, hide buttons, hide controls, show controls, map only]
---

:::until 2.1
Every map in OnMyLead can fill your whole screen. **Full Map** tucks the top bar, the layers button and the panel away, and leaves one slim bar at the bottom so you can bring everything back with one tap.
:::

:::release 2.1
Every map in OnMyLead can fill your whole screen. **Full Map** tucks the top bar and the panel away, and leaves one slim bar at the bottom so you can bring everything back with one tap. The round **Map Settings** button stays in the top-left corner and the compass in the top-right, so you can change the map without leaving Full Map.
:::

## Turn On Full Map

Tap **Full Map** at the right end of the panel's grab bar, at the top of the panel over the map. It's in the same place in:

- [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode)
- [Navigate](/help/navigation-mode)
- [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder)
- [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops)

:::release 2.1
Or swipe the panel down: a long swipe (or a quick flick) goes straight to Full Map. A short swipe folds the panel down to its grab bar as before, and swiping down again on the folded panel goes to Full Map. On a tablet, where the panel hangs from the top beside the map, swipe it up instead.
:::

In [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride), tap the **Full Map** button at the top of the buttons on the map's right edge.

:::release 2.1
[Scout](/help/scout) (**Places to Ride** on the Find tab) has the same **Full Map** button.
:::

## Bring the Buttons Back

Tap **Controls** in the bar at the bottom, or swipe the bar up.

:::release 2.1
The bar has a small grab handle on top as a reminder that it swipes up.
:::
 Everything comes back the way you left it. In Find a Ride, tap the same corner button again (**Exit Full Map**).

Your phone remembers Full Map for each map, so it opens the same way next time. Find a Ride always opens with its list.

## What Stays on Screen

The bar keeps only what you shouldn't have to dig for:

| Map | In the bar or on the map |
| --- | --- |
| Ride Mode | The rider line with every rider (on a Freeride, the group behind the leader), **EMERGENCY**, calls for help from other riders, **Center on Me**, **Follow Me**, and **Music** if you use [Music Controls](/help/music-controls) |
| Navigate | Your speed, the miles left on a trail you're following, or the length you're measuring, a red **Rec** while recording, **Undo** while measuring, **Center on Me** and **Follow Me** (not while measuring) |
| Draw a Route | The route's miles and **Undo**. Tapping the map still adds points |
| Waypoints | Just the map and its pins. Press and hold the map to drop a waypoint |

On every map, the **No Signal** tag stays when you have no service, and tapping a trail line still shows its card.

## Phones, Tablets and the Website

Full Map works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. On a tablet the bar sits in the bottom-left corner. On onmylead.com, press **F** to turn on Full Map and **Esc** to bring the controls back (not while you're typing in a box).

articles.title: Your Garage
articles.summary: Add your rig or side-by-side with a photo, fill details from the VIN, track every part of the build and see your fuel range.
articles.text:
---
title: Your Garage
summary: Add your rig or side-by-side with a photo, fill details from the VIN, track every part of the build and see your fuel range.
category: account
order: 40
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/app/garage/**
  - app/src/components/vehicle-form.tsx
  - app/src/core/garage.ts

  - app/src/lib/export.ts
  - app/src/lib/export.web.ts
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx
  - app/app.json
related: [fuel-range, trip-planner, starlink, rus-gear]
keywords: [garage, width, trail width, vehicle, machine, rig, truck, jeep, sxs, utv, side by side, vin, build sheet, mods, parts, csv, fuel range, mpg, tablet]
screenshots:
  - file: vehicle.webp
    shows: app/src/app/garage/[id]/index.tsx
---

The Garage keeps your machines in one place: a photo, the details, every part you've added and how far a tank will take you.

![A machine in the Garage with its fuel range and build](/help/img/vehicle.webp)

## Open Your Garage

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Your Gear**, tap **Garage**.

You need to be signed in.

## Add a Machine

1. Tap **Add a Machine**.
2. Under **What Are You Adding?**, pick **Vehicle** or **SXS/UTV**.
3. Tap **Choose Photo** to add a photo from your library (optional).

On Android, the system photo picker opens, and OnMyLead only gets the photo you pick.
4. Fill in a **Nickname**, or the **Year**, **Make** and **Model**. You need a nickname or a make and model. **Trim** is optional.
5. Add the rest if you like: **VIN**, **Purchase Price ($)**, **Engine Hours** and **Odometer (Miles)**.
6. Under **Fuel and Mileage**, enter **Tank (gal)**, any **Extra Fuel (gal)** you carry and **Miles per Gallon**. Use your real-world trail mileage, not the sticker.

:::release 2.0
Under **Trail Fit**, enter the machine's **Width (Inches)** at its widest point, tire to tire. Trails with a width limit then tell you whether it fits, on the trail card, a trail's page and when you plan a ride on a trail. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).
:::
7. Tap **Add to Garage**.

## Fill In Details From the VIN

1. Type the 17-character **VIN**.
2. Tap **Fill Year, Make and Model From VIN**.
3. Check the year, make, model and trim it fills in.

If there's no match, enter the details by hand. A VIN is 17 letters and numbers and never uses I, O or Q.

## See Your Fuel Range

Once a machine has a tank size and mpg, its page shows a **Fuel Range** card:

- **Full Range**: how far you can go on your tank plus extra fuel.
- **Safe Turnaround**: a third of your full range. Turn around by this many miles out.
- **Safe Trip**: two thirds of your full range, the longest round trip that still keeps a third in reserve.

It uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back, a third in reserve. If a machine has no range yet, tap **Add Fuel Range**.

Your Garage also powers the fuel check on a ride. See [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range).

## Track Your Build

:::release 2.0
Tracking parts, the Build Sheet and the CSV export are Pro features. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Your machines, their specs and the fuel range stay free.
:::

1. Open a machine.
2. Tap **Add a Part or Extra**.
3. Pick the **Area**, like **Wheels & Tires**, **Suspension**, **Lighting** or **Recovery**.
4. Enter the **Item**, and if you like the **Brand**, **Cost ($)**, **Installed** date (like 2026-05-01) and **Notes**.
5. Tap **Add**.

Parts are grouped by area with a subtotal for each. At the bottom you'll see the **Build Total**, and if you entered a purchase price, the **Purchase Price** and **All In** total.

To change or remove a part, tap it, then tap **Save** or **Remove Item**.

## Export Your Build

Under **Export** on a machine's page:

- **Build Sheet** shares your machine and its parts as text, to send in a message or paste anywhere.
- **CSV** saves the build list as a spreadsheet file you can send to Files, email or a spreadsheet app.

## Edit or Delete a Machine

1. Open the machine.
2. Tap **Edit Machine** to change its details or photo, then tap **Save Changes**.
3. Or tap **Delete**, then confirm. The machine and all its build items are removed.

articles.title: Get Started With OnMyLead
articles.summary: What OnMyLead is, how to get the app on iPhone, iPad or Android, make your account, and find your way around the Rides, Find, Groups and You tabs.
articles.text:
---
title: Get Started With OnMyLead
summary: What OnMyLead is, how to get the app on iPhone, iPad or Android, make your account, and find your way around the Rides, Find, Groups and You tabs.
category: getting-started
order: 10
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:

keywords: [install, download, new, start, tabs, home, first time, setup, permissions, website, iphone, ipad]
---

OnMyLead is a group ride app for off-road riders. The leader creates a ride, the crew joins with a code, link or QR code, and on the trail everyone shares one live map, a group chat and quick taps like **Need Fuel** and **Flat Tire** that tell the whole group at once.

## Get the App

OnMyLead runs on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. Download **OnMyLead** free from the App Store on an iPhone or iPad, or from Google Play on an Android phone or tablet, then open it. It's the same account, rides and Pro plan on every device, and iPhone and Android riders ride together on the same map.

:::release 2.0
## Agree Before You Ride

The first time you open the app, the **Before You Ride** screen shows the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. Read it, tick the box and tap **I Agree**. On onmylead.com it shows after you sign in. See [The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement](/help/rider-safety-agreement).
:::

## Make Your Account

You can look around without an account, but you need one to create rides, save your Garage and keep riding groups.

1. On the **Rides** tab, tap **Sign In or Create a Free Account**.
2. Tap **Create Account** at the top.
3. Use one of the **Continue with** buttons, or enter **Your Name**, **Email** and a **Password** of at least 8 characters, then tap **Create Account**.
4. If we email you a link, tap it on the same iPhone to confirm your email and finish signing in.

See [Sign In and Create an Account](/help/sign-in) for every way to sign in.

Next, pick your ride name. It's what other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat. Until you pick one, Home shows **Pick Your Ride Name** and other riders see you as Rider. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

New accounts start with a free Pro Trial. See [The Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial).

## Find Your Way Around

:::until 2.0
Four tabs run along the bottom of the screen.

On a tablet they run down the left edge instead. See [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet).
:::

:::release 2.0
Four tabs run along the bottom of the screen: **Rides**, **Find**, **Groups** and **You**. In the middle, the blue **Map Mode** button opens your offroad map from any tab. See [Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails](/help/navigation-mode).

On a tablet they run down the left edge instead, with **Map Mode** under **Find**. See [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet).
:::

### Rides

Your home screen.

:::until 2.0
- **Create a Ride**: start a ride that you lead. Free accounts create one ride a month. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
- **Join a Ride**: type an invite code and tap **Open**. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).
- **Find a Ride**: opens the Find tab.
- When one of your rides is live, a card at the top says **Your ride is live. Tap to open Ride Mode**.
- **Ride Invites**, **Your Rides** and **Past Rides** list the rides you're on. Swipe a ride left to delete it (if you organize it) or leave it. On onmylead.com, click **Delete** or **Leave** at the end of the row instead. The app always asks first.
- **Public Rides** shows a few upcoming public rides near the bottom.
:::release 2.0
- **The bell** at the top right: your notifications from the last 30 days, with a red number for new ones. See [See and Clear Your Notifications](/help/notifications-inbox).
:::
:::release 1.0.3
- **Navigate**: your offroad map when you're not on a group ride. Record, share and rate trails, and measure distances. See [Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails](/help/navigation-mode).
:::
:::

:::release 2.0
- **Join a Ride** is the big red card at the top: type the invite code and tap **Join**. Joining is always free and unlimited.
- **Create a Ride** shows how many rides you have left this month on Free, or **Unlimited** on Pro. **Find a Ride** shows how many public rides are near you.
- **Map Mode**: **Open Map Mode**, **Map a Custom Trail** and the **Track Line** switch.
- **Your Next Ride**, **Ride Invites** and **Past Rides**; **Your Group**; **Public Rides Near You**; your **Feed**; **Your Badges**; **Your Toolkit**; and **Help & Support**.
- **The bell** and your picture at the top right open your notifications and the **You** tab.

:::release 2.1
- **Events**, the gold card right under **Create a Ride** and **Find a Ride**, with **Map Mode** under it. Join, Create, Find, Events and Map Mode all fit on the first screen.
:::

See [Your Home Screen](/help/home-screen) for each part.
:::

### Find

Public rides on a map. Choose **Near Me** or **By State**, or use **Search Near a Place** to look around a trailhead, park or town. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).

### Groups

Your riding groups, the groups you're in, and **Leaders You Follow**. Tap **New Group** to save your crew. You need an account for this tab; if you're signed out, it takes you to sign in. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups).

:::release 1.0.3
At the top: **Out Riding**, to see which riders are out near you and message them, and your **Messages**. See [See Who's Out Riding Nearby](/help/out-riding).
:::

### You

Everything that isn't a ride:

- Your ride name and plan at the top.
- **Your Gear**: [Garage](/help/garage), [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner) and [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).
- **On the Trail**: **Share My Location** and [Starlink](/help/starlink).
:::release 1.0.3
- **On the Trail** also has **Navigate** and **Rider Trails on Maps**, which shows or hides trails other riders shared.

:::release 2.0
- **Follow Me on Maps**, also under **On the Trail**, turns off (or back on) the map moving with you in Ride Mode and Navigate. See [Follow Me on the Map](/help/follow-me).
- **Music Controls**, also under **On the Trail**, shows or hides the Music button in Ride Mode and Navigate. See [Control Your Music While You Ride](/help/music-controls).
:::
:::
- **Settings**: [Notifications](/help/notification-settings), **Directions** (which maps app **Navigate** opens), **Subscription** and **Blocked Riders**.
- **Account**: the email you sign in with.
:::until 2.0
- **Help**: **Contact Us** and **Help and Support**.
:::
:::release 2.0
- **Help**: **Help Center: How-To Guides** (these step-by-step guides), **Report a Bug**, **Contact Us** and **Help and Support**. When you're signed in, **Report a Rider** is there too.
:::
- **Sign Out** and **Delete Account** at the bottom.

:::release 1.0.3
Any sheet that slides up from the bottom of the screen, such as a new waypoint, a report or the Pro prompt, closes when you swipe it down. That works on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and tablets. On onmylead.com you can drag it down with the mouse, or click **Cancel** or **Close**.
:::

## Permissions the App Asks For

### Notifications

After you sign in, your iPhone asks if OnMyLead can send notifications. Say yes so you hear when someone in your group taps **Need Help** or **EMERGENCY**, even with the phone in your pocket. Tapping a notification opens the ride it is about. You choose everything else in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

### Location

OnMyLead asks for your location when you first use it, for example to find rides near you or when you start sharing on a ride. Your location is shared only with riders you choose, only while you're sharing.

When you share on a ride, your iPhone may also ask to allow location **Always**. Allow it so your group keeps seeing you while your phone is locked on the mount. Sharing with a ride always stops when your timer ends or the ride ends. See [Location Sharing](/help/location-sharing).

On Android, allow location **While Using the App**. OnMyLead never asks for **Allow All the Time**: while you share, Android shows a **Sharing Your Location** notification, and that keeps your group updated with the phone locked. On Android 13 and later, allow notifications too, so you can see that notification and hear **Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** alerts.

### Photos

If you add a photo of your machine to your Garage, the app asks to use your photos. Only the photo you pick is uploaded.

## Using the Website

Some things also work at onmylead.com in a web browser:

- Sign in with the same account.
- Create a ride from your computer and draw its route on a big map. See [Create a Ride on the Website](/help/create-a-ride-on-the-website).
- Open a ride with its invite code.
- Send us a message with **Contact Us**.
- On a computer, once you're signed in, **Rides**, **Find**, **Groups** and **You** run down the left side of the page.
:::release 2.0
- **Map Mode** sits in the same menu, under **Find**.
:::
- Read these guides: click **Help** at the top of the home page, on a computer or a phone.

Ride Mode and live tracking stay in the app on your phone or tablet.

## Notices From the Team

Sometimes a card at the top of Home shows a message from the OnMyLead team, like **Planned Maintenance** or an announcement. You can close an announcement with its X. A maintenance notice stays until the work is done.

If a screen says something like **Trip Planner Is Off for Now**, that feature is switched off for a while. Everything you saved is kept, and your rides work as usual.

---

Every riding group has its own chat: a group text for everyone in the group. Use it to plan the next ride or talk about the last one. It's separate from [ride chat](/help/ride-chat), which is for the riders on one ride.

![A riding group chat](/help/img/group-chat.webp)

Group chat is free for everyone in the group. Only the riders in the group can read it or post in it.

## Open the Chat

1. Tap the **Groups** tab.
2. Tap the newest message under a group, or open the group and tap **Group Chat**.

Groups with messages you haven't read show a red count.

## Send a Message

1. Type in the box at the bottom.
2. Tap the send button.

Your message shows **Sending**, then **Sent**. If it can't go through, for example with no signal, it shows **Not Sent**. Tap **Retry** to send it again, or **Remove** to drop it.

Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send a lot of messages in a row, the app asks you to wait a minute.

## Talk About a Ride

You can tie a message to one of your rides, so everyone knows which ride you mean.

1. Tap **About a Ride** above the message box.
2. Under **Which Ride Is This About?**, pick the ride.
3. Type your message and send it.

The list shows rides you've joined that are happening now, coming up, or ended in the last 30 days. To send without a ride, tap the ride's name above the message box to remove it.

Rides the group has talked about show in a strip at the top of the chat. Tap a ride to see only the talk about it, and tap **Open the Ride** to go to its page. Tap **All Talk** to see every message again.

## Mute a Group

Tap **Mute** at the top of the chat to stop notifications from that group. Tap **Unmute** to turn them back on.

To turn off notifications for all your groups' chats, switch off **Riding Group Chat** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Clear a Message

- **Your own message:** press and hold it, then confirm **Clear**. It disappears for everyone, and this can't be undone.
- **If you run the group:** press and hold anyone's message and tap **Clear**.

## Report or Block a Rider

Press and hold someone else's message, then tap **Report Rider** or **Block Rider**. Messages from riders you've blocked aren't shown to you. See [Report and Block](/help/report-and-block).

articles.text:

title: Your Home Screen
summary: What's on the Rides tab from version 2.0. Join, create and find rides, Map Mode, your group, public rides near you, your feed, badges and toolkit.
category: getting-started
order: 15
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
