keywords: [home, home screen, rides tab, main screen, feed, activity, customize feed, who sees my activity, toolkit, public rides near me, distance, radius, 500 miles, rides left, unlimited, your group]
---

The **Rides** tab is your home screen. It puts the three things riders do most at the top (join, create and find a ride), then Map Mode, events, your rides, your crew and what your friends have been up to.

:::release 2.1
Join a Ride, Create a Ride, Find a Ride, Events and Map Mode all fit on the first screen, without scrolling, in that order. Scroll down for your rides, your crew and what your friends have been up to. On small phones like the iPhone SE, the greeting line is left out to make room.
:::

## At the Top

- **Good morning**, **Good afternoon** or **Good evening** with your ride name. When friends are out riding, a line under it says how many. Tap it for [Who's Riding](/help/out-riding).
- **The flag** shows the language the app is in (for example 🇺🇸 EN). Tap it to pick another. It shows when you're signed out too. See [Change the App's Language](/help/language).
- **The bell** opens your notifications, with a red number for new ones. See [See and Clear Your Notifications](/help/notifications-inbox).
- **Your picture** (or your first letter) opens the **You** tab.

## Join, Create and Find

- **Join a Ride**, the big red card: type the invite code from the ride leader and tap **Join**. You can also open a ride's link or scan its QR code with your phone's camera. Joining is **Unlimited** on every plan. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).
- **Create a Ride**, the dark card with the red flag under Join: the label says how many rides you have left this month on Free (**1 Left This Month**, or **None Left This Month**), or **Unlimited** on Pro and during the trial. Tap the label on Free to see what Pro adds. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
- **Find a Ride**: opens the map of public rides. The label shows how many are coming up near you, like **12 Within 500 mi**. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).

When one of your rides is live, a card says **Your ride is live. Tap to open Ride Mode**.

## Events

:::until 2.1
Under Join, Create, Find and Map Mode, the gold **Events** card opens the Events area: rallies, poker runs and ride weekends. It shows your next event (one you host or said you're going to), or else the next public event near you, and how many are coming up.
:::

:::release 2.1
Right under **Create a Ride** and **Find a Ride**, the gold **Events** card opens the Events area: rallies, poker runs and ride weekends. It shows your next event (one you host or said you're going to), or else the next public event near you, and how many are coming up.
:::

See [Events](/help/events).

## Map Mode

:::until 2.1
Your offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. It's the blue card right under **Create a Ride** and **Find a Ride**, and shows how many rider trails are near you when location is allowed.
:::

:::release 2.1
Your offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. It's the blue card under **Events**.
:::

- **Open Map Mode** opens Map Mode. The blue **Map Mode** button in the tab bar opens it too, from any tab.
- **Map a Custom Trail** opens Map Mode ready to draw a trail that isn't marked on any map.
- **Track Line** draws where you've been, a new colour each day: today red, yesterday blue, older days gold.

:::release 2.1
The **Track Line** switch is the small switch in the top corner of the Map Mode card. Tap it to turn the line on or off.
:::

See [Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails](/help/navigation-mode).

## Your Rides

- **Ride Invites**: rides your riding groups invited you to.
- **Your Next Ride**: the soonest ride you're on. If you're on more than one, tap **All** to see them all.
- **Past Rides**: rides that ended. Free shows your last few; see [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

Swipe a ride left to delete it (if you organize it) or leave it. On onmylead.com, click **Delete** or **Leave** at the end of the row. The app always asks first.

## Your Group

Your riding group with the newest group chat message (or your first group), with how many riders are in it, how many of them are out riding now, and the newest message.

- **Group Chat** opens the group's chat.
- **Plan a Group Ride** starts a new ride with that group already picked to invite. Creating rides follows your plan's ride limit.
- Tap the group's name for its page. With more than one group, **All** opens the **Groups** tab.

:::release 2.1
The card shows the group's photo next to its name, if the rider who made the group added one, or the group's initials. See [Add a Group Photo](/help/riding-groups#add-a-group-photo).
:::

No group yet? **Ride With the Same Crew?** takes you to the **Groups** tab. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups).

## Public Rides Near You

Upcoming public rides, nearest first, as cards you swipe sideways. Each shows how far away its meeting area is, the date and time, and the area. Tap one to open it.

To change how far it looks, tap the distance chip (**Within 500 mi** at first) and pick **50 mi**, **100 mi**, **250 mi**, **500 mi**, **1,000 mi** or **Anywhere**, then **Done**. Your phone remembers it.

The home screen never asks for your location. If you've already allowed it, rides are measured from where you are. If not, you see every upcoming public ride.

## Feed

What your friends, riders you follow and your riding groups have been up to in the last 30 days:

- friends out riding right now (always at the top),
- finished rides, with the miles and how many rode,
- badges earned,
- trails shared with every rider,
- rides posted to your riding groups.

Tap a post about a group ride or a trail to open it. The feed shows a few posts; tap **Show More** for the rest.

:::release 2.0
Riders' own posts show in the feed too. Tap the **heart** on any post to like it, or tap the post to open it in **Social** with every comment. **Open Social**, next to **Customize**, shows all your friends' activity, your friends and your posts. See [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social).
:::

:::release 2.1
A friend's post with a photo shows a small copy of the photo on the right; tap it, or the post, to open it in Social with the photo full width and every comment.
:::

A ride is named only if it was public or you were on it. Your location is never in anyone's feed: an Out Riding post says only the spot words the rider chose, and only to riders who could already see them on Who's Riding.

### Customize Your Feed

Tap **Customize**.

1. Under **Show Posts From**, pick **Friends**, **Friends and Riders I Follow**, or **Friends, Follows and My Groups**.
2. Under **What Shows**, turn off any kind of post you don't want: **Friends Out Riding**, **Finished Rides**, **Badges Earned**, **Trails Shared** or **Group Rides Posted**. From 2.0 there's also **Posts**.
3. Under **Who Sees Your Activity**, pick **Friends Only** (the default), **Friends and Followers** (riders who follow you as a leader) or **Nobody**.
4. Tap **Save**.

Your choices are saved to your account, so they're the same on every phone, tablet and the website. Blocked riders never see your posts, and you never see theirs. See [Add Friends](/help/friends), [Follow Leaders](/help/follow-leaders) and [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## Your Badges

Your rank and all seven badge patches. Tap **See All** (or the patches) for your progress. See [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks).

:::release 2.1
Tap **Leaderboard** beside **Your Badges** to see where you rank against other riders, everywhere or in your country and state. See [See the Badge Leaderboard](/help/badge-leaderboard).
:::

## Your Toolkit

Shortcuts to the tools that live on the **You** tab: **Who's Riding**, **Friends & Social** (your friends, their activity and your posts; see [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social)), **Garage**, **Trip Planner**, **Offline Maps**, **Starlink**, **Battery Saver** and **Share Location**.

## Help & Support

Opens Help and Support. At the top, **Help Center: How-To Guides** opens these step-by-step guides; below it are **Contact Us** and quick answers to common questions, each with a **Read the Guide** link.

:::release 2.1
## Your App Version

The very bottom of Home shows which version of OnMyLead you have, like **Version 2.1 (10)**: the version number, then the build number in brackets. The same line shows at the bottom of the logo screen for a moment when the app opens. It's on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets; the website is always the newest version, so it doesn't show one. Tell us this number when you [contact support](/help/contact-support).
:::

## On a Tablet

In landscape, and on a big window, Home has two columns: join, create, find, events, Map Mode, your toolkit and help on the left; your rides, group, public rides, feed and badges on the right. In portrait it's one column, like a phone. See [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet).

## On the Website

When you're signed in at onmylead.com, the **Rides** page is the same home screen.

title: Import a GPX Route
summary: Bring in a track from Gaia, onX or any GPX file and use it as your ride's route. A Pro feature.
category: routes-maps
order: 20
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05

  - app/src/core/entitlements.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261018000000_pro_entitlements.sql
related: [route-builder, free-vs-pro, map-layers, offline-maps]
keywords: [gpx, import, track, gaia, onx, file, upload route, gpx file, tablet]
---

Already have the trail you want to ride as a track in another app? Export it as a GPX file and import it as your ride's route. Riders see it in Ride Mode just like a route drawn in OnMyLead.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Drawing a route on the map stays free: see [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).

:::release 2.0
On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold **Pro** tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags.
:::

## Import a File

You need to be the ride's organizer or a co-organizer.

1. Open the ride, tap the **Map** tab, and tap **Build the Route** (or **Edit Route**).
2. Tap **Import GPX**.
3. Pick the GPX file. On iPhone it opens your Files, so save the file there first.
4. Check the track on the map. The panel shows its miles and how many track points it has.
5. Tap **Save Route**.

If you're on the Free plan, tapping **Import GPX** shows what Pro includes instead of opening the file picker.

:::release 1.0.3
A trail you recorded or saved in [Navigate](/help/navigation-mode) doesn't need a GPX file: tap **Use One of My Trails** instead. That's also a Pro feature.
:::

## What Gets Imported

- If the file has a track, the track is used.
- If it has no track, its route is used.
- If it has neither, its waypoints are joined in order.

The track's name from the file is kept with the route. Very long tracks are simplified a little so they load and draw quickly on every rider's phone.

:::note
Waypoints inside a GPX file aren't added as OnMyLead waypoints. To mark camp, fuel or a planned stop, see [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).
:::

## Change an Imported Route

An imported track is shown as it is, so you can't drag or add points to it.

- To use a different file, tap **Clear**, then **Import GPX** again.
- To draw your own instead, tap **Clear** and start tapping the map.

Tapping a line on an imported route's map shows that trail's name and who can ride it. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).

GPX import works with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android.

## If Your Pro Plan Ends

A route you already imported stays on the ride. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro.

## On the Website

**Import GPX** works the same way in the website's route builder. Pick the file from your computer.

## Troubleshooting

- **"That file is not a GPX file."** Go back to the other app, export the track as GPX (not KML or another format) and try again.
- **"That GPX file has no track in it."** The file doesn't have at least two points to draw. Export the track itself, not just a single waypoint.

articles.summary: Send your ride by text, email or any app, copy its link, show a QR code, or invite a whole riding group in one tap.
articles.text:
---
title: Invite Riders
summary: Send your ride by text, email or any app, copy its link, show a QR code, or invite a whole riding group in one tap.
category: joining
order: 30
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

related: [join-a-ride, qr-codes, riding-groups, create-a-ride, approvals-and-waitlist]
keywords: [invite, share, send, text, sms, email, link, copy link, invite code, invite group, crew, friends, tablet]
---

Every ride has a link, an invite code and a QR code. Send any of them and your friends can open the ride and join.

## Find the Invite Card

Right after you create a ride, its page opens with the invite card at the top. Later, open the ride page and tap **Riders** to find the **Invite Riders** card.

Anyone on a ride can share it, not just the organizer. On a public ride, anyone who can see the ride page can share it. On a private ride, only riders who have joined see the invite card.

## Send the Invite

On the invite card, tap:

- **Share Invite** to send it with any app on your phone
- **Text** to open a new text message
- **Email** to open a new email
- **Copy Link** to copy the ride's link, then paste it anywhere

The message includes the ride name, the link and the invite code. When your friend taps the link, the ride opens in OnMyLead if they have it, or on onmylead.com with a button to get the app.

On Android, ride and riding group links open straight in the OnMyLead app once it's installed.

## Share the Code

The **Invite Code** is shown in big letters on the card. Friends can type it on the **Rides** tab under **Join a Ride**. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

:::release 1.0.3
Want a code that's easy to say out loud, like MOAB-2026? The ride's organizers can tap **Choose Your Own Code** under the QR code, type a new one and tap **Save Code**. OnMyLead checks right away that no other ride uses it. The old link, QR code and code stop working; riders already on the ride stay on it. See [Choose Your Own Code](/help/custom-codes).
:::

## Show a QR Code

Tap **Show QR Code** (or the small QR code) to show it full screen, so riders at the trailhead can scan it off your phone. See [QR Codes](/help/qr-codes).

## Invite a Riding Group

Organizers can invite everyone in a riding group at once. Each rider gets a notification and sees the ride on their **Rides** tab, and they join with one tap.

From the ride page:

1. Open the ride page and tap **Riders**.
2. On the invite card, under **Invite a Group**, tap **Invite All** next to the group.

:::release 2.1
Each group shows its group photo (or its initials) beside its name.
:::

From the group:

1. On the **Groups** tab, open the group.
2. Tap **Invite to a Ride**.
3. Tap the ride. It lists the upcoming rides you organize.

You can also pick groups under **Invite a Group** when you create the ride. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).

:::note
Invited riders skip approval, even on a ride where you approve riders. Saving a riding group is a Pro feature, but inviting a group you're already in to your ride is not. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

## Public or Private?

- **Public** rides can also be found by riders near you or in your state on the Find tab.
- **Private** rides are only found by people you send the link, QR code or code to. Anyone holding them can join, so share them only with people you want on the ride.

articles.summary: Join with an invite link, a QR code or a code, or from Find. Learn what public and private rides show before and after you join.

title: Join a Ride
summary: Join with an invite link, a QR code or a code, or from Find. Learn what public and private rides show before and after you join.
category: joining
order: 20
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06

related: [find-a-ride, qr-codes, approvals-and-waitlist, check-in, invite-riders, sign-in]
keywords: [join, invite code, ride code, link, accept invite, sign up for ride, rsvp, leave ride, private ride, public ride, tablet]
---

Joining a ride is free, with no limit on how many rides you join. You need a free OnMyLead account.

## Join With a Link

1. Tap the ride link someone sent you.
2. If you have OnMyLead on your phone or tablet, the ride opens in the app. If not, it opens the ride's page on onmylead.com, with a button to get the app from the App Store or Google Play.
3. Tap **Join Ride**.

If you aren't signed in, the button says **Sign In to Join**. See [Sign In](/help/sign-in).

## Join With a Code

:::until 2.0
1. On the **Rides** tab, tap **Join a Ride**.
2. Type the invite code, for example 7F3A9C21.
3. Tap **Open**.
4. On the ride page, tap **Join Ride**.
:::

:::release 2.0
1. On the **Rides** tab, type the invite code in the **Join a Ride** card at the top, for example 7F3A9C21.
2. Tap **Join**.
3. On the ride page, tap **Join Ride**.
:::

:::release 1.0.3
Some organizers pick their own code, like MOAB-2026. Type it with the dashes. Capital or small letters both work.
:::

## Join With a QR Code

Point your phone's camera at the ride's QR code and tap the link that appears. See [QR Codes](/help/qr-codes).

## Join From Find

Public rides are listed on the **Find** tab. Open one and tap **Join Ride**. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).

## Join From a Group Invite

When someone invites your riding group, you get a notification and the ride shows under **Ride Invites** on the **Rides** tab.

1. Tap the ride.
2. In the **You're Invited** card, tap **Join Ride**, or **No Thanks** to turn it down.

You don't wait for approval when you're invited. If you say no thanks, you can still join later with the ride's link or code. On a ride where the organizer approves riders, you then ask to join like anyone else.

## Public and Private Rides

**Public** rides can be found on the Find tab, and anyone can open their page.

**Private** rides (marked **Private, Invite Only**) never show in Find. You need the link, QR code or invite code to see one.

Before you join either kind, the ride page shows the name, time, general area and details. After you join, you also see:

- The exact meeting point, and directions to it
- The organizer's instructions for joined riders
- The route and planned stops
- Who's going
- The ride chat

## After You Join

The ride shows under **Your Rides** on the **Rides** tab. On the ride page you'll find **Details**, **Map**, **Riders** and **Chat** sections. When you get to the meeting spot, tap **I'm Here and Ready** to check in. See [Check In](/help/check-in).

When the organizer starts the ride, tap **Enter Ride Mode**. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

If the ride is full, you go on the waitlist. If the organizer approves riders, you wait for them to say yes. See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist).

## Leave a Ride

:::until 2.0
1. Open the ride page and tap **Riders**.
2. Tap **Leave Ride**.
:::

:::release 2.0
1. Open the ride page. **Leave Ride** is the red-outlined button at the bottom, whichever section you're on (on a tablet, it's at the bottom of the left column).
2. Tap **Leave Ride**. A box tells you what happens; tap **Leave Ride** again to confirm, or **Stay**.

In Ride Mode, tap **Together** (or **Separated**) at the top to open **Riders**, and **Leave Ride** is under the list. On a tablet it's at the bottom of the **Riders** sidebar. You go back to the **Rides** tab when you've left.

Leaving always stops your phone sharing your location for that ride, whether or not the ride has started.

Organized the ride? See [Leave a Ride You Organize](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).
:::

Or, on the **Rides** tab, swipe left on the ride and tap **Leave** (on onmylead.com, click **Leave** at the end of the ride's row). Your spot opens up for someone else. You can rejoin with the ride's link or code if there's room. If the ride is live, leaving also stops sharing your location with the group.

:::note
You can't join a ride that has ended or been cancelled.
:::

:::release 2.0
## Rides That Are Part of an Event

A ride that belongs to an event shows **Part of** and the event's name at the top of its page; tap it to see the event's agenda and its other rides. You can also join a ride from the event's **Group Rides** with **See Ride and Join**. See [Events](/help/events).
:::

articles.title: Change the App's Language
articles.summary: OnMyLead uses your phone's language when it speaks it, and English when it doesn't. Pick another language any time from the flag on Home or You > Language.
articles.text:
---
title: Change the App's Language
summary: OnMyLead uses your phone's language when it speaks it, and English when it doesn't. Pick another language any time from the flag on Home or You > Language.
category: account
order: 76
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/language.tsx
  - app/src/components/language-button.tsx
  - app/src/core/i18n.ts
  - app/src/lib/i18n.ts
  - app/src/lib/language-sync.ts
  - app/src/lib/voice.ts
  - app/src/core/translations/es.ts
related: [appearance, sync-across-devices, home-screen]
keywords: [language, languages, translate, translation, spanish, español, portuguese, french, german, italian, russian, chinese, japanese, korean, hindi, indonesian, english, flag, idioma, langue, sprache]
---

OnMyLead speaks 12 languages. The first time you open it, it uses your phone's language if it's one of them, and English if it isn't. You can switch at any time, and the app redraws in the new language straight away.

| Language | Flag shown |
|---|---|
| English | 🇺🇸 |
| Español (Spanish) | 🇪🇸 |
| Português (Portuguese) | 🇧🇷 |
| Français (French) | 🇫🇷 |
| Deutsch (German) | 🇩🇪 |
| Italiano (Italian) | 🇮🇹 |
| Русский (Russian) | 🇷🇺 |
| 中文（简体） (Chinese, Simplified) | 🇨🇳 |
| 日本語 (Japanese) | 🇯🇵 |
| 한국어 (Korean) | 🇰🇷 |
| हिन्दी (Hindi) | 🇮🇳 |
| Bahasa Indonesia (Indonesian) | 🇮🇩 |

## Change the Language

1. On **Home**, tap the flag at the top, next to the bell. It shows the flag and two letters of the language the app is in now (for example 🇺🇸 EN). You can also go to **You** > **Language**.
2. Tap a language. Each one is listed in its own words, so you can find yours whatever the app is showing now.
3. The app redraws in that language and brings you back to the Language screen.

To go back to following your phone, tap **Match Phone** at the top of the list. It shows which language your phone is set to.

## What Changes and What Doesn't

:::until 2.1
- The main screens switch: Home, the tab bar, You and its settings, Appearance, Language, Sign In, and the titles at the top of every screen. Some newer screens are still in English while they're translated.
:::

:::release 2.1
- The whole app switches: Home, Ride Mode, Map Mode, ride and group pages, chat, Events, Social, Friends, Garage, Trips, Starlink, Tilt, Pro and every setting, along with the alerts and messages OnMyLead shows you.
- Places on the Leaderboard and along the Ride Mode line are written your language's way (2.º in Spanish, 2. in German, 2 位 in Japanese), and counts like "1 Coming Up" use the right singular or plural.
- Spoken alerts in Ride Mode are read in your language. If the voice you picked under **You** > **Voice** speaks another language, your phone's own voice for your language reads them instead.
- Status buttons and the built-in quick replies (like **Need Fuel** or **Flat Tire**) show in each rider's own language, so a rider who reads Spanish sees them in Spanish even if you sent them in English. A Ride Mode message you type with the same words as a built-in quick reply (like "on my way") shows as that quick reply.
- What riders write themselves (posts, comments, chat messages and your own quick replies) shows exactly as they wrote it.
- Push notifications on your lock screen, the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy are still in English.
- The [CarPlay](/help/carplay) screen in your car uses the same language as the app.
:::
- Things riders write stay the way they wrote them: ride names, chat, posts, group names and trail names.
- On iPhone and iPad, the permission messages (location, camera, photos, motion) also show in your language.
- Distances stay in miles.

## Your Other Devices

Your choice is saved to your account, so when you sign in on your iPad, an Android phone or tablet, or onmylead.com, it switches too (see [Sync Across Devices](/help/sync-across-devices)). If you leave it on **Match Phone**, each device follows its own language.

## Device Differences

- **iPhone and iPad:** you can also set OnMyLead's language in the iPhone **Settings** app > **OnMyLead** > **Language**. With **Match Phone** picked in the app, it follows that setting.
- **Android phones and tablets (Android 13 and later):** you can also set it in **Settings** > **System** > **Languages** > **App languages** > **OnMyLead**. With **Match Phone** picked in the app, it follows that setting.
- **onmylead.com:** once you're signed in, the flag is on Home and the Language row is on You. **Match Phone** follows your browser's language. The signed-out homepage stays in English.

articles.title: Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner
articles.summary: Who rides up front, who rides at the rear, and how to make someone leader, pick a tail gunner or hand off the ride.
articles.text:
---
title: Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner
summary: Who rides up front, who rides at the rear, and how to make someone leader, pick a tail gunner or hand off the ride.
category: rides
order: 50
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/components/rider-pin.tsx
  - app/src/components/rider-puck.tsx
  - app/src/components/rider-dot.tsx
  - app/src/core/leaving.ts
  - app/src/components/leave-ride.tsx
  - app/src/components/ride-roster.tsx
  - app/src/core/roles.ts
  - app/src/core/chat.ts
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx
  - app/src/lib/api.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261014000000_ride_handoff_tail_gunner.sql
  - supabase/migrations/20261015000000_notification_settings.sql
related: [organizer-controls, ride-mode, ride-bubble, ride-chat, follow-leaders]
keywords: [leader, lead, sweep, tail gunner, tail, rear, back of the pack, hand off, give ride, transfer, co-leader, roles, tablet]
---

Every group ride needs someone up front and someone at the back. OnMyLead shows the riding order on the roster: the leader first, the tail gunner last, everyone else in between.

## The Roles

- **Organizer**: the rider who created the ride (or was given it). Runs the ride page, starts and ends Ride Mode, and leads unless someone else is made leader.
- **Leader**: rides up front. Messages sent to the leader in ride chat go to them.
- **Tail Gunner**: rides at the rear so nobody gets left behind. In OnMyLead, the tail gunner is the sweep.
- **Rider**: everyone else.

On the **Riders** section of the ride page, the line at the top of the **Going** list shows who is **Leader** and who is **Tail Gunner** (or "Not picked yet").

:::release 2.1
## On the Map

In Ride Mode the leader and the tail gunner stand out from everyone else: the leader is the biggest dot, in blue with a blue name tag, and the tail gunner is the next biggest, in violet with a violet name tag. Every other rider is a graphite dot with a dark name tag. The riders list uses the same colors.

A blue line also follows behind the leader on every rider's map, so the group can see exactly where the leader went. The leader can turn it off for everyone in **Map Settings**. See [Follow the Leader's Trackline](/help/leader-trackline).
:::

## Make Someone Leader

The organizer can put another rider up front while still organizing.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name in the **Going** list.
3. Tap **Make Leader**.

To take the lead back, tap their name and tap **Remove as Leader**. You can make more than one rider a leader.

## Pick a Tail Gunner

The organizer or the leader can pick the one rider who rides at the rear.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name.
3. Tap **Make Tail Gunner**.

There's only one tail gunner at a time. Picking someone new moves the job to them. To clear it, tap the tail gunner's name and tap **Remove as Tail Gunner**. The leader and organizers ride up front, so they can't also be tail gunner.

## Hand Off the Lead

A rider who was made leader can pass the lead to someone else.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name.
3. Tap **Hand Them the Lead**, then **Hand Off**.

They lead from here, messages to the leader go to them, and you stay on the ride as a rider.

## Give Away the Whole Ride

The organizer can hand the entire ride to another rider, for example if you can't make it.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name.
3. Tap **Give Them the Ride**, then **Give Ride**.

They become the organizer and the leader. You stay on the ride as a rider and can't undo this yourself.

:::release 2.0
## Leave a Ride You Organize

Can't make it? You don't have to cancel the ride on everyone.

1. Tap **Leave Ride** at the bottom of the ride page (or under **Riders** in Ride Mode).
2. **Who Takes Over?** lists everyone who has joined, leaders and co-organizers first. Tap who should run it.
3. Tap **Give Ride and Leave**.

They become the organizer and the leader, and you're off the ride. Your location sharing for the ride stops. You can rejoin later as a rider with the ride's link or code.

Rather call it off? Tap **Cancel the Ride Instead**. If nobody else has joined yet, **Leave Ride** offers to cancel the ride, since there's nobody to hand it to. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).

If you were made leader (but aren't the organizer) and you leave, the lead goes back to the organizer.
:::

:::note
Roles can only go to riders who have joined the ride, and they can't change after the ride has ended or been cancelled.
:::

The rider gets a notification when they're made leader, made tail gunner or given the ride.

:::release 1.0.3
Leading a ride earns toward the **Trail Boss** badge, and riding at the rear as tail gunner earns toward **Tail Gunner**. See [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks).
:::

articles.title: Follow the Leader's Trackline
articles.summary: A line in the leader's blue shows where the leader went in Ride Mode. Older passes fade when the leader crosses back over it. The leader can turn it off.
articles.text:
---
title: Follow the Leader's Trackline
summary: A line in the leader's blue shows where the leader went in Ride Mode. Older passes fade when the leader crosses back over it. The leader can turn it off.
category: ride-mode
order: 15
release: "2.1"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/core/leader-trackline.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-leader-trackline.ts
  - app/src/components/leader-trackline.tsx
  - app/src/components/leader-trackline-ink.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-leader-trail.ts
  - app/src/components/trail-map-overlay.tsx
  - app/src/components/group-mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/group-map.tsx
  - supabase/migrations/20261104210000_leader_trackline.sql
related: [ride-mode, leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner, map-layers, privacy]
keywords: [trackline, track line, trail line, breadcrumb, leader line, leader path, where did the leader go, follow the leader, blue line, faded line, dashed line, double back, crossing]
---

In Ride Mode, a line follows behind the leader on every rider's map, in the same blue as the leader's dot. It shows exactly where the leader rode, so at a fork, a wash or a faint two-track you can see which way they went.

The line starts when you open Ride Mode and grows as the leader moves. The leader sees it on their own map too.

## When the Leader Crosses Their Own Line

If the leader crosses the line, rides a loop back to where they started, or doubles back down the same trail, everything from before that point turns faded, thinner and dashed. The line from there on stays bright solid blue and is drawn on top. So where two passes share a trail, the bright line is always the newest one, the one to follow.

Short wiggles, a tight hairpin, or wandering a few yards off the old line on the way back don't start a new pass.

## Turn It Off (Leader)

The line is on for every ride unless the leader turns it off. Turning it off hides it for everyone on the ride, and turning it back on brings it back for everyone, including the part ridden while it was off.

1. In Ride Mode, tap the round **Map Settings** button on the map.
2. Under **Leader Trackline**, tap the row to switch between **On for Everyone** and **Off for Everyone**.

The switch shows for the leader and the ride's organizers. If nobody has the Leader role, the organizer leads. Riders see the line but not the switch. With no signal the switch can't save; try again when you have service.

## Good to Know

- Each phone draws the line from the leader's live position, which riders on the ride already see. Nothing new is uploaded. Your phone keeps the line for the ride you're on, so closing Ride Mode and coming back doesn't lose it, and the next ride's line replaces it.
- If your phone stops hearing from the leader for a while (no signal, or Ride Mode was closed), the line has a gap rather than a straight line across the map. A stop, like lunch or a regroup, doesn't fade the line behind the leader. Open Ride Mode early to see the whole ride.
- If the leader changes partway through the ride, the line starts again from the new leader.
- **iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets:** the line shows on every map style, including 3D Terrain and the flat Apple or Google map.
- **Website:** the line shows on the live Mapbox map. Where the website shows only a sketch of the route, there's no line.

articles.title: Share Your Location
articles.summary: Choose who sees your location and for how long, from a few hours to until you turn it off. You can stop it any time.
articles.text:
---
title: Share Your Location
summary: Choose who sees your location and for how long, from a few hours to until you turn it off. You can stop it any time.
category: safety-privacy
order: 10
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/live.tsx
  - app/src/app/share.tsx
  - app/src/components/share-picker.tsx
  - app/src/components/date-calendar.tsx
  - app/src/components/time-picker.tsx
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx
  - app/src/core/sharing.ts
  - app/src/core/freshness.ts
  - app/src/lib/location.ts
  - app/src/lib/api.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261007000000_init.sql
related: [ride-mode, family-link, privacy, ride-summary-and-ride-again, troubleshooting]
keywords: [share location, location, gps, tracking, stop sharing, background location, always allow, timer, battery, who can see me, tablet, until I turn it off, forever, end date, calendar]
---

OnMyLead only shares your location when you turn it on, only with the people you choose, and only for as long as you pick. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just the app.

:::until 1.0.2
Every share ends on its own.
:::

There are two ways to share:

- **With a ride:** everyone on the ride sees you on the Ride Mode map.

:::release 2.0
On a Freeride, if you're the leader, each rider's phone keeps the path you've ridden while they're in Ride Mode, built from the same live location they already see, to measure how far behind you everyone is. It stays on their phone, isn't uploaded, and is cleared after 18 hours or when they open another Freeride.
:::

- **With chosen people:** riders you pick, a family link, or both, from **Share My Location**.

## Share with Your Ride

When you open Ride Mode on a live ride and aren't sharing yet, the app asks **Share Your Location with This Ride?**

1. Open Ride Mode. See [Use Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).
:::until 1.0.2
2. Pick how long to share: **2 Hours**, **4 Hours**, **8 Hours** or **Until I Leave the Ride**.
3. Or type your own length in **Hours** and tap **Share**. The longest you can pick is 24 hours.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
2. Pick how long to share: **2 Hours**, **4 Hours**, **8 Hours** or **Until I Turn It Off**.
3. Or tap **Pick an End Date**, pick the day on the calendar (or type it), set **Stop Sharing At**, and tap the **Share Until** button. See [Pick an End Date](#pick-an-end-date).
:::

4. If your iPhone asks for location access, allow it. Choose **Always** so the group keeps seeing you with the phone locked.

Only riders on this ride see you. Tap **Not Now** to skip. You can start sharing later by tapping the **Off** pill at the top of Ride Mode.

### Check or Stop Ride Sharing

The pill at the top of Ride Mode shows the time left, such as **1h 20m**, or **On** when you picked

:::until 1.0.2
**Until I Leave the Ride**.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
**Until I Turn It Off**. A share that runs for more than a day shows days, such as **3d**.
:::

1. Tap the pill. A banner shows **Sharing** and the time left.
2. Tap **Stop** to stop sharing now, or **Hide** to fold the banner back into the pill.

### When Ride Sharing Ends

Sharing with a ride stops on its own at the first of these:

- Your timer runs out, or the end date you picked arrives.
- The organizer ends or cancels the ride.
- You leave the ride.
- You tap **Stop**.

:::release 1.0.2
Even **Until I Turn It Off** stops when the ride ends or you leave it. Sharing with a ride never carries on after the ride.
:::

Closing Ride Mode, or locking your phone, doesn't stop sharing. If the app was closed or your phone restarted, opening Ride Mode picks your share back up.

## Share with Chosen Riders or Family

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **On the Trail**, tap **Share My Location**.
3. Under **Who Can See You**, tap the riders you want. Only people you've been on a ride with are listed.
4. To share with someone who doesn't have the app, turn on **Family Link**. See [Share a Family Link](/help/family-link).
:::until 1.0.2
5. Under **For How Long**, pick **15 Min**, **1 Hour**, **4 Hours**, **8 Hours** or **Until I Turn It Off (Max 24 Hours)**, or type your own length in **Hours** and tap **Share**.

**Until I Turn It Off** still stops by itself after 24 hours, so a forgotten share always ends.

While you share, **Share My Location** shows a card for each share with **Sharing Now** and the time left.

- Tap **Add 1 Hour** to keep going longer. In the last 10 minutes, the button says **Ending Soon · Add 1 Hr**.
- Tap **Stop** to end it now.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
5. Under **For How Long**, pick **15 Min**, **1 Hour**, **4 Hours** or **8 Hours**, tap **Until I Turn It Off**, or tap **Pick an End Date** to choose a day and time on a calendar.

**Until I Turn It Off** has no time limit. It keeps sharing, even for days, until you tap **Stop Sharing**. The app asks you to confirm before it starts.

While you share, **Share My Location** shows a card for each share with **Sharing Now** and when it ends: the time left, the end date (such as **until Sat, Nov 14, 6:00 PM**), or **until you turn it off**. On the **You** tab, the **Share My Location** row also says you're sharing and until when, so a long share is never forgotten.

- Tap **Add 1 Hour** to keep going longer. In the last 10 minutes, the button says **Ending Soon · Add 1 Hr**. A share set to **Until I Turn It Off** doesn't need it, so it isn't shown.
- Tap **Stop Sharing** to end it now.

## Pick an End Date

Both the ride sharing sheet and **Share My Location** let you pick exactly when sharing stops, up to a year out.

1. Tap **Pick an End Date**. A calendar opens.
2. Tap a day, or type the date in the box above the calendar. Use the arrows to change months.
:::until 1.0.3
3. Check **Stop Sharing At**. It starts at 6:00 pm (or about an hour from now, later today). Type a different time, such as "9:30 am".
:::
:::release 1.0.3
3. Check **Stop Sharing At**. It starts at 6:00 PM (or about an hour from now, later today). To change it, tap the time, then tap **AM** or **PM**, the hour and the minute.
:::
4. Tap the button, such as **Share Until Sat, Nov 14, 6:00 PM**.

A share with an end date still stops early if you tap **Stop Sharing**, and a ride share still stops when the ride ends.
:::

## Location in the Background

To keep your group updated while your phone is locked or in your pocket, OnMyLead needs location access set to **Always**. You can change it any time in your iPhone's **Settings > OnMyLead > Location**. While OnMyLead is using your location in the background, iPhone shows its location indicator.

On Android, allow location **While Using the App**. OnMyLead doesn't need **Allow All the Time**. While you share, Android shows a **Sharing Your Location** notification, and that is what keeps your group updated with the phone locked. Tap it to see who can see you or to stop sharing. On Android 13 and later, also allow notifications when asked, or that notification stays hidden.

:::release 1.0.1
If you turn off location for OnMyLead while you're sharing with a ride, Ride Mode shows a **Location Is Off** notice once, because your group can't see you move. Turn location back on for OnMyLead in your phone's **Settings** to keep sharing.
:::

Keep **Precise Location** on for OnMyLead (on Android, **Use precise location**). With only an approximate location, your group sees you up to a few miles from where you are. See [Make Your Location Accurate](/help/accurate-location).

:::release 2.0
On Android, when you start sharing, OnMyLead asks once to change to a precise location if you allowed only an approximate one, and to turn on Google Location Accuracy if it's off.
:::

Your phone sends a new position each time you move about 25 meters (80 feet), and at least every 15 seconds while you're stopped, so the group can tell you're still there.

:::release 1.0.1
To make your battery last longer, you can have your phone send less often with [Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver). It starts on **Best Accuracy**, the rate above.
:::

## With No Service

Live tracking needs a connection. When your phone has no service:

- The group sees where you were last seen, with how long ago, never a dot that looks live.
- While you share with a ride, your phone keeps recording your track. When you get service again, your current position goes up, and the points from the dead zone are added to your ride track for your [ride summary](/help/ride-summary-and-ride-again).
- Sharing still ends at its end time, even if your phone can't reach the server.

Offline maps keep the map on your screen without service, but positions only update when phones have a connection. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

:::release 2.1
The exception is riders close by on the same ride: phones within Bluetooth range (about 30 to 100 meters) pass spots to each other with no service, encrypted for the ride only. Seeing those spots and sending yours over Bluetooth is part of OnMyLead Pro. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
:::

## Who Sees What

- **Ride sharing:** riders who have joined that ride.
- **Chosen riders:** only the riders you picked are allowed to see your position.
- **Family link:** anyone who has the link, until the share ends.

:::release 1.0.2
## Stopping a Long Share

A share set to **Until I Turn It Off** or a far-off end date keeps your phone's location on in the background, which uses more battery. To stop it, tap the **You** tab, tap **Share My Location**, and tap **Stop Sharing**. On Android you can also tap the **Sharing Your Location** notification to get there. [Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver) makes a long share easier on the battery.
:::

Your exact location is never shown publicly. See [Privacy](/help/privacy).

---

OnMyLead Pro is billed by Apple, so you change or cancel it in your Apple Account settings. The app takes you straight there.

## Cancel or Change Your Plan in the App

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Manage Subscription**.
3. Apple's subscription screen opens. Choose a different plan, or cancel your subscription.

If you pay for Pro, the Pro screen also has a **Manage Subscription** button where the plans usually are.

## Cancel or Change It on Android

On Android, Pro is billed by Google Play. **Manage Subscription** opens Google Play's subscription page for OnMyLead, where you can change plans or cancel. You can also do it in the **Play Store** app: tap your profile picture, then **Payments & Subscriptions** > **Subscriptions** > **OnMyLead**.

If you bought Pro on a different kind of device (on an iPhone while you're on Android, or the other way round), **Manage Subscription** tells you which store bills it and opens that store's subscription page. Cancel it there.

## Cancel or Change It in iPhone Settings

1. Open the **Settings** app on your iPhone.
2. Tap your name at the top.
3. Tap **Subscriptions**.
4. Tap **OnMyLead**, then choose a plan or cancel.

:::warning
To avoid being charged for the next period, cancel at least 24 hours before your current period ends. The subscription renews automatically until you turn it off.
:::

## Check When It Renews

On the **Subscription** screen, **Your Plan** shows **Pro** and the date it renews or ends.

## What Happens When Pro Ends

When a subscription you cancelled reaches the end of the period you paid for, your account moves to Free. Nothing is deleted:

- **Rides:** every ride you created stays. Free accounts create one new ride a month.
- **Routes:** routes you already imported from GPX stay and stay editable. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro.
- **Offline maps:** maps already on your phone keep working. Downloading new map areas needs Pro.
- **Riding groups:** your groups stay, with their chats, and you can still invite them to your rides. Creating a group or adding and removing riders needs Pro.
- **Polls:** polls already sent can still be voted on. Creating a new poll needs Pro.
- **Ride history:** Home shows your last 5 past rides. The rest are saved, and show again if you upgrade.
- **Trips:** your trips stay. Free plans one active trip at a time.

See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) for the full comparison.

## Good to Know

- Deleting your OnMyLead account does not cancel the Apple subscription. Cancel it in your Apple subscriptions too, so you aren't billed again. See [Delete Your Account](/help/delete-account).
- If your plan says **Complimentary Pro**, it was given to you by OnMyLead and isn't billed by Apple, so there's nothing to cancel.

- Deleting your OnMyLead account doesn't cancel a Google Play subscription either. Cancel it in Google Play too.
- On Android, **Your Plan** also says which store bills your Pro.
- Subscriptions can only be managed in the app on your phone or tablet. On the website, the Subscription screen says so.

OnMyLead's maps can show public trails and roads over satellite imagery or a topo map. Tap a trail to see its name and which vehicles are allowed on it.

![Trail lines and rider dots on the satellite map](/help/img/map.webp)

:::release 2.0
Satellite, topo and the trails layer are Pro features. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, **Map Style** carries a **Pro** tag and the map shows the standard map.
:::

## Open the Layers

:::until 2.1
The layers button is the round button with a stacked layers icon in the top-right corner of the map. You'll find it on:
:::

:::release 2.1
The round **Map Settings** button (a two-slider icon) is in the top-left corner of the map, level with the compass on the right (the compass shows once the map is turned away from north). While a screen's top bar is showing, both sit just under it so nothing covers them; in [Full Map](/help/full-map) they move up to the top of the screen and stay there. On an iPad or Android tablet, Ride Mode puts the button just right of the riders column, and Map Mode, the route builder and the waypoints map held sideways put it just right of the panel. On onmylead.com the compass is with the zoom buttons instead. You'll find it on:
:::

- Ride Mode's map
- Map Mode
- A ride's waypoints map
- The route builder
- The area picker for offline maps

:::until 2.1
Tap it to open the **Map Style** panel. Tap it again to close the panel.
:::

:::release 2.1
Tap it to open **Map Settings** (below). Swipe the sheet down, tap the map, or tap **X** to close it.

In Ride Mode the leader and the ride's organizers also see **Leader Trackline** in Map Settings, to turn the line behind the leader on or off for everyone. See [Follow the Leader's Trackline](/help/leader-trackline).
:::

:::release 2.1
## Map Settings

From 2.1 the stacked-layers button is the round **Map Settings** button, with a two-slider icon, and it opens **Map Settings**, one sheet for everything about the map. On a phone it slides up from the bottom; on a tablet held sideways it sits on the right so you can watch the map change. The map stays lightly visible behind it, so each change shows as you make it. Swipe it down, tap the map, or tap **X** to close it. A small blue dot on the button means the map isn't showing the standard set.

- **Map Style**: **Satellite**, **Topo** and **3D Terrain**, each shown as a picture. The one you're using has a blue ring and a check.
- **On the Map**: four big switches, each with a strip of map showing the lines it draws:
  - **Streets and Roads**: highways, paved roads, dirt roads and street-legal-only roads.
  - **Off-Road Trails**: motorized trails and tracks, including width-limited trails.
  - **Hiking Trails**: foot and horse trails.
  - **Land Boundaries**: national forests, BLM land, national and state parks. Turning it on leaves **Property Lines** off; turn that on under **Every Map Feature**.

  A switch is on while any of its lines shows. Tapping it turns them all off, or all on.
- **Every Map Feature**: tap **Fine-Tune** to open the full list below, one row per kind of line or land.
- **Leader Trackline**: for the leader and organizers in Ride Mode.
- **Your Dot** (Ride Mode and Map Mode): **Dot Style** picks how your own dot looks: **Red, White and Blue** (a glossy navy dome with a white arrow inside a red band and a white rim, the default; a white star when your phone can't tell which way you're facing), **Safety Orange** (an orange 3D dome with a white arrow and a silver rim), **Hi-Viz Dome** (lime with a black arrow), **Reflective Ring**, **Floating Arrowhead** or **Classic** (the cyan dot). **Dot Size** sets how big it is: **Small**, **Medium** or **Large**. Both are also on the **You** tab. Picking a style or size other than Red, White and Blue at Medium is part of OnMyLead Pro; on Free the picker shows the **Pro** tag and your dot stays the default.
- **Following** (Ride Mode and Map Mode): **Follow Me** keeps your dot on screen; **Zoom Out at the Edge** zooms out one step the first time your dot nears an edge, then the next time the map centers on you and moves with you; **Zoom In at Intersections** (on the Mapbox map) closes in on a junction so you can see which way to go. See [Follow Me](/help/follow-me).
- **Map Buttons** (Ride Mode and Map Mode): **Tilt Meter** (iPhone, iPad and Android) and **Music Button** (where music controls are available).
- **Download This Ride's Map** (Ride Mode), **Offline Maps**, and who the map data comes from.

The Your Dot, Following and Map Buttons settings are the same ones as on the **You** tab, so a change shows everywhere.

The round **3D** button from earlier 2.1 test builds is gone: pick **3D Terrain** under **Map Style** instead.

From 2.1 your own dot is a safety-orange 3D dome, half again as big as before at **Medium**, so it's easy to spot on a mount. Other riders' dots keep their colors (the leader blue, the tail gunner violet), so yours stands out.
:::

Your choices are remembered on your phone and used on every map in the app.

:::release 2.1
## One Map Everywhere

From 2.1 every map in the app, on iPhone, iPad, Android and onmylead.com, is drawn by Mapbox, so a map looks and works the same wherever you open it: the same satellite photos, the same topo, the same trail lines and names, and the same pinch, turn and tap. The website's Ride Mode now has the same live map as the apps.

On a Free account the map is Mapbox's outdoors map, with roads, trails, contour lines and shaded hills. Satellite, Topo and 3D Terrain are Pro.
:::

## Satellite or Topo

At the top of the panel, pick:

:::release 2.0
Each style has a small picture of how it looks; the one you're using has a blue outline.
:::

- **Satellite**: aerial imagery with road and place labels. This is the default.
- **Topo**: the USGS topographic map, with contour lines.

:::release 2.1
- **3D Terrain**: satellite on the real shape of the land, with contour lines and peak heights. It shows in Ride Mode and Map Mode; the other maps show plain satellite while it's picked. See [3D Terrain](/help/3d-terrain).
:::

:::release 2.1
## Map Features

**Map Features** lists every kind of line and land the map can show, in three groups: **Roads**, **Trails** and **Land**. Each row has a small picture of exactly how it looks on the map, its name and a line about what it is. Tap a row to turn it on or off; a blue check means it's showing. **Show All** and **Hide All** next to a group's name turn the whole group on or off.

### Roads

- **Highways and Freeways**: interstates, freeways and major highways, a heavy solid blue line. They show from far out.
- **Paved Public Roads**: state, county and town roads, a lighter blue line, with route numbers or names when zoomed in.
- **Dirt Roads**: Forest Service, BLM and county dirt roads, a solid white line.
- **Street-Legal Only**: Forest Service roads open only to plated, highway-legal vehicles, a solid lavender line. Take an unplated UTV or dirt bike somewhere else.

### Trails

- **Off-Road Trails**: motorized trails and dirt tracks, bold amber dashes, with names.
- **Width-Limited Trails**: Forest Service trails open only to vehicles 50 inches wide or less, or only to dirt bikes, shorter orange dashes.
- **Hiking Trails**: foot and horse trails with no motor vehicles, a thinner pink dash-dot line with a light outline, so it never looks like a trail you can drive. They come from Forest Service trails closed to motor vehicles, BLM non-motorized trails and OpenStreetMap paths.
- **Closures**: red dashes. See [Closed Trails and Roads](#closed-trails-and-roads).
- **Rider Trails**: mint dots. See [Rider Trails](#rider-trails).
- **Park Trails**: the trails of offroad parks in the park's own level colors (green, blue, white, red). Free for everyone. See [Park Trails](#park-trails).

Roads, trails and closures are all on unless you turn them off. Highways, paved roads and hiking paths from OpenStreetMap are drawn on Mapbox maps (every map from 2.1); on the rare map that falls back to Apple, Google or the website's basic map, the base map shows roads in its own colors.

### Land

Land is off until you turn it on, since it tints the whole map:

- **National Forests**: Forest Service land and grasslands, tinted green with a green edge.
- **BLM Land**: Bureau of Land Management land, tinted gold.
- **National Parks**: national parks, monuments and recreation areas, tinted purple.
- **State Parks**: state parks and state recreation areas, tinted teal.
- **Property Lines**: private parcel lines in coral, in Texas for now. They show when you're zoomed in to a few blocks across. No owner names are shown.

Land shows once the map is about one county across (about 60 miles on a phone screen), fading in as you zoom, with each area's name when you're zoomed in closer. Further out it stays hidden, so whole states aren't covered in color. If you turned land on and see **Zoom In to See Land Boundaries**, zoom in a little. iPad and Android tablets show it at the same zoom as a phone, over their bigger map. Tap the map with land on to see a card with whose land it is: the area's name, who manages it, whether it's open to the public and its size. In Texas, with **Property Lines** on, tapping private land shows **Property Parcel**, its county and acres. If you tap a trail, its card comes first.

Land boundaries come from public records (USGS PAD-US and the Texas Geographic Information Office) and can be out of date. Posted signs and fences always win. Land doesn't download with an offline map yet; it shows when you have signal.

Your Map Features choices are saved and follow you to your other devices.
:::

:::until 2.1
## Public Trails and Roads

Turn **Public Trails and Roads** on to draw trail and road lines on the map. It's on unless you turn it off.
:::

:::until 1.0.1
- **Trail**: a dashed sand-colored line.
- **Road**: a solid pale line.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
- **Trail**: a bold dashed amber line.
- **Road**: a solid white line.
- **Closed**: red dashes on a dark outline. See [Closed Trails and Roads](#closed-trails-and-roads).

Every line has a dark outline, so it stands out on forest, desert and snow.

### Trail and Road Names

Zoomed in, the map shows names:

- OpenStreetMap trails get a name tag in the middle of the trail, like **Hell's Revenge 4x4 Trail**. A tag with a red border and **Closed** marks a trail mapped as closed or private. Each name follows its line's switch: Off-Road Trails names show with **Off-Road Trails**, hiking path names with **Hiking Trails**.
- Forest Service roads and trails show their name and number along the line, like **Jenny Lind 414.1**.
- Road names come from the satellite map's own labels, and the topo map has its own road names.
:::

The lines come from:

- **USDA Forest Service**: the Motor Vehicle Use Map roads and trails.
- **Bureau of Land Management**: BLM routes.

:::release 2.1
BLM moved its route map to a new address in 2026, which kept BLM lines from showing for a while. From 2.1 they show again: motorized roads in white, motorized trails as amber dashes, and trails closed to motor vehicles as pink hiking trails.

Trail lines also show up faster when you zoom in. The Forest Service and BLM draw their lines on request, so the map now asks them for far fewer, bigger pieces at a time, and close in, Mapbox draws OpenStreetMap tracks and their names itself as you pinch, instead of waiting for the map to finish loading.
:::
- **OpenStreetMap**: tracks mapped by riders, including off-road parks, state land and county roads.

:::until 1.0.2
Trail lines show once you zoom in. If you see **Zoom In to See Trails**, zoom in a little. If you see **Zoom In for Park and Local Trails**, the Forest Service and BLM lines are showing, and the OpenStreetMap tracks appear when you zoom in closer.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
Trail lines show from pretty far out. Forest Service and BLM lines appear when the map is about 60 miles across a phone screen, and OpenStreetMap tracks when it's about 15 miles across. iPad and Android tablets show them at the same zoom as a phone, over their bigger map.

- If you see **Zoom In to See Trails**, zoom in a little.
- If you see **Zoom In for Park and Local Trails**, the Forest Service and BLM lines are showing, and the OpenStreetMap tracks appear when you zoom in a bit more.
- Zoomed far out, the map draws the longest trails first and fills in short spurs as you zoom in.
- Lines already on screen stay put while you pan and zoom.
:::

:::release 1.0.3
## Rider Trails

Trails other riders mapped and shared in [Navigate](/help/navigation-mode) are drawn as **mint dotted lines**, so you can tell them apart from agency and OpenStreetMap trails. They show once you zoom in to about a county's width, when you're signed in. Tap one to see its card: it says **User Submitted Trail**, who mapped it, its difficulty, its **Quality** and **Line Accuracy** stars, and has **Rate Trail**, **Navigate** and **Details**.

Turn **Rider Trails** off in the panel (in **Map Features** from 2.1) to hide them. The same choice is on the **You** tab as **Rider Trails on Maps**. They're on unless you turn them off.
:::

:::release 2.1
## Park Trails

The trails of offroad parks (Hidden Falls Adventure Park, Katemcy Rocks, Hollister Hills and about fifty more) draw on every map as **solid lines with a dark edge**, colored by the park's own level where it rates its trails, with the park's name from far out. The **Park Trails** row in the **Trails** group of Map Features turns them off; it's free for everyone. See [Offroad Park Trails](/help/park-trails).
:::

The map on the **Find a Ride** tab shows trail lines too when you zoom in, following the choice you made here.

## See Who Can Ride a Trail

1. Make sure **Public Trails and Roads** is on (from 2.1, the trail and road rows in **Map Features**) and you're zoomed in.
2. Tap a trail or road line. In the route builder, press and hold instead, since a tap adds a route point.
3. A card shows the trail's name, where it is, whether it's a trail, road or track, the segment's miles and surface when known.

Under **Open To**, the card lists the vehicles the agency allows. If access changes by season, it says **Open To, by Season** with the open dates. If the agency data doesn't say, the card tells you.

:::release 1.0.1
If the trail or road is closed today, a red box at the top of the card says so, for example **Closed for the Season** with the date it opens again, **Closed to Motor Vehicles** or **No Public Access**. On a seasonal trail, a vehicle whose season is over shows **Closed Now** next to its dates.
:::

For an OpenStreetMap track, the card says it was mapped by riders on OpenStreetMap, and that parks and private land need permission or a pass.

:::release 2.0
## Trail Width Limits

Some trails only fit narrow machines. When the card knows a trail's width limit, it shows it under the trail's name, for example **50" Width Limit**:

- **Forest Service trails** open only to ATVs and side-by-sides 50 inches or less show **50" Width Limit**, from the Forest Service's own vehicle rules.
- **Any public trail** (Forest Service, BLM or OpenStreetMap) can show a width other riders added. The card shows the middle of everyone's entries, so one wrong number doesn't change it, and says how many riders added one.

If you added widths to your machines in the [Garage](/help/garage), the card also says whether they fit, for example **Your RZR Is Too Wide (64")** in red or **Your Grizzly Fits (48")** in green.

### Add a Width Limit

Found a gate, a posted limit or a narrow gap? Add it so other riders know before they go.

1. Tap the trail line to open its card. You need to be signed in and have signal.
2. Tap **Add Width Limit**.
3. Type the narrowest width in inches (30 to 120) and tap **Save Width**.

Your width counts once per trail. To change it, tap **Change Your Width** on the same trail. To take it back, tap **Change Your Width**, then **Remove My Width**. OnMyLead can remove a width that's far off from what other riders found.

Trails other riders mapped show the width their mapper entered. See [Map Mode](/help/navigation-mode).
:::

:::warning
Map data can be out of date. Always check posted signs and closures before you ride.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
## Closed Trails and Roads

Closed trails and roads are drawn as red dashes on a dark outline, and the panel's legend shows **Trail**, **Road** and **Closed**. A line is marked closed when:

- **Forest Service**: the road is listed as closed to motor vehicles (red, labeled **CLOSED** along the line), or a seasonal road or trail is outside its open dates for every vehicle today (red, over the trail's normal line).
- **BLM**: the route's travel plan closes it to off-highway vehicles.
- **OpenStreetMap**: the track is mapped as closed or private.

Seasonal closures show once you zoom in to about a county's width, and need a signal to load. The other closures are part of the trail lines, so they're saved with a downloaded map.

:::warning
Closures come from the agencies' published travel plans and seasons and from OpenStreetMap. They are not live gate reports: a trail can also be closed for fire, snow, repairs or a local order that isn't in this data, and coverage outside Forest Service and BLM land depends on what riders have mapped. Always check posted signs and local orders before you ride.
:::
:::

## Download a Ride's Map

On a ride with a route, the panel has **Download This Ride's Map**. One tap saves satellite, topo and trails around the route for riding with no signal. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) and [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

The **Offline Maps** link at the bottom of the panel opens all your downloaded maps.

## With No Signal

When your phone loses signal, a **No Signal** tag with **Downloaded Map** appears under the layers button. The map then shows only what's saved on your phone, and the satellite view switches to downloaded USGS aerial photos. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

## On the Website

The website's route builder and waypoints map have the same layers button and map panel: **Satellite** or **Topo**, **Public Trails and Roads** (from 2.1, every **Map Features** row, including land), the trail and road names, and closed trails in red. The satellite map shows road names too. Zoomed in, the **Find a Ride** map shows the trail lines and names as well.

On the website, click a trail line to see its card when you're not adding points: on a route imported from a GPX file, for example. On the waypoints map a click adds a waypoint, so read the names on the map there. Downloading maps for no signal is only in the app.

## Map Data and Credits

- Trails and roads: USDA Forest Service MVUM and Forest Service roads, Bureau of Land Management, and map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, © OpenMapTiles, served by OpenFreeMap.
- Topo: USGS The National Map.
- Land (from 2.1): USGS PAD-US for national forests, BLM land and parks, and the Texas Geographic Information Office (StratMap land parcels) for Texas property lines.
- Hiking trails (from 2.1): USDA Forest Service trails.
- Satellite with no signal: USGS The National Map: Orthoimagery.

The credits for what's showing are listed at the bottom of the layers panel. Loading map squares only sends the area being looked at, never anything about you.

Music Controls let you pause, skip and turn the music up or down without switching apps, so the group map stays on your screen. They control the music already playing on your phone, from the app you play it in.

:::release 2.0
Music controls are a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, the music button carries a **Pro** tag. Your music app itself keeps playing as usual.
:::

## Open Music Controls

1. In **Ride Mode** or **Navigate**, tap the round **Music** button with the music note. It sits on the right, just above **Center on Me**.
2. The Music sheet shows what's playing and which app it's in, with big **Previous Song**, **Play** or **Pause** and **Next Song** buttons, and the volume with **−** and **+**.
3. Swipe the sheet down or tap **Close** to go back to the map.

In [Full Map](/help/full-map), the Music button sits in the bar at the bottom, between **Controls** and **EMERGENCY**.

The buttons are big enough to use with gloves on, but pull over before you look at your phone.

## What Works on Your Phone

| | Play, Pause and Skip | Volume |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Android phone or tablet** | Any music or podcast app: Spotify, YouTube Music, Apple Music, Pandora, Amazon Music and more | Yes |
| **iPhone or iPad** | Apple Music | Yes, for any app |
| **onmylead.com** | No | No |

**On iPhone and iPad,** Apple lets other apps control only Apple Music. When Spotify or another app is playing, the Music sheet says **Playing in Another App** and gives you the volume, plus **Open Spotify** if Spotify is on your phone (that leaves OnMyLead). Use the buttons on your headset or helmet communicator to skip. When nothing is playing, **Play** starts Apple Music.

**On Android,** the buttons control whichever app last played music. To see the song name and the app's name, tap **Show Song Names**, then switch on **OnMyLead Music Controls** under Notification Access in Settings. Android shares what's playing only with apps you allow there. OnMyLead doesn't read your notifications, and the buttons work without it.

**On iPhone,** tapping **Show Song Names** asks to let OnMyLead see the Apple Music song. If you said no before, it opens OnMyLead in Settings, where you can switch on **Media & Apple Music**.

## Hide the Music Button

Don't want it? Tap **Hide Music Button** at the bottom of the Music sheet, or go to the **You** tab and switch off **Music Controls**. The button disappears from Ride Mode and Navigate. Switch **Music Controls** back on in the **You** tab any time. The setting is kept on each phone or tablet separately.

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 you can also show or hide it from the map: tap the round **Map Settings** button, then switch **Music Button** under **Map Buttons**.
:::

:::note
What you listen to stays on your phone. OnMyLead doesn't send it to the server or show it to other riders.
:::
