:::until 2.0
**Navigate** is OnMyLead's offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. It has the same trails and roads as the rest of the app, shows where you are, and lets you record your own trails, keep them on your phone or share them with every rider. The map, following trails, measuring and rating trails are free. Recording, sharing your trails and planning group rides on them are part of [OnMyLead Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

:::release 2.0
On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold **Pro** tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags.
:::

## Open Navigate

- On Home, tap the **Navigate** card.
- Or on the **You** tab, tap **Navigate** under **On the Trail**.

At the top of the map are three tabs: **Explore**, **Record** and **Measure**. Swipe the panel down to see more of the map, and up to bring it back.
:::

:::release 2.0
**Map Mode** (called Navigate before version 2.0) is OnMyLead's offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. It has the same trails and roads as the rest of the app, shows where you are, and lets you map your own trails by drawing or recording them, keep them on your phone or share them with every rider. Free accounts get 8 hours of Map Mode a month, with the standard map and following trails. The clock never runs while you're sharing your location on a group ride, and Pro has no limit. Map layers, drawing, recording, saving, rating and sharing trails, Track Line, named spots and planning group rides on your trails are part of [OnMyLead Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

On a Free account, the top of Map Mode shows your time left, like **Free Map Mode: 5 h 20 m Left This Month**. The clock only runs while Map Mode is on your screen. When the month's time is used up, Map Mode offers **See OnMyLead Pro** and opens again at the start of the next month. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro#free-map-mode-time).

## Open Map Mode

- From any tab, tap the blue **Map Mode** button in the middle of the bar at the bottom of the screen. On a tablet, and on onmylead.com on a computer, it's in the menu down the left edge, under **Find**.
- On Home, tap **Open Map Mode** (or the little map) on the **Map Mode** card.
- To map a trail that isn't marked anywhere, tap **Map a Custom Trail** on the same card. Map Mode opens on the **Draw** tab.
- Or on the **You** tab, tap **Map Mode** under **On the Trail**.

At the bottom of the map are three tabs: **Explore**, **Record** and **Draw**. Swipe the panel down to see more of the map, and up to bring it back.

Map Mode opens on where you are, close enough to see the trails. If your phone is still finding your location (say, right after you turn it on), the map moves to you as soon as it does, unless you've already moved the map yourself.
:::

:::release 2.0
For the whole screen, tap **Full Map** on the panel's grab bar. A slim bar keeps your speed (or the miles left on a trail you're following, or the length you're measuring, with **Undo**), a red **Rec** while you record, and **Center on Me** stays. Tap **Controls**, or swipe the bar up, to bring everything back. See [Full Map](/help/full-map).
:::

:::tip
On a tablet, the panel sits beside the map in landscape, and floats over the corner of the map in portrait.
:::

## Explore

:::until 2.0
**Explore** shows your speed and elevation, with the map centered on you. Use the layers button for **Satellite** or **Topo** and trail lines (see [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers)), the search box to jump to a place, and the round **Center on Me** button to center on you again. Tap any line to see what it is.
:::

:::until 2.1
**Explore** shows your speed big on the left, with the map centered on you. Use the layers button for **Satellite** or **Topo** and trail lines (see [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers)), the search box to jump to a place, and the round **Center on Me** button to center on you again. Tap any line to see what it is.
:::

:::release 2.1
**Explore** shows your speed big on the left, with the map centered on you. Use the round **Map Settings** button for **Satellite** or **Topo** and trail lines (see [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers)), the search box to jump to a place, and the round **Center on Me** button to center on you again. Tap any line to see what it is.
:::

:::release 2.0

Next to your speed are four readings:

- **Elevation**, in feet.
- **Heading**, the way you're facing, such as **NE 62°**. While you're moving it comes from GPS. When you stop, it comes from your phone's compass. The website shows it only while you're moving.
- **Trip**, the miles you've covered since you last reset it, like the trip meter on a dash.
- **Moving**, how long you've been moving on this trip (minutes, then hours and minutes).

To start a new trip, press and hold **Trip**. Trip and Moving only count while Map Mode is open, and they're kept on your phone only. When you follow a trail, the big number shows the miles left, and **Speed** moves into the readings in place of **Moving**.
:::

:::release 2.0
Under the readings, the **Tilt** tile shows your **Roll** and **Pitch**, turning amber, then red, near your limits. Until you calibrate the tilt meter it says **Calibrate Tilt**. Tap it for the full tilt meter. See [Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert](/help/tilt-and-crash-alert).
:::

### The Map Follows You

:::until 2.0
While you record a trail, or follow a trail you're on or near, the map moves with you so your dot stays in view. Tapping **Center on Me** also makes the map follow you. The button turns white while the map is following.

To look around, drag or pinch the map. It stops following until you tap **Center on Me** again. The map also holds still while the **Measure** tab is open, and when you jump to a place with search.
:::

:::release 2.0
With **Follow Me** on (it is unless you turn it off), the map moves with you so your dot stays in view, and while you're moving your dot has a white arrow pointing the way you're heading. The **Follow Me** button sits just left of **Center on Me** and shows **Following**.

To look around, drag or pinch the map. It pauses (the button shows **Paused**) until you tap it or **Center on Me** again. The map also holds still while the **Measure** tab is open, and when you jump to a place with search. Tap **Following** to turn Follow Me off; the map then stays where you put it, even while you record. See [Follow Me on the Map](/help/follow-me).
:::

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 the map zooms out one step the first time your dot nears an edge, then the next time centers on your dot and moves with you so it stays on screen, and zooms in as you come up on a junction of roads or trails, then back out once you're through. Your own dot (Red, White and Blue unless you pick another Dot Style in Map Settings) has its arrow built in, and the arrow follows your phone's compass when you stop. Turn the junction zoom off with **Zoom In at Intersections** in the **You** tab.
:::

The screen stays on while Navigate is open.

:::release 2.0
:::release 2.1
From 2.1 Map Mode's map is drawn by Mapbox on every device and on onmylead.com, so it looks the same everywhere, and a trail's page shows the trail on a real map (your map look, with the trails around it) instead of a line drawing. Pick **3D Terrain** under **Map Style** to explore on the real shape of the land, with contour lines and peak heights. Recording, Track Line and the distance finder work the same in 3D. See [3D Terrain](/help/3d-terrain).
:::

:::release 2.1
### Drop a Waypoint

Press and hold the map to drop a waypoint there (right-click on onmylead.com). Tapping the map still shows what a trail is. Your Map Mode waypoints are yours alone and stay on your phone with no signal; with Sync they follow you to your other devices. If you're sharing your location with a live group ride, the waypoint goes on that ride instead, and the leader's are shared with the group. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops#press-and-hold-the-map).
:::

## Track Line

**Track Line** draws exactly where you've been, in a different color each day, so today's line is easy to tell from yesterday's: today is red, yesterday blue, and older days gold and other colors. It keeps the last 7 days.

:::release 2.0
Track Line is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, the **Track Line** switch carries a **Pro** tag.
:::

1. Turn on **Track Line** on Home's **Map Mode** card, or at the bottom of the **Explore** tab.
2. Ride. Your line is drawn on the map while Map Mode is open, and also while you share your location on a group ride.
3. To delete every day of it, tap **Clear** next to the colors, then **Clear**.

Track Line is kept on this phone only. It is never shared or sent to OnMyLead. It isn't a recording: to keep a trail, record or draw it.
:::

### Follow a Trail

1. Open a trail from **My Trails**, or tap a rider trail on the map.
2. Tap **Follow in Navigate** (your trails) or **Navigate** (rider trails).
3. The trail is drawn on the map, and the panel shows the distance **Left on Trail**, or how far you are from its start. Tap **Stop** to stop following.

:::release 2.0
From version 2.0, the button on your own trails is **Follow in Map Mode**.
:::

## Record a Trail

This is in the OnMyLead app on your phone or tablet. The website can't record.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

1. Tap the **Record** tab, then **Record a Trail**.
2. Ride. Your line is drawn on the map with its distance, time and climb.
3. Tap **Pause** for a break and **Resume** to carry on.
4. Tap **Finish and Save** when you're done. Or tap **Discard Recording** to throw it away.

Keep Navigate open while you record: the screen stays on, and recording stops if you leave Navigate or lock the phone. If the app closes, the recording is still there when you open Navigate again.

:::release 2.0
### Name a Spot While You Record

Tap **Mark a Spot Here** to name the place you're at, like a ledge, a water crossing or a viewpoint. Pick **Obstacle**, **Hazard**, **Water Crossing** or **Viewpoint**, type a name (up to 40 letters) and tap **Add to Trail**. The spot is saved with the trail.
:::

:::until 2.0
## Measure a Distance

1. Tap the **Measure** tab.
2. Tap the map where you want to measure from, then where you want to measure to. On the website, click.
3. Pick **Follow Trails** to measure along the trails and roads, or **Straight Line** for the distance as the crow flies.
4. Keep tapping to add points. **Undo** removes the last one, **Clear** starts over.
5. Tap **Save as Trail** to keep the line in My Trails, so you can follow it or plan a ride on it.
:::

:::release 2.0
## Map a Custom Trail or Measure a Distance

The **Draw** tab maps a trail that isn't marked on any map, and measures distances.

Map a Custom Trail, **Mark a Spot** and **Save Trail** are Pro features. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, the **Draw** tab and those buttons carry a **Pro** tag.

The first time you open it, **How Custom Trails Work** explains how custom trails stay private, how sharing and ratings work, and when a shared trail comes down. Tick **Don't show this again** to skip it next time, then tap **Start Mapping**.

1. Tap the **Draw** tab (or **Map a Custom Trail** on Home).
2. Tap the map where the trail starts, then along it. On the website, click.
3. Pick **Follow Trails** to snap along trails and roads on the map, or **Straight Line** for a trail that isn't marked anywhere.
4. Keep tapping to add points. **Undo** removes the last one, **Clear** starts over. The panel shows the length.
5. To name a spot, tap **Mark a Spot**, then tap the spot on the map. Pick a kind, type a name and tap **Add to Trail**. Tap a spot's name on the map to rename or remove it.
6. Tap **Save Trail** to keep it in My Trails as a custom trail, so you can follow it, share it or plan a ride on it.
:::

## My Trails

Tap **My Trails** in Explore (or the trail chip on the map) to see every trail on this phone: ones you recorded, drew, or saved from other riders. Tap a trail to open it.

On a trail you can:

- Name it and add details: **Difficulty** (Easy, Moderate, Hard or Extreme), **Vehicles That Fit**, **Surface**, **Season**, **Width Limit (Inches, Optional)** for the narrowest gate or gap, **One Way** and notes.
- Add up to 6 photos. Press and hold a photo to remove it.
- See its distance, climb, high point and, for a recording, moving time.
- **Follow in Navigate**, **Plan a Group Ride on This Trail** or **Delete Trail**.

:::release 2.0
- See its **Named Spots**. Tap one to rename it, change its kind or **Remove** it, then tap **Save Changes** (or **Save on This Phone**).
:::

:::until 2.0
Trails stay on your phone until you share them. Deleting the app deletes them too.
:::

:::release 2.0
Your trails are backed up privately to your account, so they're in My Trails on every device you sign in on, and deleting the app doesn't lose them. Nobody else sees them until you share them. See [Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device](/help/sync-across-devices).
:::

## Share a Trail With Every Rider

Sharing is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

1. Open the trail in My Trails.
2. Give it a name, a difficulty and at least one vehicle type. Other details are optional but help other riders.
3. Tap **Share with Everyone** and confirm.

:::until 2.0
Shared trails show your ride name as the mapper, with the trail's photos and details. To keep where you start and finish private, the first and last 200 meters (about 650 feet) of a shared trail are left off. A trail too short for that can't be shared.
:::

:::release 2.0
Shared trails show in full, end to end, with your ride name as the mapper, the trail's photos, details and named spots.

If you recorded a trail that starts at your house or camp, turn on **Hide My Start** on the trail before you share it. The first and last 200 meters (about 650 feet) are then left off, along with any named spots on them. It's off unless you turn it on, and drawn trails always share in full. A trail has to be at least 200 meters long to share, or longer with Hide My Start.
:::

If your Pro ends, trails you already shared stay up and you can still edit them or stop sharing.

To take it back, tap **Stop Sharing**. The trail comes off the public map and its ratings are removed. It stays on your phone.

You need to be signed in to share. Sharing trails also counts toward the **Trailblazer** badge. See [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks).

## Delete a Trail

Only the rider who mapped a trail can delete it.

1. Open the trail in **My Trails**.
2. Tap **Delete Trail**, then **Delete**.

The trail is deleted from your phone. If you shared it, it also comes off the public map with its photos and ratings. If that can't happen (with no signal, for example), the app says so and keeps the trail, so try again with a signal.

:::release 2.0
It's deleted from your backup and your other devices too, the next time each one syncs.
:::

On a trail you shared, the trail's page also has **Delete Your Trail**. It takes the trail off the public map and keeps the copy on this phone in My Trails.

Group rides that already used the trail as their route keep their route.

## Rider Trails on the Map

Trails other riders shared are called rider trails. They're drawn as **mint dotted lines**, so they stand out from the agency and OpenStreetMap trails. They show in Navigate (Map Mode from 2.0) and on the other maps with trail lines once you zoom in, when you're signed in.

Tap one to see its card. It says **User Submitted Trail**, who mapped it, the difficulty, distance, its **Quality** and **Line Accuracy** stars, and buttons to rate it, navigate it or see the details. The details page adds the vehicles, notes, photos and **Save to My Trails**.

:::release 2.0
If the mapper entered a width limit, the card and details page show it (**Width Limit**). With widths on your machines in the [Garage](/help/garage), they also say whether your machine fits or is too wide.
:::

:::release 2.0
When you follow a rider trail, the spots its mapper named show on the map with their names.
:::

### Hide Rider Trails

On the **You** tab, under **On the Trail**, turn off **Rider Trails on Maps**. You can also turn off **Rider Trails** in the map's layers panel. They're on unless you turn them off.

## Rate a Rider Trail

:::release 2.0
Rating trails is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Seeing a trail's ratings stays free.
:::


1. Tap a rider trail, then **Rate Trail** (or **Rate This Trail** on its page).
2. Give the trail's **Quality** from 1 to 5 stars: is it worth riding?
3. If you rode it, rate how accurate the line is under **Rode It? How Accurate Is the Line?**
4. Add a note for the mapper if you like, then tap **Save Rating**.

You can change your rating later. You can't rate your own trails. After you follow a rider trail for a while, Navigate asks you to rate it.

### When Riders Rate a Trail as Inaccurate

If several riders rate a trail's line 2 stars or fewer for accuracy, it's hidden from everyone else's map. Right now that's 3 riders, who make up at least half of its accuracy ratings. The mapper keeps the trail on their phone and gets a notification, and My Trails shows it as hidden. OnMyLead can also put a trail back or take one down.

:::warning
Rider trails are mapped by riders, not by a land agency. Always check posted signs, closures and land access before you ride.
:::

## Use a Trail for a Group Ride

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

- On a trail, tap **Plan a Group Ride on This Trail**. The new ride uses the trail as its route and its start as the meeting point.
- On a ride's route, tap **Use One of My Trails** and pick a trail.

See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride) and [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).

:::release 2.0
## Control Your Music

The round **Music** button above **Center on Me** pauses, skips and changes the volume of the music on your phone. See [Control Your Music While You Ride](/help/music-controls).
:::

## On the Website

:::until 2.0
On onmylead.com, Navigate has Explore, Measure and My Trails (kept in that browser). Sign in to see, share and rate rider trails. Recording a trail is only in the app.
:::

:::release 2.0
On onmylead.com, Map Mode has Explore, Draw, Track Line and My Trails (kept in that browser). Sign in to see, share and rate rider trails. Recording a trail is only in the app.
:::

You decide what OnMyLead tells you about. Every change saves as soon as you make it, and your choices apply on any device you sign in on.

## Open Notification Settings

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Settings**, tap **Notifications**. The line under it sums up your settings, like **Everything on** or **2 turned off**.

:::release 2.0
You can also tap the bell at the top of the **Rides** tab, then **Notification Settings** at the bottom of the list.
:::

## Always On: Help and EMERGENCY

When someone in your group taps **Need Help** or **EMERGENCY**, you're always told, even during quiet hours. This can't be turned off.

:::release 2.1
**Emergency Siren**, just below, starts on: an EMERGENCY from your group sounds a loud siren until you silence it. Tap **Play Siren** to hear it, or switch it off to get EMERGENCY notifications with the normal sound. See [Hear the Emergency Siren](/help/emergency-siren).
:::

## What You Can Turn On or Off

Everything below starts on.

### On the Trail

- **Rider Status**: status buttons and quick replies from Ride Mode, like **On My Way**, **Need Fuel** and **Flat Tire**, and when a rider cancels one.
- **Announcements**: what the organizer tells the whole group.
:::release 2.1
- **Announcements** also cover new waypoints the leader shares while the ride is live. See [New Waypoint Alerts](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops#new-waypoint-alerts).
:::

:::release 2.0
Messages riders type in Ride Mode with **✎ Message** follow the **Rider Status** setting too.
:::

### Ride Chat

- **Group Chat**: messages and quick replies from your group.
- **Messages to the Leader**: leader-only messages, when you're leading.
- **Show Message Text**: turn this off to keep messages off your lock screen. You'll see who wrote, not what.

### Before the Ride

- **Ride Changes**: a ride starts, is cancelled, or gets a new time or meeting spot, or you get a spot or a role.
- **New Riders**: someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize.
- **Email When a Ride Is Cancelled**: an email as well as the notification if a ride you joined is cancelled or removed.

### Your Riding Groups

- **Ride Invites**: someone invites you, or a group you're in, to a ride.
- **Riding Group Chat**: new messages in your riding groups' chats. To mute just one group, do it from that group's chat. See [Group Chat](/help/group-chat).
- **Leaders You Follow**: a leader you follow posts a new public ride.

:::release 1.0.3
- **Direct Messages**: a rider messages you, say after seeing you Out Riding. To mute one conversation, do it from inside it. See [See Who's Out Riding Nearby](/help/out-riding).
- **Friend Requests**: a rider asks to be your friend, or accepts your request. See [Add Friends](/help/friends).
:::
:::release 2.0
- **Likes and Comments**: a rider likes or comments on your post, ride, badge or trail, or replies after you comment. Likes on one post come at most once every 15 minutes. See [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social).
:::
:::release 2.1
- **Likes and Comments** also covers a rider liking or replying to your comment. Likes on one comment come at most once every 15 minutes too.
:::

### Your Account

:::until 1.0.3
- **Pro Trial Reminders**: a week, 3 days and a day before your Pro Trial ends, and when it does.
:::
:::release 1.0.3
- **Badges and Pro Trial**: when you earn a badge (see [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks)), and a week, 3 days and a day before your Pro Trial ends. It also tells you when a trail you shared is hidden from the public map (see [Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails](/help/navigation-mode)).
:::
- **Email Me Too**: the same Pro Trial reminders by email.

## Tapping a Notification

Tapping a notification takes you straight to what it's about, whether OnMyLead was open, in the background or closed:

- A status tap like **Need Help**, a quick reply, or a ride going live opens **Ride Mode** for that ride.
- A ride chat message opens the ride's **Chat**.
- A riding group message opens that group's chat.
- Ride changes, new riders, invites and reminders open the ride.
:::release 1.0.3
- A new badge opens **Badges**.
- A direct message opens the conversation.
- A friend request, or a request someone accepted, opens **Friends**.
- A trail of yours being hidden opens **My Trails**.
:::
:::release 2.0
- A like or a comment opens that post with all its comments.
:::

:::release 2.0
Notifications you've missed or swiped away are kept under the bell on the **Rides** tab for 30 days. See [See and Clear Your Notifications](/help/notifications-inbox).
:::

## Ride Reminder

Get a heads-up before each ride you've joined, with the meeting spot. Under **Ride reminder**, pick **Off**, **30 Min**, **1 Hour**, **2 Hours** or **Day Before**. It starts at **1 Hour**.

## Quiet Hours

1. Under **Quiet hours**, turn on **Silence Overnight**.
2. Use the minus and plus buttons under **From** and **Until** to set the times. Each tap moves the time by half an hour.

During quiet hours everything is held except help alerts. Until you change them, quiet hours run from 10 PM to 6 AM.

## If Notifications Aren't Arriving

- If you see **Notifications Are Off for OnMyLead**, your iPhone is blocking them. Tap **Open iPhone Settings** and turn on **Allow Notifications**.

On Android, the button is **Open Settings**. Android also sorts OnMyLead's notifications into three categories you can tune in **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Notifications**: **Rider Alerts** (Need Help, EMERGENCY and other status taps, shown at the highest priority), **Ride Chat** (ride and group chat) and **Ride Updates** (ride changes, new riders, invites, reminders and account notices).
- If you see **Let OnMyLead Send Notifications**, tap **Turn On Notifications** and allow them.
- While OnMyLead is open, new ride chat messages pop up inside the app instead of as a banner.

## On the Website

You can change these settings at onmylead.com too. Notifications themselves come to the app on your phone or tablet.

articles.summary: The bell on the Rides tab lists the notifications OnMyLead sent you in the last 30 days. Open them, mark them read, or clear one or all.
articles.text:
---
title: See and Clear Your Notifications
summary: The bell on the Rides tab lists the notifications OnMyLead sent you in the last 30 days. Open them, mark them read, or clear one or all.
category: account
order: 25
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:

  - app/src/components/inbox-bell.tsx
  - app/src/core/inbox.ts
  - app/src/lib/inbox.ts
  - app/src/lib/notification-tray.ts
  - app/src/lib/notification-tray.web.ts
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx
  - supabase/migrations/20261102100000_notification_inbox.sql
related: [notification-settings, ride-chat, status-buttons, friends, emergency-and-safety]
keywords: [notifications, inbox, bell, alerts, clear, dismiss, badge, unread, mark read, history, missed]
---

Missed a notification, or swiped one away too soon? OnMyLead keeps the ones it sent you, so you can find them again and clear them when you're done.

## Open Your Notifications

Tap the bell at the top right of the **Rides** tab. A red number on the bell shows how many are new.

Notifications are listed newest first under **Today**, **Yesterday** and **Earlier**. Each one has a colored icon, so a rider alert like **Need Help** stands out from chat and ride changes. New ones have a dot.

Several messages from the same chat are kept together in one line, with **+2 More** (or however many) under the latest message, so a busy chat doesn't bury anything else.

## Open One

Tap a notification to go straight to what it's about, the same as tapping it on your lock screen: Ride Mode for a rider's status or a ride going live, the ride's chat for a message, Friends for a friend request, and so on. It's marked read.

:::release 2.1
A new waypoint from the leader opens Ride Mode with that waypoint showing.
:::

To mark everything read without opening it, tap **Mark All Read**.

## Clear Notifications

- **Clear one**: swipe it to the left and tap **Clear**, or swipe all the way to clear it straight away. On onmylead.com, click the **X** on the right of the notification.
- **Clear all**: tap **Clear All** at the top, then **Clear All** again to confirm.

Clearing in OnMyLead also clears the same notifications from your phone or tablet's own notification list, and Clear All resets the number on the OnMyLead app icon.

## What's Kept

- Every notification OnMyLead sent you: ride chat, announcements, status buttons, ride changes, new riders, invites, riding group chat, direct messages, friend requests, badges and Pro Trial reminders.
- What you turned off in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings) isn't sent, so it isn't kept either. The same goes for quiet hours (except help alerts) and riders you blocked.
- If a rider cancels a status like **Need Help**, the cancellation replaces it. If someone deletes a chat message, it's removed here too.
- Notifications are kept for 30 days, up to the 100 newest.
- Ride reminders are set on your phone itself, so they don't appear in the list.

Your notifications are private to you, and they're the same on every device you sign in on.

## On the Website

The bell is on the Rides page at onmylead.com too, with the same list. It shows the notifications OnMyLead sent to the app on your phone or tablet, so if you haven't allowed notifications in the app, the list stays empty.

## Notification Settings

To choose what you're told about, tap **Notification Settings** at the bottom of the list. See [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

articles.summary: Download a ride's map or any area before you leave, so the map and route are still there when the signal drops. A Pro feature.
articles.text:
---
title: Offline Maps
summary: Download a ride's map or any area before you leave, so the map and route are still there when the signal drops. A Pro feature.
category: routes-maps
order: 60
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/maps/index.tsx
  - app/src/app/maps/area.tsx
  - app/src/components/offline-map-ui.tsx
  - app/src/components/area-picker-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/area-picker-map.web.tsx
  - app/src/components/trail-map-overlay.tsx
  - app/src/components/trail-tiles.tsx

related: [sync-across-devices, map-layers, free-vs-pro, ride-mode, route-builder, troubleshooting]
keywords: [offline, no signal, no service, download map, save map, dead zone, backcountry, storage, delete map, topo offline, satellite offline, tablet]
---

Out on the trail the signal often drops. Download a map before you leave and the map keeps working with no signal: satellite photos, topo and trail lines for the area you saved.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Maps already on your phone keep working on the Free plan.

:::release 2.0
On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold **Pro** tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags.
:::

:::warning
Offline maps keep the map, not the tracking. With no signal, your phone can't send or receive positions. Riders show where they were last seen, and positions update again when phones get a connection.
:::

Offline maps are in the app on your phone or tablet only, not on the website.

## Open Offline Maps

- On the **You** tab, tap **Offline Maps**.
- Or, on any map with the layers button, open the layers panel and tap **Offline Maps**.

The screen shows how much space your maps use, how much is free on your phone, your downloads under **On This Phone**, and your upcoming rides under **Your Rides**.

:::release 2.0
Areas you downloaded on your other devices (signed in with the same account) show under **On Your Other Devices**. Tap **Download** to save the same area here, or **Hide** to stop seeing it. See [Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device](/help/sync-across-devices).
:::

## Download a Ride's Map

The quickest way. It saves satellite, topo and trails around the ride's route.

:::release 2.1
If your map style is 3D Terrain, **Download This Ride's Map** on the ride's map saves 3D Terrain too. The ride list on Offline Maps saves the flat maps only; use **Download a Map Area** to add 3D Terrain there.
:::

From Offline Maps:

1. Under **Your Rides**, find the ride. Each one shows about how much space it needs.
2. Tap **Download**.

From the ride's map:

:::until 2.1
1. Open Ride Mode or the ride's waypoints map.
2. Tap the layers button.
3. Tap **Download This Ride's Map**.
:::

:::release 2.1
1. Open Ride Mode or the ride's waypoints map.
2. Tap the round **Map Settings** button.
3. Tap **Download This Ride's Map**.
:::

**Your Rides** lists upcoming rides you've joined that have a mapped route. Downloading a ride again replaces its earlier download, which is handy if the route changed.

## Download Any Area

1. On Offline Maps, tap **Download a Map Area**.
2. Move and zoom the map until the frame holds the area you'll ride. The frame's size in miles shows in its corner.
3. Pick the maps to save: **Satellite**, **Topo** and **Trails**. All three are on to start.
:::release 2.1
   You can also pick **3D Terrain** so the 3D map works there with no signal. It's a bigger download (a 20-mile-square area is roughly 150 MB more), so it's only ticked to start if your map style is 3D Terrain.
:::
4. Check the estimate under the choices.
5. Tap **Download This Area**.

The download is named after the nearest town when your phone can find one.

If you see **Too big for one download. Zoom in a little.**, the area is too large to save with enough detail to ride by. Zoom in, or save it as two downloads.

## Watch and Manage Downloads

Each download on **On This Phone** shows its maps, its size and how it's going.

- **Pause** stops a download for now.
- **Resume** carries on from where it stopped.
- **Finish** appears when some pieces didn't download. The download shows how many are missing; tap **Finish** to try them again.
- **Delete** takes it off your phone. Tap **Delete** again to confirm, or **Keep**.

One download runs at a time. If you close the app during a download, it's paused; open Offline Maps and tap **Resume**.

Deleting a download only removes pieces that no other download also uses, so overlapping maps keep working.

## When the Signal Drops

You don't need to do anything. The app checks for a connection while a map is open. When it can't reach the internet:

- A **No Signal** tag with **Downloaded Map** appears under the layers button.
- The map shows what's saved on your phone. Zoomed in past what you saved, it stretches the closest saved detail.
- The satellite view switches to USGS aerial photos from your download, since the live satellite view can't be saved ahead of time.

The ride's route and waypoints are saved on your phone once you've opened the ride, so they're still on the map too.

:::tip
Download before you leave, while you have good signal. Then open the ride once so its route is on your phone.
:::

## What Gets Saved

- **Satellite**: USGS aerial photos.
- **Topo**: the USGS topo map.
- **Trails**: Forest Service and BLM lines, plus OpenStreetMap tracks (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors).

:::release 2.1
- **3D Terrain**: Mapbox's satellite photos, land height, contour lines and names, saved by Mapbox inside the app. While it saves, the download shows **Saving 3D Terrain** and how far along it is. With no signal, the Satellite and 3D Terrain styles show Mapbox's map only over an area with 3D Terrain saved; anywhere else, and in the Topo style, the app shows the flat downloaded map (USGS photos, topo and trails), so you always have a map.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
The Forest Service's closed roads are saved too, so closed lines still show red with no signal. Seasonal closures need a signal to load.

:::release 2.1
**Trails** also saves the Forest Service's hiking trails. With no signal, a downloaded map shows every saved trail line whatever you picked in **Map Features**, since the lines are saved together. Land boundaries (national forests, BLM land, parks and property lines) aren't saved yet; they show when you have signal. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).
:::
:::

Trail and topo areas you've already looked at with signal are also kept on your phone for a while, but only a download makes sure the whole area is there.

## If Your Pro Plan Ends

Maps you already downloaded stay on your phone and keep working. Starting a new download needs Pro.

articles.title: Organizer Controls
articles.summary: Everything you can do as a ride's organizer, from starting Ride Mode and approving riders to ending the ride for everyone.
articles.text:
---
title: Organizer Controls
summary: Everything you can do as a ride's organizer, from starting Ride Mode and approving riders to ending the ride for everyone.
category: rides
order: 40
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

  - app/src/app/e/[code].tsx

related: [leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner, approvals-and-waitlist, edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride, ride-mode, invite-riders, ride-chat]
keywords: [organizer, host, run a ride, start ride, end ride, manage riders, approve, announcement, admin of ride, tablet]
---

When you create a ride, you're its organizer. You're also its leader until you hand that job to someone else. Here's what you can do from your ride page.

## Before the Ride

- **Invite riders.** Share the link, code or QR code, or invite a whole riding group. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders).
- **Approve requests.** If riders asked to join, the **Riders** section shows a red count and a **Waiting for You** list with **Approve** and **Decline**. See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist).
- **Build or edit the route** and add planned stops in the **Map** section. See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder).
- **Pick a leader and a tail gunner** from the roster in **Riders**. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).
- **Post announcements** in the ride chat. Your latest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page for everyone on the ride. See [Ride Chat](/help/ride-chat).

You get a notification when someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize. You can turn these off in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Start the Ride

1. Open the ride page.
2. Tap **Start Ride Mode**.

The ride goes live, riders on it get a notification that it started, and Ride Mode opens for you. Everyone else on the ride sees **Enter Ride Mode** on the ride page, and a banner on their **Rides** tab. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

## End the Ride

When everyone is off the trail:

1. Open the ride page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card on **Details**, tap **End Ride for Everyone**.

Ending the ride stops everyone's location sharing for this ride. Riders then see their ride summary on the ride page. See [Ride Summary and Ride Again](/help/ride-summary-and-ride-again).

:::warning
A live ride doesn't end by itself. Remember to tap **End Ride for Everyone** when you're done, so location sharing for the ride stops.
:::

## Hand Off the Whole Ride

If you can't make it, give the ride to another rider who has joined. Open **Riders**, tap their name and tap **Give Them the Ride**. They become the organizer and leader, and you stay on the ride as a rider. You can't undo this yourself. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

:::release 2.0
Or tap **Leave Ride** at the bottom of the ride page: pick who takes over under **Who Takes Over?** and tap **Give Ride and Leave**. They run the ride and you're off it.
:::

:::release 2.1
## Change the Details

Tap **Edit Ride Details** in the **You're Organizing** card to change the name, day, time, meeting point and the rest. Riders hear about a new time or meeting point. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).
:::

## Call It Off

Use **Cancel Ride** or **Delete Ride** in the **You're Organizing** card. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).

## Run It Again

Tap **Copy This Ride** (or **Ride Again** after it ends) to start a new ride with the same details and route. See [Ride Summary and Ride Again](/help/ride-summary-and-ride-again).

:::note
As the organizer you can't leave your own ride. Hand it to another rider first if you need to step away.
:::

:::release 2.0
## Ride Managers for Event Rides

When a ride is one of an event's group rides, an event host who organizes the ride can pick a **Ride Manager** on the event's page. The Ride Manager becomes a **Co-Organizer** of the ride (after joining it, if they weren't on it). See [Events](/help/events).
:::

articles.title: See Who's Out Riding Nearby
articles.summary: Switch on Out Riding to see which riders are out near you right now, roughly how far away they are, and send them a message.
articles.text:
---
title: See Who's Out Riding Nearby
summary: Switch on Out Riding to see which riders are out near you right now, roughly how far away they are, and send them a message.
category: groups
order: 25
release: "1.0.3"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/app/out-riding.tsx
  - app/src/app/messages/index.tsx
  - app/src/app/messages/[id].tsx
  - app/src/components/out-riding-card.tsx
  - app/src/components/range-rings.tsx
  - app/src/core/out-riding.ts
  - app/src/lib/out-riding.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-direct-chat.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261101700000_out_riding.sql
related: [riding-groups, report-and-block, privacy, notification-settings, location-sharing]
keywords: [online, nearby, who's riding, friends nearby, out riding, park, weekend, direct message, dm, message a rider, inbox, messages, tablet]
---

Heading to a park for the weekend, or just out on the trail? Switch on **Out Riding** and OnMyLead shows you which other riders are out near you right now, like friends showing online in a game. You can message any of them.

Out Riding is off until you switch it on, and other riders never see where you are. They see your ride name and roughly how far away you are, in whole miles.

## Switch On Out Riding

1. Go to the **Groups** tab and tap **Out Riding** at the top.
2. Under **Who Can See Me**, pick one:
   - **Riders I Know**: only your [friends](/help/friends), and riders you've been on a ride with or share a riding group with. This is the default.
   - **Everyone Nearby**: also any other OnMyLead rider who is Out Riding near you and picked **Everyone Nearby** too.
3. Under **Turn Off After**, pick **4 Hours**, **Today** or **This Weekend**.
4. If you like, type where you're riding under **Where You're Riding (Optional)**, like the park's name. Riders who can see you see it.
5. Tap **Go Out Riding**. Allow location if your phone asks.

The **Out Riding** card on the Groups tab turns green and shows who's out within 10 miles.

:::note
OnMyLead only uses your location while the app is open to work out your rough area, and it keeps an area of about a mile, never your exact spot. Out Riding doesn't share your live location. For that, see [Location Sharing](/help/location-sharing).
:::

## See Who's Out Near You

While you're Out Riding, the **Out Near You** list shows each rider with roughly how far away they are (like **Under a Mile** or **About 6 Miles**), where they said they're riding, and whether they're your friend or you've ridden with them. Friends are listed first.

- Tap **10 Mi**, **25 Mi** or **50 Mi** to look farther.
- If you picked **Everyone Nearby**, switch between **Riders I Know** and **Everyone Nearby** to see only your riders or everyone.
- The rings at the top show the same riders by distance. They never show which way anyone is. Riders you know are green.

You only see other riders while you're Out Riding yourself, and you only see riders outside your own riders while they can see you too.

## Message a Rider

1. In the list, tap the blue message button next to a rider (or tap their dot on the rings).
2. Type your message and tap send.

Only the two of you see the conversation. You can start one with a friend, a rider you see Out Riding near you, or a rider you've ridden with. Until they reply, you can send up to 3 messages.

Find all your conversations under **Messages** on the Groups tab or the Out Riding screen. In a conversation:

- **Mute** stops notifications for that conversation.
- **•••** opens **Add Friend**, **Report Rider**, **Block Rider** and **Delete Conversation**. Deleting removes it from your Messages only; the other rider keeps their copy.
- Long press one of their messages to report it. The message goes with your report.

:::tip
Meeting up with someone new? Meet at a trailhead or staging area.
:::

## Add a Rider as a Friend

In the list, tap **•••** next to a rider, then **Add Friend**. Once they accept, they see you whenever you're both Out Riding with **Riders I Know**, and you can message each other any time. See [Add Friends](/help/friends).

## Change or Turn It Off

1. Open **Out Riding** from the Groups tab.
2. Tap **Change** to switch who can see you or where you're riding, or **Turn Off** to stop.

Out Riding also turns itself off at the time you picked, or after 6 hours without opening OnMyLead. Opening the app while it's on updates your rough area.

## Blocking

If you block a rider, neither of you sees the other in Out Riding, their messages are hidden from you, and they can't message you. They aren't told. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## On a Tablet

On a tablet in landscape, or a wide window, your Out Riding status is on the left and the rings and list are on the right. Conversations sit in a readable column in the middle of the screen.

articles.title: Offroad Park Trails
articles.summary: Every map shows the trails of offroad parks like Hidden Falls, colored by the park's own levels and named, so you know a park before you ride it.
articles.text:
---
title: Offroad Park Trails
summary: Every map shows the trails of offroad parks like Hidden Falls, colored by the park's own levels and named, so you know a park before you ride it.
category: routes-maps
order: 55
release: "2.1"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/core/park-trails.ts
  - app/src/lib/park-trails.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-trail-map.ts
  - app/src/components/trail-map-overlay.tsx
  - app/src/components/trail-tiles.tsx
  - app/src/components/mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/mapbox-map.web.tsx

  - app/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx
  - app/scripts/parks/parks.json
  - supabase/migrations/20261104180000_park_trails.sql
related: [map-layers, navigation-mode, find-a-ride, offline-maps, route-builder]
keywords: [park trails, offroad park, off-road park, ohv park, orv park, atv park, hidden falls, hidden falls adventure park, katemcy, hollister hills, svra, park map, trail levels, level 5, trail names, private park, openstreetmap]
---

OnMyLead draws the trails of offroad parks on every map: Ride Mode, Map Mode, the route builder, waypoints, Find a Ride and the maps on onmylead.com. Hidden Falls Adventure Park, Katemcy Rocks, Wolf Caves, General Sam's, Hollister Hills, Hungry Valley, Ocotillo Wells, Interlake, SMORR, Sand Mountain and about fifty more parks and OHV areas are in, with their trail names and, where the park rates its trails, the park's own levels.

## See a Park's Trails

1. Open any map and zoom in to about a county's width. Park trails draw as **solid lines with a dark edge**, so they don't look like the dashed amber agency trails or the mint dotted rider trails.
2. From farther out, each park's **name** sits on the map with how many trails and miles are mapped (trails only, not the park's roads), so you can see where the parks are while you pan across the state.
3. Zoom in closer and the trail **names** appear along the lines.

Park trails show for everyone, signed in or not, and they're on unless you turn them off.

## What the Colors Mean

Where a park rates its trails (Hidden Falls does, level 1 to 5), the line takes the color of that level, the same colors as trailhead signs and rider trails:

- **Green**: level 1 and 2, the easiest.
- **Blue**: level 3.
- **White**: level 4.
- **Red**: level 5, the hardest.
- **Amber**: a trail the park hasn't rated.
- **Thin white**: a park road.
- **Red dashes**: a trail the park has closed.

The key is in **Map Settings**: tap **Fine-Tune** under **Every Map Feature**, and the **Park Trails** row in the **Trails** group shows the four level colors.

## Tap a Trail

Tap a park trail to see its card: the park's name, the trail's name, its level (or **Park Road** / **Trail** when it has none), its length, and whether it's one way. The card reminds you that levels and lines come from OpenStreetMap, the open map that riders and parks contribute to, so check the park's posted map too: trails change after storms and work days, and a park may re-rate a trail before the map catches up.

## Turn Park Trails Off

Tap the round **Map Settings** button on any map, tap **Fine-Tune** under **Every Map Feature**, then tap the **Park Trails** row in the **Trails** group to turn it off. The same choice is on the **You** tab as **Park Trails on Maps**. Either one changes every map, on every device you're signed in on. Park Trails is free for everyone, like Rider Trails, so it stays even without Pro.

## With No Signal

A park you've looked at while connected stays on your phone, so its trails draw again at the park with no service. Parks you've never opened need a signal the first time.

## Where the Trails Come From

Park trails are OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors), published under the Open Database License, which allows OnMyLead to show them with that credit. OnMyLead never copies a park's own copyrighted map. A park that isn't on the map yet simply isn't mapped in OpenStreetMap; anyone, including the park, can add its trails there and they'll come into OnMyLead with the next park update.

If a line is wrong or a trail is gone, use **Contact Us** on the You tab and name the park and the trail. The OnMyLead team can take a line off the map right away.

related: [create-a-ride, find-a-ride, route-builder, create-a-ride-on-the-website]
keywords: [search, place, address, trailhead, park, town, coordinates, gps coordinates, lat long, find location, meeting point, tablet]
---

Wherever OnMyLead asks for a place, you can type its name instead of hunting on a map: a trailhead, an off-road park, a campground, a town or a street address.

## Where You Can Search

- **Creating a ride**: **Search a Place or Address** sets the meeting point, and **Search a Destination** fills in where the ride ends up. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).
- **Find a Ride**: **Search Near a Place** shows rides near the place you pick instead of near you. Tap **Back to Near Me** (or **Clear**) to go back. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).
- **Route builder**: **Search** moves the map to a place before you draw. See [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).

:::release 1.0.1
- **Waypoints map**: **Search** moves the map to a place so you can drop a waypoint or planned stop there. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).
:::

## Search

1. Tap the search box and type at least three letters.
2. Results show as you type. Each one says what it is and where, like "Trailhead in Moab, Utah".
3. Tap the one you want.

What happens next depends on where you searched:

- For a meeting point, the coordinates and place name fill in for you. You can still edit the **Place Name**.
- In the route builder, the map moves to the place and marks it. Nothing is added to your route.

:::release 1.0.1
- On the waypoints map, the map moves to the place and marks it. Press and hold (or click) the map there to drop a waypoint.
:::

If nothing turns up, try the full name, a street address with the town, or a nearby town.

## Search by Coordinates

Type coordinates as latitude and longitude, like `38.5733, -109.5498`, and pick the result. This works for spots that don't have a name.

## Good to Know

- Search covers places in the United States.
- Results near you, or near where the map is looking, come first.
- Search needs a connection. With no signal you'll see **No signal for place search. Try again with service.**
- Only the words you type and a rough area are sent to the search service, never who you are or your exact location.

## On the Website

The same searches work on onmylead.com. When you create a ride on the website, you can also click the map to drop the meeting point and drag the pin to fine-tune it. See [Create a Ride on the Website](/help/create-a-ride-on-the-website).

## Place Data

Places come from OpenStreetMap (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors), searched through Photon, a free service with no account.

articles.title: What Other Riders Can See
articles.summary: Your location is never public. See what strangers, riders on your ride and family links can see, and how OnMyLead's server enforces it.
articles.text:
---
title: What Other Riders Can See
summary: Your location is never public. See what strangers, riders on your ride and family links can see, and how OnMyLead's server enforces it.
category: safety-privacy
order: 30
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

  - supabase/migrations/20261102950000_events.sql

related: [location-sharing, family-link, report-and-block, ride-name-and-profile, delete-account]
keywords: [privacy, private, who can see me, meeting point, exact location, rounded, public ride, data, safe, stranger, tablet]
---

OnMyLead is built so your location is never public. You choose who sees it and for how long, and sharing always ends. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just hidden in the app.

## Before You Join a Ride

Anyone can see a ride's public page: its name, time, description and details such as difficulty and vehicles. What they don't get:

- **The exact meeting point.** Public listings and the ride map show a meeting area rounded to about a mile. The ride page says **Shown after you join**, or **Near** and the area's name.
- **The route, the meeting instructions and the roster.** Only riders who have joined the ride get these.

The exact meeting point and the route are stored separately from the public ride, and the server only hands them to riders on the ride.

## Riders on Your Ride

Once you've joined a ride, the other riders on it can see:

- Your ride name. If you turned on **Show My Google (or Apple or Facebook) Profile**, they also see that account's name and photo. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

:::release 1.0.3
- Your profile picture, if you added one. Like your ride name, any signed-in rider can see it, never people who aren't signed in. See [Add a Profile Picture](/help/profile-picture).
:::

- That you're on the ride, your role, and whether you've checked in.
- Your messages in the ride chat, except leader-only messages, which only you and the leader can read.
- Your status taps and quick replies from Ride Mode (and, from 2.0, messages you type there). A status tap carries your phone's location at the moment you tapped it.
- Your live location, but only while you're sharing with the ride.

:::release 2.1
- If you're the leader, the path you've ridden while sharing, drawn as the [Leader Trackline](/help/leader-trackline). Each rider's phone draws it from the live positions it already gets; nothing extra is uploaded. You can turn it off for the ride.
:::

## Your Live Location

The server only lets someone read your location while all of these are true:

- You have turned sharing on.
- Your share hasn't run out or been stopped.
- They are someone your share covers: a rider on that ride, a rider you picked, or someone with your family link.
- For ride sharing, the ride is still going and you're still on it.

When the ride ends, every ride share on it stops at once. When you leave a ride, your share for it stops. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

## Your Ride Track

While you share with a ride, your phone keeps a track of where you rode for your ride summary. Only you can see your own track. The group summary shows totals only, never anyone's route.

## Waypoints

Waypoints you drop are only yours, unless you're the ride's leader and choose to share one with the ride. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

## Family Links

Anyone with your family link can see your last location until that share ends. See [Share a Family Link](/help/family-link).

:::release 1.0.3
## Out Riding

[Out Riding](/help/out-riding) is off until you switch it on. While it's on, riders who can see you get your ride name, where you said you're riding (if you typed it) and roughly how far away you are in whole miles, never your location. OnMyLead keeps only an area of about a mile, and deletes it when you turn Out Riding off. It turns itself off at the time you picked, or after 6 hours without opening the app. By default only your friends, and riders you've ridden with or share a group with, can see you.

## Friends

Only you and the other rider can see that you're friends, or that one of you sent a request. Nobody can search for riders by name: a rider can only send you a request if they've ridden with you, share a riding group with you, can see you in Out Riding, have messaged with you, or have your friend link. Being friends never shares your location. See [Add Friends](/help/friends).
:::

:::release 2.0
## Reports

The OnMyLead team can't read your direct messages or chats. The one exception is a report: when a rider reports another rider, their messages with that rider (direct messages, and what either of them wrote in the last 30 days in a group or ride chat they share) are saved with the report so the team can look into it. Only the OnMyLead team can read them, and every time they're opened it's logged. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## Your Feed

Home's **Feed** shows your finished rides, badges, shared trails and group rides to **Friends Only** unless you change it. Under **Customize**, **Who Sees Your Activity** can be **Friends and Followers** or **Nobody**. A ride is named only to riders who were on it, or if it was public. Your location is never in a feed. Blocked riders never see your posts. See [Your Home Screen](/help/home-screen).

The same setting decides who can see your posts, likes and comments in Social and your activity on your profile. Photos you post are made smaller and have no location added. Anyone who can see a post can see its photo, and like any photo, someone with its address could pass it on. Sharing to Facebook, Instagram or X only happens when you tap **Share**, and a share never includes your location. See [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social).
:::

:::release 2.1
## The Badge Leaderboard

Signed-in riders can see the badge leaderboard: your ride name, picture, badges and the state or country you picked. Nothing else, and never where you are. Turn off **Show Me on the Leaderboard** to leave it. If **Who Sees Your Activity** is **Nobody**, you're left off until you turn it on. See [See the Badge Leaderboard](/help/badge-leaderboard).
:::

## Blocked Riders

When you block a rider, nothing tells them, and they can't see who has blocked them. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## Your Data

OnMyLead doesn't sell your data or use it for advertising. It shares data only with the services that run the app, such as Apple for notifications and purchases on iPhone. For the full list, read the Privacy Policy at onmylead.com/privacy.

On Android, Google delivers notifications (Firebase Cloud Messaging), handles purchases (Google Play) and draws the map (Google Maps).

:::release 2.0
[Music Controls](/help/music-controls) read what's playing only on your phone. On Android, the optional Notification Access is used only to see the song and the app playing it; OnMyLead never reads or keeps your notifications.

:::release 2.0
Your app settings and your own Map Mode trails (with their photos) are backed up to your account so they show on every device you sign in on. Only you can read that backup; a trail becomes public only when you tap **Share with Everyone**. Track Line and your live location are never part of it. See [Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device](/help/sync-across-devices).
:::
:::

:::release 2.0
When you agree to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement, a record of it is saved (your account, the version, the time, the device and app version, and your IP address). Other riders never see it, and it's kept as a legal record if you delete your account. See [The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement](/help/rider-safety-agreement#what-gets-saved).
:::

You can delete your account and its data at any time. See [Delete Your Account](/help/delete-account).

:::release 2.0
## Events

An event's place is picked by its host and is shown to everyone who sees the event, so hosts are asked to pick a public spot. It's stored to about 100 m. Events never show any rider's location. Anyone with an event's link can see it, but the names of its hosts, Ride Managers and riders going only show to signed-in riders.
:::

title: Your Free 30-Day Pro Trial
summary: Every new account gets 30 days of OnMyLead Pro with no payment, and it never turns into a paid subscription on its own.
category: pro

---

When you make a new OnMyLead account, you get 30 days of OnMyLead Pro for free. It starts on its own. There's nothing to sign up for and no payment details to enter.

:::tip
You're never charged when the trial ends. It does not turn into a paid subscription. Your account simply moves to Free unless you choose to subscribe.
:::

:::release 2.1
## A Fresh Trial With 2.1

OnMyLead 2.1 makes a few more things Pro: Bluetooth Sharing with no service, CarPlay, customizing your dot and group photos. So nobody loses anything the day it arrives, every rider who doesn't have Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial when 2.1 comes out, even if you already had a trial or are partway through one. Riders who subscribe, or have Pro from OnMyLead, keep it as before.

While a trial runs, Home shows **Your Pro Trial Runs Until** and the date. Close it with the **×**; it comes back only if your trial's end date changes.
:::

## See How Many Days Are Left

On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**. **Your Plan** shows **Pro Trial** with the days remaining, the date it ends, and a row of 30 marks that fills in as the days go by.

The trial is the same on Android. It belongs to your account, not your phone, so it shows the same days left on every device you sign in to.

## Trial Reminders

OnMyLead reminds you a week, 3 days and a day before your trial ends, and again when it ends.

:::until 1.0.3
- To turn off the notifications, switch off **Pro Trial Reminders** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).
:::
:::release 1.0.3
- To turn off the notifications, switch off **Badges and Pro Trial** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings). That also stops badge notifications and the notice when a trail you shared is hidden.
:::
- The same reminders come by email too. Switch off **Email Me Too** to stop the emails.

## When the Trial Ends

Your account moves to Free. Nothing you made during the trial is deleted:

- Your rides, routes, groups and downloaded maps stay yours.
- New Pro actions, like downloading another map area or importing a GPX file, need Pro again.
- Free accounts create one ride a month. Rides you created earlier in the same month, during the trial, count toward that month.

See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) for exactly what changes.

## Keep Pro After the Trial

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Keep Pro After the Trial**.
3. Choose **Annual** or **Monthly**.
4. Tap the **Subscribe for** button under the plans and confirm with Apple.

Apple charges you when you confirm, and your paid subscription starts right away. See [Subscribe to Pro](/help/subscribe-to-pro).

## Good to Know

:::until 2.1
- Each account gets one trial.
:::
:::release 2.1
- Each account gets one trial when it's made, plus the 2.1 trial above.
:::
- The trial is part of OnMyLead, not an Apple free trial, so it doesn't show in your Apple subscriptions.

---

Add a profile picture so the riders you meet know who's who. It shows in place of your initial wherever riders see you:

- the rider list on a ride page (who's going) and the riders in your riding groups
- ride chat and group chat
- **Messages** and your conversations
- **Friends** and **Out Riding**
- your name at the top of the **You** tab

Until you add one, riders see your initial, the same as before. Riders on the live ride map still show as colored dots, so the leader, tail gunner and anyone who stopped sharing stay easy to spot.

## Add or Change Your Picture

1. Go to the **You** tab and tap your name at the top.
2. Under **Profile Picture**, tap **Take Photo** to use the camera, or **Choose Photo** to pick one from your photo library.
3. Move and zoom the photo so your face (or your machine) sits in the square, then tap **Choose** (or the check mark).
4. The picture saves straight away and the screen says **Picture saved**.

To change it, do the same again: the button says **Choose New Photo**. Your old picture is replaced.

The first time, the app asks to use your camera or your photos. Only the photo you pick is uploaded. If you said no, turn access back on in your device's Settings app under OnMyLead.

:::tip
Every picture is cropped square and made smaller before it's uploaded, so it loads quickly even on one bar of signal.
:::

:::release 2.0
Pictures are kept under 200 KB, and anyone can tap a rider's picture to see it full size.
:::

## On the Website

On onmylead.com, tap your name on the **You** page, then **Choose Photo**. Your browser opens its file chooser; on a phone it also offers the camera. The picture is cropped to the middle square for you.

## Remove Your Picture

1. Go to the **You** tab and tap your name at the top.
2. Under **Profile Picture**, tap **Remove**, then **Remove** again to confirm.

Riders see your initial again.

## Who Can See It

Your picture follows the same rule as your ride name: riders who are signed in to OnMyLead see it next to your name. OnMyLead never shows it to people who aren't signed in, and its web address is a long random one that only signed-in riders are given. Like any photo, someone who has that address could still pass it on. It never shows where you are.

Your Apple, Google or Facebook photo is separate. It only shows if you turn on **Show My Google Profile** (or Apple or Facebook), and your uploaded picture comes first when you have both. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

## Keep It Friendly

Pictures that are offensive or break the rules can be removed by the OnMyLead team. You can upload a new one afterwards. If you see a picture that shouldn't be there, report the rider and pick **Inappropriate Photo**. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

When you delete your account, your picture is deleted with it.

articles.summary: Got an OnMyLead promo code? Redeem it in the app through Apple to get OnMyLead Pro with the offer it includes.
articles.text:
---
title: Redeem a Promo Code
summary: Got an OnMyLead promo code? Redeem it in the app through Apple to get OnMyLead Pro with the offer it includes.
category: pro
order: 50
release: "1.0"

related: [subscribe-to-pro, manage-subscription, restore-purchases]
keywords: [promo code, offer code, coupon, discount, redeem, gift, free months, tablet, app store offer]
---

OnMyLead promo codes are Apple offer codes for OnMyLead Pro. You redeem them through Apple, right from the app.

## Redeem a Code in the App

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Redeem Promo Code**.
3. Enter your code in Apple's window and follow the steps to confirm.

Apple shows what the code gives you before you confirm. Once Apple accepts the code, OnMyLead checks it and your plan changes to **Pro**. This can take a moment.

You can also tap **Redeem Promo Code** at the bottom of the Pro screen.

:::release 2.0
A 50% off code you earned by inviting a friend opens from **Invite Friends** with the code already filled in. See [Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro](/help/refer-a-friend).
:::

## Redeem a Code on Android

On Android, OnMyLead promo codes are Google Play promo codes.

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Redeem Promo Code**. Google Play's **Redeem Code** page opens.
3. Enter your code and follow the steps to confirm.
4. Come back to OnMyLead. Once Google Play has the code, your plan changes to **Pro**.

You can also redeem a code in the **Play Store** app: tap your profile picture, then **Payments & Subscriptions** > **Redeem Code**. A Google Play code works only on Google Play, and an Apple offer code works only in the App Store.

## Redeemed It in the App Store Instead?

That works too. Open OnMyLead afterwards, signed in to your account, with signal. The app picks up the code on its own and turns on Pro.

## Good to Know

- A promo code becomes an OnMyLead Pro subscription with your Apple Account. Manage or cancel it like any subscription. See [Manage or Cancel Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).
- Promo codes can only be redeemed in the app on your phone or tablet, not on the website.
- If your plan doesn't change to Pro, make sure you have signal and are signed in to the right OnMyLead account, then tap **Restore Purchases**. See [Restore Purchases](/help/restore-purchases).

articles.summary: Show your ride's QR code so riders can scan it at the trailhead, share it as a picture, or scan one to join a ride.
articles.text:

title: QR Codes
summary: Show your ride's QR code so riders can scan it at the trailhead, share it as a picture, or scan one to join a ride.
category: joining
order: 40
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05

related: [invite-riders, join-a-ride, getting-started]

screenshots:
  - file: qr.webp
    shows: app/src/components/ride-qr-sheet.tsx
---

Every ride has its own QR code. It's the quickest way to get riders on your ride at the trailhead: they point their camera at your screen and they're in.

![A ride QR code with its invite code](/help/img/qr.webp)

## Show Your Ride's QR Code

1. Open the ride page. Right after creating a ride, the invite card is at the top. Later, tap **Riders** to find it.
2. Tap **Show QR Code**, or tap the small QR code on the card.

The QR code opens full screen with the ride name and the invite code under it (**Or Enter Code**), so riders can type the code if their camera won't scan. Tap **Done** to close it.

:::release 1.0.3
You can also swipe it down to close it.
:::

## Share the QR Code as a Picture

1. Show the QR code full screen.
2. Tap **Share QR Code**.
3. Pick how to send it: text, email or any app.

It sends a picture of the QR code card along with the ride link. You can print it or post it for a club ride.

## Scan a QR Code to Join

1. Open your phone's Camera and point it at the QR code.
2. Tap the link that appears.
3. If you have OnMyLead, you go straight to the ride. If not, the ride's page opens on onmylead.com with a button to get the app.
4. Tap **Join Ride**. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

:::tip
Opened a ride link on your computer? The ride's web page shows its QR code. Scan it with your phone to open the ride there.
:::

:::note
The QR code holds only the ride's link and invite code. It doesn't show the meeting point. On a private ride, anyone who scans it can join, so share it with care.
:::

---
title: Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro
summary: Invite a riding buddy who's new to OnMyLead. When they finish their first ride, you both get Pro Annual at half price for the first year.
category: pro
order: 45
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

  - app/src/components/referral-reward.tsx

related: [friends, subscribe-to-pro, promo-codes, manage-subscription, free-vs-pro]
keywords: [refer a friend, referral, invite friends, invite code, discount, 50% off, half price, reward, pro annual, coupon, friend link]
---

Invite a riding buddy who's new to OnMyLead. When they finish their first ride, you both get **Pro Annual for $14.99 your first year** instead of $29.99. The discount comes from the App Store or Google Play, so it's billed the same way as any Pro subscription.

## Invite a Friend

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Invite Friends**. You can also tap **Invite Friends, Both Get 50% Off** at the bottom of the Pro screen.
2. Tap **Share Invite** and send it, or tap **Copy Link**.

Your invite link is your friend link, so your friend can also add you as a friend. See [Add Friends](/help/friends).

## What Your Friend Does

1. Opens your link and creates a new OnMyLead account within 7 days.
2. Finishes a ride: leads one or joins one that starts (goes live), runs for at least 10 minutes and is ended. A ride that's ended without ever starting doesn't count.

That's it. You both get a notification in the inbox, and the discount shows on **Invite Friends** and on the Pro screen.

## Claim Your Discount

1. On **Invite Friends** (or the Pro screen), find **You Earned 50% Off Pro Annual**.
2. Tap **Claim 50% Off**.

On iPhone and iPad, the App Store opens with your personal offer code filled in. Confirm it there. If the App Store doesn't open, the code is shown on the card: tap **Redeem Your Code** to try again.

On an Android phone or tablet, Google Play opens Pro Annual at the discounted price. Confirm the purchase there.

Once the store confirms it, your plan changes to **Pro**. The first year costs $14.99. After that, Pro Annual renews at the regular price unless you cancel. See [Manage Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).

### Already Paying for Pro

- **On Google Play:** Google Play offers are for new subscriptions only, so instead your next bill moves back 6 months. Tap **Apply Your Reward**.
- **On the App Store:** your code is used at your next renewal. A monthly plan moves up to Pro Annual at half price.

On the website, the card says to claim the discount in the app.

## The Fine Print

- Each rider can earn the discount once. Your other invites still show under **Your Invites**.
- Your friend's account has to be new. Riders who already had an account can't be invited.
- You have 6 months to claim the discount.
- A discount you claimed in one store works in that store only. An Apple code is redeemed on an iPhone or iPad, and the Google Play offer on Android.
- If you see **Invites aren't open right now**, invites are paused. A discount you already earned can still be claimed.

articles.summary: Report a rider or a ride to the OnMyLead team, and block a rider to hide their chat messages. Nobody is told who reported or blocked them.

title: Report or Block a Rider
summary: Report a rider or a ride to the OnMyLead team, and block a rider to hide their chat messages. Nobody is told who reported or blocked them.
category: safety-privacy
order: 40
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/e/[code].tsx
  - app/src/components/report-sheet.tsx

---

If a rider or a ride isn't right, report it to the OnMyLead team. If you'd rather not hear from a rider, block them. Neither one tells the other person it was you.

:::warning
If anyone is in danger, call 911 first.
:::

:::release 2.0
## Report a Rider From the You Tab

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **Help**, tap **Report a Rider**.
3. Tap the rider. The list shows riders you've messaged, added as friends, ridden with or share a group with, and riders you blocked. Type in **Search** to find one by name.
4. Pick what's wrong, add details if you like, and tap **Send Report**.

Riders you've never ridden with or messaged aren't listed, so nobody can look riders up by name.
:::

## Report a Rider

1. Open the ride and tap **Riders**.
2. In the **Going** list, tap the rider.
3. Tap **Report Rider**.
:::until 1.0.3
4. Under **What's Wrong**, pick **Harassment**, **Unsafe Riding**, **Spam or Scam**, **Fake Account** or **Something Else**.
:::
:::release 1.0.3
:::until 2.0
4. Under **What's Wrong**, pick **Harassment**, **Unsafe Riding**, **Spam or Scam**, **Fake Account**, **Inappropriate Photo** or **Something Else**.
:::
:::
:::release 2.0
4. Under **What's Wrong**, pick **Harassment**, **Threats**, **Unsafe Riding**, **Spam or Scam**, **Fake Account**, **Inappropriate Photo** or **Something Else**.
:::
5. Add details under **Anything Else (Optional)** if you like.
6. Tap **Send Report**.

:::release 1.0.3
To close the report without sending it, swipe it down or tap **Cancel**.
:::

You can also press and hold one of the rider's messages in ride chat or group chat, then tap **Report Rider**.

:::release 1.0.3
From a direct message, tap **•••** then **Report Rider**, or press and hold one of their messages. The message goes with your report. In Out Riding, tap **•••** next to a rider. See [See Who's Out Riding Nearby](/help/out-riding).
:::

:::release 2.0
## Report a Post or Comment

In Social, tap **⋯** on a post and tap **Report This Post**, or tap **Report** under a comment. Pick what's wrong, add details if you like, and tap **Send Report**. You can also report a rider from their profile. When three different riders report the same post or comment, it's hidden until the OnMyLead team looks at it. See [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social).
:::

## Report a Ride

1. Open the ride's page.
2. Scroll to the bottom and tap **Report Ride**.
3. Under **What's Wrong**, pick **Unsafe Plan**, **Spam or Scam**, **Offensive Content** or **Something Else**.
4. Add details if you like, then tap **Send Report**.

Reports go to the OnMyLead team, not to the rider or the organizer. OnMyLead looks at every report, and the person reported isn't told who sent it.

:::release 2.0
## What Happens After You Report a Rider

- The OnMyLead team is emailed about every report straight away.
- Your messages with the rider are saved with the report: your direct messages, and what either of you wrote in the last 30 days in a group chat or ride chat you share. Only the OnMyLead team can read them, and only to look into your report. Deleting a message or leaving a group afterwards doesn't remove the copy.
- If the rider broke the rules, OnMyLead can suspend their account for 1, 7, 30 or 90 days, or ban it for good. They're signed out within the hour and can't sign in until the suspension ends.
- You aren't told what action was taken, and they aren't told who reported them.

If you see **This account is suspended** when you sign in, your account was suspended for breaking the rider rules. If you think it's a mistake, [contact us](/help/contact-support).
:::

:::release 2.0
## Report an Event

On an event's page, scroll down and tap **Report This Event** (you need to be signed in, and it isn't shown to the event's hosts). Pick what's wrong (**Spam or Scam**, **Fake Event**, **Offensive Content**, **Inappropriate Photo**, **Unsafe Plan** or **Something Else**), add a note if you like, and tap **Send Report**. It goes to the OnMyLead team as a report about the event's host, with the event attached. The host isn't told who sent it. The team can hide the event or take down a photo.
:::

## Block a Rider

Blocking hides a rider's chat from you.

1. Open the ride and tap **Riders**.
2. In the **Going** list, tap the rider.
3. Tap **Block Rider**.
4. Tap **Block** to confirm.

You can also block from:

- Ride chat or group chat: press and hold their message, then tap **Block Rider**.
- A report: tap **Block This Rider**, or **Also Block This Rider** after you send it.

### What Blocking Does

- You don't see their messages or polls in ride chat or group chat.
- You don't get chat notifications or pop-ups from them.
- They aren't told, and they can't see that you blocked them.

:::release 1.0.3
- Neither of you sees the other in Out Riding, their direct messages are hidden from you, and they can't message you.
- If you were friends, you aren't anymore, and any friend request between you is removed. Neither of you can send a new one.
:::

### What Blocking Doesn't Do

- Announcements and Ride Mode quick replies from them still show, because they carry the plan and safety of a ride you're both on.
- Their Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts always come through.
- It doesn't remove them from a ride or stop them seeing you on a ride you're both on. If you're worried about your safety on a ride, leave the ride or stop sharing your location. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

## Unblock a Rider

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **Settings**, tap **Blocked Riders**.
3. Tap **Unblock** next to the rider.

You can also tap the rider in a ride's **Going** list and tap **Unblock Rider**.
