title: Restore Purchases
summary: Bring your OnMyLead Pro subscription back after getting a new iPhone, reinstalling the app, or signing in again.
category: pro

---

If you pay for OnMyLead Pro but your plan shows Free, for example on a new iPhone or after reinstalling the app, use **Restore Purchases**. It finds your Pro subscription with Apple and turns Pro back on.

## Restore Your Subscription

1. Sign in to your OnMyLead account.
2. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
3. Tap **Restore Purchases**.
4. If Apple asks, sign in with the Apple Account you used to buy Pro.

When it works, the app says **Your Pro subscription is restored.** and your plan shows **Pro**.

You can also tap **Restore Purchases** at the bottom of the Pro screen.

## If It Says No Purchase Was Found

The app says **No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Apple ID.** when the Apple Account on this iPhone has no active OnMyLead Pro subscription. Check that:

- You're signed in to the same Apple Account you used to subscribe.
- The subscription is still active. Look in iPhone **Settings** > your name > **Subscriptions**.
- You have signal.

## Restore on Android

On Android, **Restore Purchases** looks for OnMyLead Pro on the Google account signed in to the Play Store. If it finds none, the app says **No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Google account.** Check that the Play Store is signed in to the Google account you used to subscribe, and that the subscription is still active in the **Play Store** app under **Payments & Subscriptions** > **Subscriptions**.

You don't need to restore on a different kind of device. Pro bought on an iPhone shows on your Android phone or tablet as soon as you sign in to the same OnMyLead account, and the other way round.

## One Subscription, One Account

An Apple subscription gives Pro to one OnMyLead account at a time. If you restore it while signed in to a different OnMyLead account, Pro moves to that account. Make sure you're signed in to the account you want Pro on before you tap **Restore Purchases**.

:::note
Restore Purchases works in the app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. Once Pro is on your account, it also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.
:::

articles.title: Keep the Group Together with Ride Bubble
articles.summary: Ride Bubble watches for riders who drop back, run ahead or stop moving, and warns the leader and tail gunner before anyone gets lost.
articles.text:
---
title: Keep the Group Together with Ride Bubble
summary: Ride Bubble watches for riders who drop back, run ahead or stop moving, and warns the leader and tail gunner before anyone gets lost.
category: ride-mode
order: 30
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/core/bubble.ts
  - app/src/core/precise-location.ts
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/live.tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/new.tsx
  - app/src/components/rider-pin.tsx
  - app/src/components/group-map.tsx
related: [ride-mode, leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner, status-buttons, create-a-ride, location-sharing]
keywords: [bubble, separated, together, left behind, gap, distance alert, stopped rider, tight trail, desert, highway, tablet]
---

Ride Bubble keeps an eye on the gaps in the group while Ride Mode is open. When a rider gets too far from everyone else, stops while the group keeps moving, or goes quiet, Ride Bubble flags them. It's free on every plan.

## How It Decides

Each rider is measured against the nearest other rider, not just the leader. That way a rider who has run far ahead counts too, and the tail gunner at the back is measured against the last rider rather than the whole pack.

A rider turns yellow or red when:

- **They're too far from the nearest rider.** The distances depend on the ride's Ride Bubble setting (below).
- **They've stopped while at least half the group is moving.** Yellow after 2 minutes stopped, red after 5 minutes.
- **Their phone has gone quiet.** No update for 5 minutes turns a rider red, with a message like "No update from Sam for 6 minutes. Showing last known location."

Only riders who are sharing their location are part of Ride Bubble. A rider who isn't sharing can't be measured.

:::release 2.0
A rider whose phone shares only an approximate location (Precise Location turned off) can show up a mile or more from where they are. Ride Bubble leaves out the distance their rough location could be off by, so a rider beside you isn't called separated. See [Make Your Location Accurate](/help/accurate-location).
:::

## Ride Bubble Settings

The organizer picks the setting when creating the ride, under **Add Route, Difficulty and More**, in **Ride Bubble**.

| Setting | Yellow when the nearest rider is more than | Red when the nearest rider is more than |
|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | 0.5 miles | 1.5 miles |
| **Tight Trail** | 0.1 miles | 0.25 miles |
| **Desert** | 0.75 miles | 2 miles |
| **Highway** | 1 mile | 3 miles |

The stopped and no-update times are the same for every setting.

## What Everyone Sees

- A yellow or red ring around a rider's dot on the map.

:::release 2.0
With **Color Blind Mode** on (**You** > **Appearance**), the ring is yellow or orange-red, OK riders show sky blue, and a **!** or **✕** appears before the rider's name. See [Change the Look](/help/appearance).
:::

- At the top of Ride Mode, **Together** in green, or the number of red riders, such as **2 Separated**, in red. Tap it to see every rider and when they last updated.

## What the Leader and Tail Gunner See

The ride's leader, tail gunner, organizer and co-organizers also get:

- **An alert card** for each yellow or red rider, such as "Mike is 1.7 miles behind the group. Last moving 4 minutes ago." Tap **Navigate** for directions to them. Leaders and organizers can also tap **Regroup** to set a regroup point at their location.
- **A spoken alert and a buzz** the moment a rider turns red, so you don't have to look down.

The alert cards hide when the bottom panel is folded. Tap **Buttons ▲** to open the panel and see them.

:::note
Spoken alerts pause while your own phone has no service. When you lose signal everyone looks quiet, and that's your signal dropping, not theirs.
:::

:::release 2.0
Spoken alerts use the most natural voice on your phone. To hear and pick another, see [Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts](/help/voice).
:::

## Tips

- Ask everyone to share their location for the whole ride so Ride Bubble can see them. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
- Give someone the tail gunner role so the back of the group is covered. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

articles.summary: Message everyone on the ride or just the leader, post announcements, and clear or resolve your own messages.

title: Use Ride Chat
summary: Message everyone on the ride or just the leader, post announcements, and clear or resolve your own messages.

Every ride has its own chat for the riders on it. Use it to plan before the ride and check in after. Only riders who have joined the ride can read or post in it.

![Ride chat with polls](/help/img/chat.webp)

:::warning
Don't type while driving or riding. In Ride Mode, use the one-tap quick replies instead. See [Send a Status or Quick Reply](/help/status-buttons).
:::

:::release 2.0
In Ride Mode you can also tap **Message** to send the group a short message of your own, or one of your saved quick replies, once you've pulled over. See [Type Your Own Message](/help/status-buttons).
:::

## Open Ride Chat

1. Open the ride from the **Rides** tab.
2. Tap **Chat** in the row of sections under the ride's name.

Tap **Ride Chat** at the top of the card to hide or show the messages. Hidden, it shows the message count and the latest message. The chat shows the newest 30 messages. To see older ones, tap the button above them, such as **Show 12 Earlier**.

## Send a Message

1. Under **Send To**, pick who it's for:
   - **Everyone:** every rider on the ride.
   - **Leader Only:** only you and the ride's leader see it. The leader's name is shown on the option.
2. Type in the **Message** box.
3. Tap **Send to Everyone** or **Send to Leader**.

Your message shows in the chat straight away as **Sending…**, then **Sent**. If it doesn't go through, it stays as **Not Sent** with **Retry** and **Remove**.

Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send more than 10 messages in a minute, you're asked to wait a minute.

:::note
The ride's leader is every rider with the Leader role. If nobody has been given that role, the organizer leads. Leader-only messages are kept private by the server, not just hidden in the app. If you're the leader, you won't see the **Leader Only** option.
:::

## Post an Announcement

Organizers and co-organizers can post an announcement for the whole group.

1. Under **Send To**, pick **Announcement (Pinned, Read Aloud)**.
2. Type in the **Announcement** box.
3. Tap **Post Announcement**.

The newest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page.

:::until 2.0
In Ride Mode it shows as a yellow banner and is read aloud, so riders don't have to look at their phones. Tap the banner to hear it again.
:::

:::release 2.0
In Ride Mode it shows as a banner at the top with an amber edge and a megaphone, under the sender's name, and is read aloud, so riders don't have to look at their phones. Tap the banner to hear it again.
:::

## Clear or Resolve Your Own Message

1. Tap **•••** next to a message you sent.
2. Choose one:
   - **Mark Resolved:** the message gets a green **Resolved** tag for everyone. Tap **Reopen** to undo it. Marking your latest announcement resolved takes it off the pinned spot.
   - **Clear:** removes the message from the ride chat for everyone. Tap **Clear** again to confirm. This can't be undone.

Only the person who sent a message can clear it or mark it resolved.

## Quick Replies in Chat

Quick replies sent from Ride Mode, like **On My Way**, also show in the ride chat in italics.

:::release 2.0
So do messages typed in Ride Mode with **Message**.
:::

:::release 2.1
With no service, a quick reply or message from a rider close by arrives over Bluetooth and shows here marked **Via Bluetooth** until OnMyLead has it. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
:::

## Message Pop-Ups

When a new message arrives on a ride you're on, a pop-up slides in at the top of the screen, whatever screen you're on.

- Tap the pop-up to open the ride.
- Tap **Dismiss** to close it. When several are waiting, it shows **+2 More** and **Dismiss All**.
- Pop-ups close on their own after a few seconds, and announcements stay up a little longer.
- If the sender clears a message or marks it resolved before you see it, its pop-up goes away.

Pop-ups and notifications follow your choices in **Notifications**. See [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Report or Block Someone in Chat

Press and hold someone else's message, then tap **Report Rider** or **Block Rider**. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

articles.summary: See the forecast for the meeting area and check whether your ride gets back before sunset, right on the ride page.

---
title: Ride Day and Weather
summary: See the forecast for the meeting area and check whether your ride gets back before sunset, right on the ride page.
category: rides
order: 60
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-04
sources:

  - app/src/app/r/[code].tsx
related: [create-a-ride, directions, fuel-range, emergency-and-safety]
keywords: [weather, forecast, rain, wind, temperature, sunset, sunrise, daylight, dark, countdown, storm, tablet]
---

The **Ride Day** card on the ride page shows the weather for the meeting area and how your ride lines up with daylight, so nobody gets surprised by a storm or the last miles in the dark.

## Where to Find It

Open the ride page. **Ride Day** is in the **Details** section. It shows on upcoming and live rides.

## The Forecast

Ride Day shows the meet day's forecast:

- The conditions, such as Clear, Partly Cloudy, Rain or Thunderstorms
- The high and low temperature
- The chance of rain
- The wind speed, and gusts when they're much stronger than the wind

The forecast shows up about two weeks before the ride. Until then the card says when it will appear. The forecast is for the ride's general meeting area, not the exact spot.

:::tip
The last forecast your phone loaded is saved, so it still shows at a trailhead with no signal. It only updates when you have a connection.
:::

### Weather Warnings

Ride Day adds a heads-up when the forecast calls for:

- Thunderstorms (watch for lightning and flash floods in washes)
- A 60% or higher chance of rain
- Gusts of 35 mph or more
- A high of 100°F or more
- A low of 32°F or below

## Daylight Check

Ride Day shows sunrise and sunset at the meeting area, with a bar that shows when the ride runs against the daylight.

If the ride has a **Back By** time (the **Expected Finish** you set when creating the ride), Ride Day tells you:

- How long before sunset the group is back
- When it's cutting it close: back less than 45 minutes before sunset
- When the group will be back after dark, with a reminder to bring lights

If there's no finish time, the card says to add a Back By time so it can check it against sunset.

## Countdown

At the top of an upcoming ride's page, a tag counts down to the meeting time, such as "Tomorrow", "In 4 Days" or "Starts in 25 min".

Ride Mode is the screen you use on the trail. It puts the whole group on one map, shows how fresh each rider's position is, places everyone along the route, and gives you big one-tap buttons for telling the group what's going on. Ride Mode is free on every plan.

![Ride Mode with the route strip and status buttons](/help/img/live.webp)

## Open Ride Mode

Ride Mode opens once the organizer starts the ride.

- **Organizers:** on the ride page, tap **Start Ride Mode**. The ride goes live for everyone and Ride Mode opens.
- **Riders:** once the ride is live, open the ride page and tap **Enter Ride Mode**. Riders on the ride also get a notification when the ride starts.

:::release 1.0.3
The map opens centered on you, zoomed in to about 10 miles across so nearby trails show, and clear of the panels over the map. If your phone hasn't found you yet, the map centers on you as soon as it does, unless you've already moved the map yourself. If OnMyLead can't use your location, the map opens on the group, the route or the meeting point instead.
:::

The first time you open Ride Mode on a ride, it asks **Share Your Location with This Ride?** Pick how long to share, or tap **Not Now**. You can see the group without sharing, but the group can't see you. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

:::tip
Your screen stays on while Ride Mode is open, so the map is ready when you glance at it. Keep a charger handy on long rides.
:::

## What's on the Screen

### The Top Bar

:::until 2.0
- **‹ Ride name:** tap it to go back to the ride page.
- **The sharing pill:** shows how long you have left sharing, such as **1h 20m**, or **On** when there's no timer. It says **Off** when you aren't sharing; tap it to start. While you share, tap it to show **Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left** with **Stop** and **Hide**.
:::

:::release 2.0
- **‹ (back):** the round button on the left goes back to the ride page.
- **Ride name and sharing:** under the ride's name a green dot and **Sharing · 1h 20m Left** (or just **Sharing** when there's no timer) show you're sharing. When you aren't, it says **Not Sharing · Tap to Share**; tap it to start. While you share, tap the name to show **Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left** with **Stop** and **Hide**.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
If you've turned on [Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver), that banner also names the setting, such as **Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left · Balanced**.
:::

- **Together** or **2 Separated** (on the right): green when the group is together, red with a count when [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble) sees riders who have dropped away. Tap it to open the **Riders** list.

### The Map

The map shows the ride's route, waypoints, planned stops and any regroup point. Every rider who is sharing shows as a dot with their ride name beside it. Tap a rider's dot to see their name, whether they're live, and their latest status.

:::until 1.0.3
The leader is the one bigger blue dot, so you can find them at a glance.
:::

:::release 1.0.3
Each rider is a white ring with a dark center and a dark name tag, easy to spot on satellite, topo and the dark map. The leader is the bigger solid blue dot with a blue name tag, so you can find them at a glance. Every dot sits on the rider's exact position and stays there as you zoom in and out.

When a rider is moving, a small white arrow on the edge of their dot points the way they're heading, even when you turn the map. A rider who is stopped, or whose position is only last seen, has no arrow, because a phone can only tell direction while it moves.
:::

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 every live rider is a glossy disc with a white rim and a white arrow built into it, pointing the way they're heading. The leader is the biggest dot, in blue with a blue name tag; the tail gunner is the next biggest, in violet with a violet name tag; everyone else is graphite with a dark name tag. A rider keeps their arrow, pointing the last way they were heading, while they're stopped and still live. A rider whose position is only last seen is a hollow ring with no arrow, as before.

Your own dot is Red, White and Blue unless you pick another Dot Style in [Map Settings](/help/map-layers), with a soft beam ahead of it. Its arrow always shows which way you're facing: the way you're riding while you move, and your phone's compass when you stop.
:::

:::release 2.0
Riders glide smoothly to each new position instead of jumping, and with [Follow Me](/help/follow-me) on, the map moves with you in one steady motion.
:::

:::release 2.1
A blue line follows behind the leader, showing exactly where they rode. When the leader crosses back over it or doubles back, the older pass fades so the fresh line stands out. The leader can turn it off. See [Follow the Leader's Trackline](/help/leader-trackline).
:::

You don't need to leave Ride Mode to see new riders. Someone who joins the ride while you're on the map appears within a few seconds of starting to share, and a rider whose share ends or who leaves the ride drops off the map within about 15 seconds.

:::until 2.1
To switch map layers or download the ride's map for riding with no signal, use the layers button on the map. See [Map Layers](/help/map-layers) and [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).
:::

:::release 2.1
To switch map layers or download the ride's map for riding with no signal, use the round **Map Settings** button on the map. See [Map Layers](/help/map-layers) and [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).
:::

:::release 1.0.2
### Center the Map on You

Tap the round target button to move the map so you're in the middle of it. The map keeps how far you've zoomed in or out (if you're zoomed far out, over a whole state or more, it zooms in to about 10 miles across), and puts you in the middle of the part you can see, clear of the panel. If the app doesn't have your location yet, the button spins for a moment while your phone finds you. If location is off for OnMyLead, it offers **Open Settings** so you can turn it on.

- **iPhone and Android phones:** the button sits on the right, just above the bottom panel (above **Add Waypoint**). When the panel is open and fills the screen, fold it to see the button.
- **iPad and Android tablets:** the button sits at the bottom of the map, just left of the buttons panel.
:::

:::release 2.0
### Follow Me

With **Follow Me** on (it is unless you turn it off), the map moves with you as you ride, so your dot stays in view. Drag or pinch the map to look around and it pauses; tap **Paused** or **Center on Me** to follow you again. Tap **Following** to turn it off. The button sits just left of **Center on Me**. See [Follow Me on the Map](/help/follow-me).

:::until 2.1
While you're moving, your own dot has the same white arrow as everyone else's, pointing the way you're heading.
:::
:::

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 your dot moves through the middle of the map; near an edge the map zooms out one step, and the next time it centers on your dot and moves with you so you're always on screen. Coming up on a junction, it zooms in so you see the turn, then zooms back out (**Zoom In at Intersections** in the **You** tab turns that off). See [Follow Me on the Map](/help/follow-me).
:::

### The Bottom Panel

:::until 2.0
The panel at the bottom holds the route strip, alert cards, the quick replies and the status buttons. See [Status Buttons and Quick Replies](/help/status-buttons).
:::

:::release 2.0
The panel at the bottom holds, from the top:

- the route strip, with how far along the route you are;
- an alert row for each rider who has dropped away or called for help, with **Navigate** (and **Regroup** for leaders);
- three quick replies, **On My Way**, **Need a Minute** and **All Good**, and **More**, which opens every quick reply (like **Running Late** and **Beverage Break**) and status;
- **Regroup Here** (for organizers and leaders) and **EMERGENCY**.

See [Send a Status or Quick Reply](/help/status-buttons).
:::

:::release 2.0
Tap **Message** at the top left of the panel to type your own message to the group or send one of your saved quick replies. See [Type Your Own Message](/help/status-buttons).
:::

Above the panel are two buttons: **Directions** (on the left) for Apple Maps or Google Maps, and **Add Waypoint** (on the right) to mark your spot. You can also press and hold anywhere on the map to drop a waypoint there.
:::release 2.1
When the leader shares one during the ride, everyone else gets a notification with a sound. See [New Waypoint Alerts](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops#new-waypoint-alerts).
:::
See [Get Directions](/help/directions) and [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

On Android, **Directions** opens Google Maps, and while you share, a **Sharing Your Location** notification stays in the notification shade. Tap it to come back to OnMyLead. If your phone restarted or the app was updated while you were sharing, opening Ride Mode starts that notification and your sharing again.

## Read the Rider Dots

A dot only looks live when the phone behind it is actually checking in. A sharing phone sends its position at least every 15 seconds while it has service, even when it's parked.

| What you see | What it means |
|---|---|
| Solid dot (from version 1.0.3: a white ring, or solid blue for the leader) | Live. The position is less than a minute old. |
| Hollow dot (from version 1.0.3: a thin grey ring) with **Last Seen 2 Min Ago** | Where the rider was last seen, a minute or more ago. |
| Dashed grey ring with **No Signal, 8 Min Ago** | Nothing for three minutes or more. Their phone has likely lost service or stopped sending. |
| Faint ring, **Not Sharing** | The rider is on the ride but isn't sharing their location. |
| Yellow or red ring around a dot | Ride Bubble thinks the rider is separating from the group. |
| Amber wrench on a dot | The rider tapped **Mechanical Issue**. |
| White arrow on a dot (version 1.0.3 and later) | The rider is moving; the arrow points the way they're heading. |

## See Every Rider

Tap **Together** (or **Separated**) at the top to open the **Riders** list. It shows everyone on the ride, the leader first, with **Live**, **Last Seen** and an age, **No Signal**, or **Not Sharing**. The leader and tail gunner are labeled.

:::release 1.0.3
A small patch beside a rider's name is their top badge. See [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks).
:::

:::release 2.0
A rider whose phone shares only a rough spot shows **Approximate Location**. Their dot can be a mile or more from where they are. See [Fix Common Problems](/help/troubleshooting).
:::

Tap **Navigate** next to a live rider, or **Go to Last Seen** for a rider whose spot is old, to get directions to them in your maps app.

## See Where You Are on the Route

:::until 2.0
When the ride has a route, the route strip at the bottom shows the whole route as one straight line from start to finish, with each rider placed by how far along they are. It shows your miles so far, such as **12.3 of 40.1 mi**, and how far you have to go. Below the line it tells you where you stand, for example "The leader is 0.4 miles ahead" or "2 riders ahead of you, 1 behind", and warns you if you're off the route.
:::

:::until 2.1
When the ride has a route, the line at the bottom shows your miles so far, such as **12.3 of 40.1 mi**, and how far you have to go. Below the line it tells you where you stand, for example "The leader is 0.4 miles ahead" or "2 riders ahead of you, 1 behind", and warns you if you're off the route.
:::

:::release 2.1
When the ride has a route, the line at the bottom shows every sharing rider in order. Under it, centered, it tells you where you stand, for example "The leader is 0.4 miles ahead" or "2 riders ahead of you, 1 behind", and warns you if you're off the route.
:::

If you've added your machine in the [Garage](/help/garage) with its fuel details, the strip also says whether your range covers the route. See [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range).

### See the Whole Group in Order

:::until 2.0
Every rider who is sharing has a dot on the route line, strung out in running order: the rear on the left, the front on the right. Each dot sits as close to the rider's real spot as it can, and riders bunched together line up side by side instead of hiding each other, so the leader can see everyone between the front and the rear at a glance.
:::

:::release 2.0
Every rider who is sharing has a dot on the leader line, strung out in running order. The leader is always at the far left and the tail gunner is always at the far right. Everyone else sits between them by how far behind the leader they are, and riders bunched together line up side by side instead of hiding each other, so the leader can see the whole group at a glance.

- If the leader isn't sharing, the rider out front takes the left end. With no tail gunner sharing, the rider furthest back takes the right end.
- A rider who gets ahead of the leader, or drops behind the tail gunner, still shows just inside the ends; tap their dot to see how far ahead or behind they are.
:::

- **L** in blue is the leader, **S** in purple is the tail gunner, and the red **You** dot is you. Other riders show their initial.
- A hollow dot is a rider off the route. A grey dashed dot is where a rider was last seen.
- Tap a dot to see who it is and their place, such as "Mia · 3rd of 6 · 0.4 mi behind the leader".
- Riders who aren't sharing their location aren't on the line.
- With a big group, the dots get smaller to fit the line.

:::release 2.1
### See How Spread Out the Group Is

A thin measuring line runs under the leader line, from under the leader's dot to under the tail gunner's dot. The number in the middle, such as **0.8 mi**, is how far the rider furthest back is behind the leader (in feet when the group is close, or **a few yards** when everyone is together). Small ticks along the line mark round steps, such as every 0.1 mi or every 0.5 mi, so you can see how far apart the dots really are.

- It works on routes and on Freerides, and it uses whatever spots your phone has, including ones passed over [Bluetooth Sharing](/help/bluetooth-sharing) with no service.
- When the leader or the last rider is only last seen, the number starts with **~**, because it's from their last known spot.
:::

:::release 2.0
### See the Group Behind the Leader on a Freeride

A Freeride has no route, so the line at the bottom of Ride Mode shows the group behind the leader instead. The leader is at the far left, the tail gunner (or the rider furthest back) is at the far right, and everyone else is in order between them.

:::until 2.1
- The top of the line shows how spread out the group is, such as **0.9 mi spread, Leader to Tail Gunner**. When everyone is close, it says how many riders are together.
:::
:::release 2.1
- The measuring line under the dots shows how spread out the group is, such as **0.9 mi** from the leader to the tail gunner.
:::
- Below the line it tells you where you stand, for example "The leader is 0.3 mi ahead". The leader sees how far back the tail gunner (or the last rider) is.
- Distances are measured along the path the leader has ridden, so bends and switchbacks count. Your phone keeps that path from the leader's live location while you're in Ride Mode; it stays on your phone and isn't uploaded.
- A hollow dot is a rider who isn't on the leader's path, such as someone who took another way or was already behind when you opened Ride Mode. Their distance is measured in a straight line.
- Until the leader shares their location, the line says it's waiting for the leader.
- Tap a dot to see who it is and their place, just like on a route.
:::

## Fold the Panel to See More Map

:::until 2.0
Swipe the bottom panel down, or tap **Hide ▼** on its handle, to fold it away.
:::

:::release 2.0
Swipe the bottom panel down, or tap the grab bar at its top, to fold it away.
:::

Swipe up or tap **Buttons ▲** to bring it back. The app remembers your choice.

While the panel is folded:

- **Mechanical Issue** and **EMERGENCY** stay on screen.
- Need Help and EMERGENCY calls from other riders stay on screen. The leader, tail gunner and organizers also keep Mechanical Issue calls.
- Other alerts are counted in a badge on **Buttons ▲**.

:::release 1.0.3
Sheets that slide up over the map (**Riders**, **Directions**, a waypoint, Share Your Location and **EMERGENCY**) close when you swipe them down, the same as tapping **Cancel**, **Close** or **Done**. In a long sheet, the first swipe scrolls back to the top. If the keyboard is up, the first swipe puts the keyboard away.
:::

On a tablet the map fills the screen. The **Riders** list sits on the left (tap **Hide** or swipe it left to fold it, **Show Riders** to bring it back) and the buttons panel on the right. See [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet).

:::release 1.0.3
## Full Map

Want the map and nothing else? Tap **⤢ Full Map** at the top of the bottom panel. The ride name, banners, map buttons and the riders list tuck away, and a slim bar at the bottom keeps:

- the route line with every rider's dot (when the ride has a route);
- **EMERGENCY**, always one tap away;
- Need Help and EMERGENCY calls from other riders.

Full Map works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets.
:::

:::until 2.0
The bar also has **Menus ▲**, with a badge counting any other alerts. Tap it to bring back the status buttons, quick replies and everything else.
:::

:::release 2.0
The bar also has **Controls**, with a badge counting any other alerts. Tap it, or swipe the bar up, to bring back the status buttons, quick replies and everything else. **Center on Me** and the **No Signal** tag stay on the map (from 2.0, **Follow Me** too), and tapping a trail line still shows its card. Your phone remembers Full Map, so Ride Mode opens the same way next time. Every other map works the same way: see [Full Map](/help/full-map).
:::

:::release 2.0
:::release 2.0
:::release 2.1
## On the Car Screen

If your vehicle has Apple CarPlay, connect your iPhone and tap **OnMyLead** on the car screen while Ride Mode is open. You get big status buttons, your group and EMERGENCY on the dash. See [Use OnMyLead on CarPlay](/help/carplay).
:::

## Control Your Music

Tap the round **Music** button above **Center on Me** to pause, skip or change the volume of the music on your phone without leaving Ride Mode. See [Control Your Music While You Ride](/help/music-controls).

:::release 2.0
The **Tilt** tile on the left of the map shows your vehicle's roll and pitch (until you calibrate the tilt meter it says **Calibrate Tilt**); tap it for the full tilt meter. **Crash Alert** also runs while Ride Mode is open: after a hard hit or a rollover it counts down 30 seconds, and if you don't tap **I'm OK**, your group gets an EMERGENCY alert. See [Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert](/help/tilt-and-crash-alert).
:::
:::

:::release 2.0
## Spoken Alerts

Ride Mode reads announcements, regroup points, a rider falling behind and Mechanical Issue out loud in the most natural voice on your phone. To hear and pick another voice, go to **You** > **Voice**. See [Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts](/help/voice).
:::

## When Your Location Isn't Sharp

If your phone's location is rough, a yellow banner says why: **Precise Location Is Off**, **Google Location Accuracy Is Off** (Android) or **Your Phone Has a Rough Location Right Now**. Tap it to fix it. On Android the phone asks to change to a precise location or to turn on Google Location Accuracy; on iPhone and iPad Settings opens; for a rough location you get steps, such as calibrating in Google Maps. The banner goes away once it's fixed. See [Make Your Location Accurate](/help/accurate-location).
:::

## When You Lose Service

If your phone can't reach the server for a short while, a banner says **No Service. Riders Show Where They Were Last Seen**. Everyone else's dots switch to last seen with their ages, because your phone can't hear new positions. If you're sharing, the banner adds that yours sends when service returns.

:::until 2.1
**Live positions only update when a phone has a connection.** With an offline map downloaded, you keep the map and the route on screen with no signal, but other riders' dots don't move until your phone, and theirs, get service again.
:::

:::release 2.1
Riders close to you on the same ride keep moving with no service, over Bluetooth, and the banner says **No Service. Sharing With 2 Nearby Phones Over Bluetooth**. Your status taps, quick replies and messages reach them too, phones pass everything along the group, and the card under your tap names who got it. Tap **Bluetooth On** on the banner to turn Bluetooth Sharing off, and tap it again to turn it back on. Seeing riders and sharing your spot, taps and messages over Bluetooth are Pro; on Free the button shows the **Pro** tag, and your phone still passes things along and sends EMERGENCY. Riders out of Bluetooth range show where they were last seen. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
:::

Status taps and quick replies you make with no service wait on your phone and send on their own when you get signal.

:::release 2.1
## See the Land in 3D

From 2.1 the live map is drawn by Mapbox on every device, and on onmylead.com too, so the website's Ride Mode shows the same live map as the phone. Tap the **Map Settings** button and pick **3D Terrain** under **Map Style** to see the ride on the real shape of the land, with contour lines and peak heights. Rider dots, the route, waypoints and the regroup pin all show the same way. See [3D Terrain](/help/3d-terrain).
:::

## Leave Ride Mode

:::until 2.0
Tap **‹ Ride name** at the top to go back to the ride page.
:::

:::release 2.0
Tap **‹** at the top left to go back to the ride page.
:::

Leaving the screen doesn't stop sharing: your location keeps going to the group until your timer runs out, the ride ends, you leave the ride, or you tap **Stop**.

:::release 2.0
## Leave the Ride

Heading home early? Tap **Together** (or **Separated**) at the top to open **Riders**, then tap **Leave Ride** under the list and confirm. On a tablet, **Leave Ride** is at the bottom of the **Riders** sidebar. Your location stops going to the group and you're taken back to the **Rides** tab. The organizer first picks who takes the ride over; see [Leave a Ride You Organize](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).
:::

:::until 2.0
Opened Ride Mode by tapping a notification? Tap **‹ Ride name** (or Android's Back) to go to **Home**.
:::

:::release 2.0
Opened Ride Mode by tapping a notification? Tap **‹** at the top left (or Android's Back) to go to **Home**.
:::

articles.summary: Pick the ride name other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat, and choose whether to show your Apple, Google or Facebook profile.

---
title: Your Ride Name and Profile
summary: Pick the ride name other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat, and choose whether to show your Apple, Google or Facebook profile.
category: account
order: 20
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:

keywords: [nickname, display name, username, change name, profile photo, social profile, google profile, facebook profile, apple profile, tablet]
---

Your ride name is how the group knows you. It shows on the group map, the rider list and in ride chat. A nickname works fine.

:::release 1.0.3
Under your name on the **You** tab you also see your rank and badges. See [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks).
:::

:::release 1.0.3
The same screen also has your **Profile Picture**. See [Add a Profile Picture](/help/profile-picture). The screen is called **Your Name and Picture**.
:::

## Pick or Change Your Ride Name

1. Go to the **You** tab and tap your name at the top. If you haven't picked one yet, it says **Pick Your Ride Name**. You can also tap **Pick Your Ride Name** on the **Rides** tab.
2. Type your name in **Ride Name**.
3. Check the preview at the top. It shows your pin on the map and a chat line, the way the group sees you.
4. Tap **Save Name**. The button changes to **Name Saved**.

Until you pick a name, other riders see you as Rider.

:::tip
Keep it to 24 characters or fewer so it fits on the map. Extra spaces are tidied up when you save.
:::

## Where Your Name Comes From at First

If you created your account with your name, or signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, your ride name may already be filled in from that. You can change it any time.

## Show Your Apple, Google or Facebook Profile

If you signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, you can let the riders you ride with see that account's name and photo. It helps people recognize who joined.

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Account**, find **Show My Google Profile** (or **Show My Apple Profile** or **Show My Facebook Profile**, depending on how you signed in).
3. Turn the switch on.

When it's on, your photo replaces your initial, and a line like "Your Name on Google" shows under your ride name in a ride's rider list and in your riding groups.

When it's off, nobody else sees it. It's off until you turn it on.

### Who Can See It

- Only riders who have been on a ride with you or share a riding group with you.
- Never strangers browsing public rides.
- Never someone you've blocked, or who has blocked you.

The name and photo come from the account you signed in with, and the app keeps them up to date each time you open the **You** tab. You can only turn the setting on or off.

If you signed in with email only, this setting doesn't appear.

## Your Email

Under **Account** on the **You** tab, **Email** shows the email on your account. Only you see it.

articles.title: Ask the Group with a Ride Poll
articles.summary: Leaders post a quick question in ride chat, like a lunch stop or the pace, and every rider votes with one tap.
articles.text:
---
title: Ask the Group with a Ride Poll
summary: Leaders post a quick question in ride chat, like a lunch stop or the pace, and every rider votes with one tap.
category: ride-mode
order: 50
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/components/ride-poll.tsx
  - app/src/components/ride-chat.tsx
  - app/src/core/polls.ts
  - app/src/core/pro.ts
  - app/src/app/r/[code].tsx
  - app/src/hooks/use-ride-chat.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261017420000_ride_polls.sql
related: [ride-chat, free-vs-pro, organizer-controls]
keywords: [poll, vote, voting, question, lunch stop, pace, survey, tablet]
screenshots:
  - file: chat.webp
    shows: app/src/components/ride-poll.tsx
---

A ride poll is a quick question in the ride chat with a few choices. Every rider on the ride gets one vote, can change it, and sees the live counts.

![Polls in ride chat](/help/img/chat.webp)

## Who Can Post a Poll

The ride's leader, the organizer and co-organizers can post polls. Every rider on the ride can vote.

Creating a poll: This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free plan, picking **Quick Poll** shows **Create Ride Polls**, marked Pro, instead of the poll form. Voting stays free for everyone.

:::release 2.0
From version 2.0, voting on a poll is also a Pro feature. On a Free account, the vote line carries a **Pro** tag. Reading a poll and its results stays free.
:::

## Post a Poll

1. Open the ride and tap **Chat**.
2. Under **Send To**, pick **Quick Poll**.
3. Tap a starter to fill it in, or type your own:
   - **Lunch Stop?** (Yes, No)
   - **How's the Pace?** (Too Slow, Just Right, Too Fast)
   - **Saturday or Sunday?**
   - **Morning or Afternoon?**
4. Type or edit the **Question**.
5. Fill in **Choice 1** and **Choice 2**. Tap **Add Choice** for more, or **Remove** to drop one.
6. Tap **Post Poll**.

The poll shows in the chat for everyone, and riders get a pop-up saying "Poll from" your name.

### Poll Limits

- 2 to 5 choices, each different.
- The question can be up to 200 characters.
- Each choice can be up to 60 characters.

## Vote

1. Open the ride and tap **Chat**.
2. Tap a choice. It's marked **Your Vote**.

To change your vote, tap another choice. Each choice shows its count and a bar for its share of the votes, and the leading choice is shaded darker. Under the choices you'll see the total, such as **3 Votes**, or **No Votes Yet**.

## Remove a Poll

The person who posted the poll can tap **•••** next to it and tap **Clear**. The poll and its votes are removed for everyone.

articles.title: Ride Summary and Ride Again
articles.summary: After a ride ends, see your distance and route, who finished, share a ride card, and set up the same ride again in a few taps.
articles.text:
---
title: Ride Summary and Ride Again
summary: After a ride ends, see your distance and route, who finished, share a ride card, and set up the same ride again in a few taps.
category: rides
order: 70
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/components/ride-summary.tsx
  - app/src/components/ride-card.tsx
  - app/src/core/summary.ts
  - app/src/lib/location.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261102200000_ride_miles_cleanup.sql
  - app/src/app/r/[code].tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/new.tsx
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx
  - app/src/core/pro.ts
  - app/src/core/entitlements.ts
related: [organizer-controls, create-a-ride, location-sharing, free-vs-pro, ride-mode]
keywords: [summary, stats, statistics, distance, track, ride card, share, recap, ride again, repeat ride, copy ride, history, past rides, tablet]
---

When the organizer ends a ride, everyone who was on it gets a summary on the ride page. Organizers can also start the same ride again with one tap.

## See Your Ride Summary

1. On the **Rides** tab, find the ride under **Past Rides**.
2. Tap it. The summary is at the top of the ride page.

The summary has three parts.

### Your Ride

Your **Distance** and how long you were **Out For**, plus a map of your route. Only you can see your route.

Your stats come from sharing your location in Ride Mode. If you didn't share, there's no track for you on that ride. See [Location Sharing](/help/location-sharing).

:::release 2.0
Your distance counts only the miles you actually rode. OnMyLead leaves out:

- spots where your phone said its location was rough (off by more than about 100 m, or 330 ft), such as indoors or with Approximate Location on;
- GPS jumps, where your dot bounces away and straight back, or moves while your phone says you're standing still;
- time when your location was off for more than five minutes, such as with the app closed. The miles across that gap aren't guessed with a straight line, so turn sharing on before you roll out.

If your distance looks short, check that your phone has a good location (see [Make Your Location Accurate](/help/accurate-location)) and that you shared for the whole ride.
:::

**Moving Time**, **Average Speed**, **Top Speed** and **Climbing** are part of Advanced Ride Statistics. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Your full stats are saved either way.

### The Group

Who finished the ride: the riders still on it when it ended. With Pro, you also see the group's totals: the **Longest** and **Average** distance and the **Group Top Speed**. These are totals only, and nobody's route is shown.

### Ride Card

A picture of the ride to share with friends or on social media.

1. Pick a layout: **Standard**, **Full Stats** or **Big Number**.
2. Tap **Share Ride Card**.

**Standard** is free. **Full Stats** and **Big Number** are Premium Ride Cards. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). The card never shows the meeting point or anyone's route.

## Ride Again

Organizers can set up the same ride again without filling everything in.

1. Open the ended ride's page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card, tap **Ride Again**.
3. The Create a Ride form opens with the name, details, meeting point and route already filled in. The day is set to the next one on the same weekday.
4. Check the day and times.
5. Tap **Create Public Ride** or **Create Private Ride**.

On a ride that hasn't ended yet, the same button is called **Copy This Ride**.

:::note
Ride Again creates a new ride, so it counts toward your monthly rides on Free. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).
:::

Advanced Ride Statistics, Premium Ride Cards and full ride history work with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android.

## Past Rides

Ended and cancelled rides move to **Past Rides** on the **Rides** tab. Free shows your last 5. Full ride history is a Pro feature. Nothing is deleted, so older rides show again with Pro. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

To remove a ride from your Past Rides, swipe left on it and tap **Leave** (or **Delete** if you organized it). On onmylead.com, click the button at the end of the ride's row instead.

articles.title: The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement
articles.summary: Why OnMyLead asks you to agree before you ride, what the agreement says, where to read it again, and what gets saved when you tap I Agree.
articles.text:
---
title: The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement
summary: Why OnMyLead asks you to agree before you ride, what the agreement says, where to read it again, and what gets saved when you tap I Agree.
category: safety-privacy
order: 45
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/components/rider-agreement.tsx
  - app/src/app/rider-agreement.tsx
  - app/src/core/rider-agreement.ts
  - app/src/lib/rider-agreement.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261102700000_rider_agreement.sql
  - supabase/migrations/20261106020000_rider_agreement_v2.sql
related: [emergency-and-safety, getting-started, privacy, delete-account]
keywords: [911, call 911, emergency disclaimer, disclaimer, liability, waiver, release, terms, agreement, risk, legal, before you ride, i agree, safety agreement]
---

The first time you open OnMyLead, a **Before You Ride** screen shows the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. Every rider agrees to it before using the app: on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and tablets, and on onmylead.com after you sign in.

## What It Says

In short: you ride at your own risk, and you're responsible for riding safely.

- Riding and driving can lead to injury, death and damage, and you accept those risks.
- Never look at, type on or tap your phone while your vehicle is moving. Pull over first, or let a passenger use the app.
- Only ride where it's legal and allowed. Maps, routes, trails and waypoints, including ones other riders share, can be wrong, closed or on private land.
- OnMyLead is not an emergency or safety service. Alerts can be late or never arrive. In an emergency, call 911. See [Emergencies and Staying Safe](/help/emergency-and-safety).
:::release 2.1
- **Always call 911 in an emergency.** The EMERGENCY button, Crash Alert, Need Help and the Emergency Siren only alert other riders on your ride who use OnMyLead. They don't call or text 911 or any rescue service, and they can be late or not work at all with no signal, a dead battery or Bluetooth out of range. If anyone is hurt or in danger, call 911 or your local emergency number first, then tell your group.
:::
- You're responsible for what you do and for any accident you cause, and you release RUS Offroad LLC and OnMyLead from liability for your riding and your use of the app.
- If you're under 18, a parent or guardian agrees for you.

The full text is at [onmylead.com/rider-agreement](/rider-agreement). It's part of the [Terms of Use](/terms).

## Agree to It

1. Read the agreement on the **Before You Ride** screen. Scroll to see all of it.
:::until 2.1
2. Tick the box that says **I have read and agree to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement, and I accept the risks of riding**.
:::
:::release 2.1
2. Tick the box that says **I have read and agree to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement, I accept the risks of riding, and I will always call 911 in an emergency**.
:::
3. Tap **I Agree**. The button stays grey until the box is ticked.

You're asked once, the first time you open the app. You won't see it again on that phone, tablet or browser, even after signing out, unless the agreement changes, in which case everyone is asked to agree to the new version. If you agree before you sign in, that answer counts for the account you sign in with next on that device. If you use a new phone or reinstall the app, it checks your account and doesn't ask again.

:::release 2.1
Version 2 of the agreement (November 6, 2026) adds **Always Call 911 in an Emergency**, so after you update to OnMyLead 2.1 the **Before You Ride** screen shows once more. Read it, tick the box and tap **I Agree** to keep riding.
:::

No signal? Tapping **I Agree** works offline, so you can still use Ride Mode and Help and SOS. The app sends the record as soon as it's back online.

The **Terms of Use** and **Privacy Policy** links on the screen open those pages. Go back to return to the agreement.

## Read It Again

- In the app: on the **You** tab, tap **Safety Agreement** at the bottom.
- On the website: **Rider Safety Agreement** at the bottom of the onmylead.com homepage, or go to onmylead.com/rider-agreement.

## What Gets Saved

When you tap I Agree, OnMyLead saves a record of it: your account, email address and ride name, the version you agreed to and a fingerprint of its exact words, the time, the app version, the kind of device and its system version, your language, IP address and browser. Other riders never see it.

The record can't be changed or deleted, and it's kept if you delete your account, because it's a legal record of what you agreed to. See the [Privacy Policy](/privacy).

---
title: Create and Manage a Riding Group
summary: Save the people you ride with as a group, invite friends with a link, and invite the whole group to a ride in one tap.
category: groups

A riding group is your regular crew, saved once. When you create a ride, you can invite everyone in the group in one tap instead of sending the invite to each rider. Each group also has its own [Group Chat](/help/group-chat).

Your groups live on the **Groups** tab, on the **Riding Groups** screen. It shows **Your Groups** (the ones you run) and **Groups You’re In** (the ones someone else runs).

:::release 1.0.3
The top of the Groups tab also has **Out Riding**, to see who's out riding near you, **Messages**, your direct messages, and **Friends**. See [See Who's Out Riding Nearby](/help/out-riding) and [Add Friends](/help/friends).
:::

:::note
This is a Pro feature. You need Pro to create a group and to add or remove riders. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Joining a group with its link, the group chat, inviting a group to your rides and getting the group's ride invites are free for everyone.

:::release 2.0
On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold **Pro** tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags.
:::
:::

## Create a Group

1. Tap the **Groups** tab.
2. Tap **New Group**.
3. Type a **Group Name**, like Saturday Crew. Names can be up to 60 characters.
4. Under **Add Riders You’ve Ridden With**, tick the riders you want in the group.
5. Tap **Save Group**.

The list only shows people you have been on a ride with, the ones you ride with most at the top. If nobody shows up yet, save the group anyway and send friends the group link (see below).

A group holds up to 100 riders.

## Invite Friends With the Group Link

The group link is for friends who aren't on OnMyLead yet, or anyone you haven't ridden with. Anyone in the group can share it.

1. On the **Groups** tab, tap the group.
2. Scroll to **Invite by Link**.
3. Tap **Share Group Link**, or tap **Text**, **Email** or **Copy**.

When your friend opens the link, they see the group's name, who runs it and how many riders are in it. They don't see who the riders are until they join.

:::release 2.1
If the group has a group photo, the link shows it at the top too, so your friend can tell it's your crew.
:::

They tap **Join Group**, or **Create a Free Account to Join** if they don't have an account yet.

:::release 1.0.3
The card also shows the **Group Code**, the end of the group's link. The rider who runs the group can tap **Choose Your Own Code** to make it something like SATURDAY-CREW, or type one under **Group Code (Optional)** when creating the group. See [Choose Your Own Code](/help/custom-codes).
:::

:::tip
If a link got shared somewhere it shouldn't, the rider who runs the group can tap **Make a New Link**. The old link stops working, and everyone already in the group stays in.
:::

## Add More Riders

If you run the group:

1. Open the group.
2. Tap **Add Riders You’ve Ridden With**.
3. Tick the riders and tap **Add Riders**.

## Invite Your Group to a Ride

You can invite a group you're in to any upcoming ride you organize or co-organize. There are two ways.

From the group:

1. Open the group.
2. Tap **Invite to a Ride**.
3. Tap **Invite** next to the ride.

From the ride:

1. Open the ride and go to **Riders**.
2. Under **Invite a Group**, tap **Invite All** next to the group.

:::release 2.0
Or plan a new ride for the group: on Home, tap **Plan a Group Ride** on the **Your Group** card. The new ride has that group ticked under **Your Riding Groups**, so everyone is invited when you create it.
:::

Everyone in the group gets a notification and sees the ride under **Ride Invites** on their home screen. They can tap **Join Ride**, with no waiting for approval, or **No Thanks**. Riders who are already on the ride, waiting, or who said no thanks are left alone.

To get these invites, keep **Ride Invites** on in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

:::release 2.1
## Add a Group Photo

If you made the group, you can give it a photo, like the crew lined up by the trailhead. Everyone in the group sees it at the top of the group page, next to the group's name on the **Riding Groups** screen, on the **Your Group** card on Home and under **Invite a Group** on a ride. It also shows on the group link. Until you add one, the group shows its initials.

Adding or changing a group photo is part of OnMyLead Pro, including the Pro Trial. On Free, **Take Photo** and **Choose Photo** show the **Pro** tag. Everyone can see group photos on every plan, and you can always remove one.

1. Open the group.
2. Scroll down to **Group Photo**, below the riders.
3. Tap **Take Photo** to use the camera, or **Choose Photo** to pick one from your photo library. On onmylead.com, **Choose Photo** opens your computer's or phone's file picker.
4. The photo saves straight away and the screen says **Group photo saved**.

The photo is wide (16:9). On an Android phone or tablet you frame it on the crop screen before it saves. On iPhone, iPad and the website the middle of the photo is used, so keep the crew near the center.

To change it, tap **Choose New Photo** (or **Take Photo**). To take it down, tap **Remove**, then **Remove** again. Tap the photo at the top of the group page to see it full size.

Only the rider who made the group can add, change or remove its photo. Anyone with the group link can see it, so keep it friendly: the OnMyLead team removes photos that break the rules.
:::

## Rename a Group

If you run the group, open it, tap the group's name, type the new name and tap **Save Name**.

## Remove a Rider, Leave or Delete a Group

- **Remove a rider:** if you run the group, tap **Remove** next to the rider. They stop getting the group's ride invites. You can add them back later.
- **Leave a group:** open the group and tap **Leave Group**. The group link brings you back if you change your mind.
- **Delete a group:** if you run the group, tap **Delete Group**. The group goes away for everyone in it. Rides you already invited it to stay as they are.

## Who Can See a Group

A group's name and who is in it are only visible to the rider who runs it and the riders in it. The group link only shows the name, who runs it and how many riders are in it.

:::release 2.1
The group link also shows the group photo, if the group has one.
:::

If your Pro ends, your groups stay. Everyone in them can still chat, and you can still invite the group to your rides. Creating new groups and adding or removing riders needs Pro again.

summary: Tap the map to lay down your ride's route. It snaps to trails for you, and every rider sees it in Ride Mode.

keywords: [route builder, draw route, map a route, trail snapping, follow trails, straight line, undo, route miles, mapped ride, edit route]
---

A route is the line your group will follow. Once it's saved, every rider on the ride sees it on the ride page and in Ride Mode, with everyone placed along it. You draw it by tapping points on a satellite map, and OnMyLead follows the trails between your taps for you.

:::until 2.0
Drawing a route is free.
:::

:::release 2.0
Drawing a route is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, **Mapped** on Create a Ride and **Build the Route** carry a **Pro** tag. Freeride rides, and following the leader's route on a ride, stay free.
:::

Bringing one in from a GPX file is covered in [Import a GPX Route](/help/import-gpx).

:::release 1.0.3
To ride one of your own trails from [Navigate](/help/navigation-mode), tap **Use One of My Trails** in the route builder and pick it. The trail is used as the route just as you recorded or drew it. This is a Pro feature, like GPX import. Clear it to draw your own.

:::release 2.0
On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold **Pro** tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags.
:::
:::

## Who Can Draw the Route

The ride's organizer and any co-organizers can build or change the route, until the ride has ended or been cancelled. Everyone else on the ride sees the finished route but can't change it. See [Organizer Controls](/help/organizer-controls).

## Open the Route Builder

When you create a ride and pick **Mapped** under **The Route**, the route builder opens as soon as the ride is created.

To open it later:

1. Open the ride and tap the **Map** tab.
2. Tap **Build the Route**. If the ride already has a route, tap **Edit Route**. For a Freeride, tap **Map a Route Anyway**.

:::note
A Freeride that gets a saved route becomes a mapped ride.
:::

## Draw Your Route

The map opens at the ride's meeting point.

1. Tap the map where the ride starts. That's point 1, shown in green. To get there fast, tap **Search** at the top and type a trailhead, park or town.
2. Tap further along the trail. The route follows the trail between your two taps.
3. Keep tapping along the way. Each new point is numbered, and the last one is shown in white.
4. Watch the miles add up at the top of the panel at the bottom of the screen.
5. Tap **Save Route** when you're done.

After you save, you're taken back to the ride. Only riders on this ride can see the route.

### Follow Trails or Straight Line

Two choices in the panel decide how the next points are joined:

- **Follow Trails**: each tap lands on the nearest trail or road, and the line between taps runs along it. While it works this out you'll see a dashed straight line and **Finding the trail…**.
- **Straight Line**: draws straight from point to point. Use it for open ground, a wash or a park nobody has mapped.

You can switch between them as you go. Points you already placed keep the way they were drawn. The app remembers your choice for next time.

If no mapped trail joins two points, that part is drawn as a straight line and the app tells you so. Add a point on the trail, or zoom in and try again. Points very far apart are also joined with a straight line, so tap more often on long stretches.

:::tip
Trails come from OpenStreetMap, so snapping works best where riders have mapped the trails. Zooming in before you tap helps each point land on the trail you meant.
:::

### Fix Mistakes

- **Undo** takes back the last point.
- Drag any numbered point to move it. If the line next to it was following a trail, it snaps again.
- **Clear** removes every point. Nothing is saved until you tap **Save Route**.

To see more of the map, swipe the panel down or tap its handle. It folds down to the miles and an **Undo** button.

:::release 2.0
For the whole screen, tap **Full Map** on the panel's grab bar. The top bar, layers button and panel tuck away, and a slim bar keeps the miles and **Undo**. Keep tapping the map to add points, and tap **Controls** (or swipe the bar up) to bring everything back. See [Full Map](/help/full-map).
:::

## Search for a Place

To jump the map to a trailhead, park, forest or town before you draw:

1. Tap **Search** at the top of the screen.
2. Type a name, an address or coordinates.
3. Tap a result. The map moves there and marks it.

Searching only moves the map. Nothing is added to your route. See [Search for a Place](/help/place-search).

## Check Who Can Ride a Trail

While drawing, a tap adds a point, so press and hold a trail line instead to see its name and which vehicles it's open to. You can also turn trail lines on or off and switch to a topo map with the layers button. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).

## Change or Remove a Route

1. Open the ride, tap the **Map** tab, and tap **Edit Route**.
2. Move, add or undo points, then tap **Save Route**.

To take the route off the ride, tap **Clear**, confirm, then tap **Remove Route**.

When you save a route, the ride's listed miles update to match it.

## On the Website

You can build the route at onmylead.com too, using the same steps:

- Click the map instead of tapping, and drag a point to move it.
- Press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) to undo the last point.
- Trail lines and their names appear once you zoom in to about a county's width, and **Follow Trails** snaps to them the same way.
- On a wide screen, the tools panel sits beside the map.

On a tablet held sideways, the tools panel sits beside the map; swipe it up or tap **Hide** to fold it. Held upright, it floats in the bottom corner of the map.

:::release 2.1
The route builder's map is drawn by Mapbox on every device from 2.1, so it looks the same on the phone and the website. Tapping, dragging a numbered point and the trail lines work as described here. It stays flat: with **3D Terrain** picked, the builder shows plain satellite.
:::

The website's map has the same layers button: switch to **Topo**, turn trail lines on or off, and see trail names and closed trails in red. A click adds a point while you draw, so to see a trail's card, click its line on a route you aren't editing (an imported GPX route). See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers). A route you save on the website is in the app as soon as you save it.

## No Signal

Once you've opened a ride with a route, the route is saved on your phone, so it's still there without signal. With no signal, **Follow Trails** can only use trail data already saved on your phone, so in other places it draws straight lines. Saving a route needs a connection.

## Map Data

Trail lines and snapping use map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, © OpenMapTiles, served by OpenFreeMap. Snapping is worked out on your phone or in your browser. Your taps aren't sent to a routing service.

title: Gear From RUS Offroad
summary: Why you may see product suggestions from RUS Offroad on your machine's page and your trip packing list, and how they're picked.

---

OnMyLead is made by RUS Offroad. In a couple of places, the app may suggest RUS Offroad products that fit your machine or your packing list. The section is always labeled **Gear From RUS Offroad**.

## Where You'll See It

- On one of your machines in your [Garage](/help/garage), with products that fit that machine.
- On a trip in the [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner), with products that fit your packing list and the machine you're taking.

Each suggestion shows the product, its price and how it fits, like "Fits your" followed by your machine, or "Fits most machines."

## Buy or Browse

- Tap **Buy** to open that product on the RUS Offroad store inside the app.
- Tap **Shop more at rusoffroad.com** to browse the whole store.

Purchases happen on the RUS Offroad website, not through OnMyLead or your Apple subscription.

## When It Doesn't Show

The section only appears when something fits. You won't see it if nothing matches, if the store can't be reached, or if suggestions are switched off for a while.

title: Find Places to Ride With Scout
summary: Scout shows off-road parks, OHV areas, trail systems, trailheads and motocross tracks near you, up to 1,000 miles away.
category: joining
order: 15
release: "2.1"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

related: [find-a-ride, create-a-ride, directions, place-search]
keywords: [scout, discover, explore, places to ride, parks, offroad parks, off-road parks, ohv, orv, atv park, trails near me, trailheads, motocross, mx track, riding areas, distance, miles]
---

Scout finds places to ride near you: off-road parks, OHV areas, trail systems, trailheads and motocross tracks. It looks 250 miles around you to start, and you can change that from 10 to 1,000 miles.

## Open Scout

1. Tap the **Find** tab.
2. Tap **Places to Ride** at the top. (**Rides** takes you back to public rides.)
3. Allow location if asked. If location is off, tap **Use My Location**, or search a town or park instead.

Places show on the map as teal signs, with a picture of the kind of place (a flag on a peak for an off-road park, a quad for an OHV area, a forked trail for a trail system, a signpost for a trailhead and a checkered flag for a motocross track), and in a list under it (beside it on a tablet or a wide screen), nearest first. Each place shows what kind it is, where it is, how far away it is and how many public rides are coming up there.

## Change How Far Scout Looks

Under **How Far to Look**, drag the slider, tap along it, or tap **-** and **+** to move one step: 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 750 or 1,000 miles. The list and the circle on the map update when you let go. Scout remembers the distance on this device for next time.

## Look Somewhere Else

Planning a trip? Tap **Look Around a Town or Park**, type a place and pick it from the results. Scout shows **Places Near** that place. Tap **Back to Near Me** to look around you again.

## Show Only Some Kinds of Places

Under the slider, tap a kind, such as **Off-Road Parks** or **Trailheads**, to show only that kind. Tap more than one to see each of them. Tap a kind again to turn it off. Each chip shows how many places of that kind Scout found.

## Open a Place

Tap a place in the list, or tap its sign on the map and then **Open Place**. Its page shows:

- what kind of place it is, where it is and how far away it is;
- **Create a Ride Here**, which starts a public ride with the meeting point already on the place;
- its website, when we have one;
- **Directions** in your maps app (see [Directions](/help/directions));
- **Public Rides Here**: public rides meeting within 15 miles that you can join;
- a short description, when the source has one.

:::note
Place details come from the US Forest Service, the Bureau of Land Management and OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors), plus places riders suggested. Each page says where its details came from. Check the rules, hours, fees and which vehicles are allowed with the park or agency before you go.
:::

## Suggest a Place We're Missing

1. At the bottom of the Scout list, tap **Know a Place We're Missing?**
2. Enter the name and pick what kind of place it is.
3. Show us where it is: search for it, tap the map, or tap **I'm There Now** if you're standing at it.
4. Add the website and anything we should know if you like, then tap **Send Suggestion**.

You need to be signed in to suggest a place. We check every suggestion before it shows in Scout. Riders never see who suggested a place.

## On a Tablet or the Website

On an iPad, an Android tablet or a wide browser window, the slider, the filters and the list sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen. Tap **Full Map** to make the map fill the whole screen. On the website, Scout is at onmylead.com under **Find** once you sign in.

keywords: [log in, login, sign up, register, password, forgot password, reset, magic link, email link, apple, google, facebook, sign out, log out, tablet]
---

You need an account to create rides, keep a Garage and save riding groups. You can sign in with a social account, with your email and a password, or with a link we email you.

## Open the Sign-In Screen

1. On the **Rides** tab or the **You** tab, tap **Sign In or Create a Free Account**.
2. At the top, choose **Sign In** if you already have an account, or **Create Account** if you're new.

Tapping something that needs an account, like the **Groups** tab, also opens this screen.

## Sign In With Apple, Google or Facebook

Depending on what's turned on, you'll see **Continue with Apple**, **Continue with Google** and **Continue with Facebook** at the top of the screen.

1. Tap the button for the account you want to use.
2. Follow the steps on the Apple, Google or Facebook screen.
3. You're signed in and taken back to OnMyLead. If you were new, your account is created.

With Apple, the name on your Apple Account is used as your ride name the first time you sign in, if Apple shares it. You can change it any time. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

:::note
On the website and on Android, **Continue with Apple** uses Apple's web sign-in: the page goes to Apple and comes straight back. It's only there when it's been switched on; if you don't see it, use Apple in the iPhone app or sign in another way. The Android app needs version 2.1 or later for it.
:::

## Create an Account With Email and a Password

1. Tap **Create Account** at the top.
2. Enter **Your Name**. This is what riders will see, and you can change it later.
3. Enter your **Email**.
4. Enter a **Password** of at least 8 characters.
5. Tap **Create Account**.
6. If the app says **Almost done**, open the email we sent and tap the link on the same iPhone. Your email is confirmed and you're signed in.

## Sign In With Email and a Password

1. Tap **Sign In** at the top.
2. Enter your **Email** and **Password**.
3. Tap **Sign In**.

## Sign In With an Email Link (No Password)

1. Enter your **Email**.
2. Tap **Or email me a sign-in link instead (no password)**.
3. Open the email on the same iPhone and tap the link.

The link signs you in and opens Home, even if the sign-in screen was still open. If you don't have an account yet, it creates one.

## Reset a Forgotten Password

1. Tap **Sign In** at the top.
2. Enter your **Email**.
3. Tap **Forgot your password? Email me a reset link**.
4. Open the email on your iPhone and tap the link.
5. Enter a **New Password** of at least 8 characters.
6. Tap **Save Password**.

If you see **This Link Has Expired**, tap **Back to Sign In** and ask for a new reset link.

## Opening an Email Link on Another Device

If you tap a link from us in a browser on an iPhone, you may see **Open OnMyLead**. Tap **Open in the App** to finish in the app, or **Continue on the Website** to stay in the browser.

:::release android
On an Android phone or tablet, a link from us opens Chrome for a moment and then OnMyLead, which finishes signing you in. If OnMyLead isn't installed, the website signs you in instead. If you see **Open OnMyLead** in the browser, tap **Open in the App**.
:::

If you see **Your Email Is Confirmed** and a request to sign in again, the link opened somewhere other than where you signed up. Your email is confirmed. Tap **Sign In** and sign in once more with your email and password.

## Sign Out

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Scroll down and tap **Sign Out**.

This signs you out on this device only. If you're also signed in on another device or the website, you stay signed in there, and any location you're sharing from that device keeps going.

## If Something Goes Wrong

- **That email and password don't match**: check for typos, or use the reset link above.
- **Please confirm your email first**: tap the link in the email we sent you, then sign in.
- **There's already an account with that email**: switch to **Sign In** at the top.
- **Too many emails sent just now**: wait a few minutes and try again.
- **That Link Didn't Work**: the link expired or was already used. Tap **Back to Sign In** and ask for a new one.

Still stuck? [Contact Us](/help/contact-support) and pick **Account and Sign-In**.

articles.summary: See what your friends are up to, like and comment on rides, badges and trails, reply to comments, post ride reports with a photo, and share them.
articles.text:

title: Like, Comment and Post in Social
summary: See what your friends are up to, like and comment on rides, badges and trails, reply to comments, post ride reports with a photo, and share them.
category: groups
order: 27
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

related: [home-screen, friends, profile-picture, free-vs-pro, report-and-block, notification-settings, privacy]
keywords: [social, timeline, feed, like, likes, heart, comment, comments, reply, replies, like a comment, reply to a comment, photos, post, ride report, photo, profile, rider profile, pro badge, pro tag, share, facebook, instagram, x, twitter, share card, friends activity]
---

**Social** is where you see everything your friends and the riders you follow have been up to: finished rides, badges, shared trails, group rides and posts. You can like anything, read every comment, and open any rider's profile.

## Open Social

- On the **Rides** tab, tap **Open Social** next to **Feed**, or tap any post in the feed.
- Or tap **Friends & Social** in your toolkit.

On a phone, Social has three tabs: **Activity** (everyone's posts), **Friends** and **My Posts**. On an iPad, an Android tablet or a big window, your friends sit on the left and the posts on the right, so you can switch without losing your place.

## Like and Comment

- Tap the **heart** under a post to like it. Tap it again to take the like back.
- Tap **Comment**, or tap the post, to open it on its own page with every comment and who liked it.
- Type in the box at the bottom (up to 500 characters) and tap the red arrow.

You can delete your own comments. You can also delete any comment on your own posts, rides, badges and trails.

:::release 2.1
## Like and Reply to Comments

- Tap **Like** under a comment to like it. The heart turns red and shows how many riders liked it. Tap it again to take the like back.
- Tap **Reply** under a comment. "Replying to" and the rider's name show above the box; type your reply and tap the red arrow. Tap **✕** to go back to a plain comment.
- Replies sit under the comment they answer, a step in. Replying to a reply keeps it in the same conversation and starts it with **@** and the name of the rider you answered.

The rider whose comment you like or answer gets a notification. Deleting a comment deletes its replies too.
:::

## Post on Your Profile

1. In Social, tap **Post a ride report…** at the top (it's also at the top of your own profile).
2. Write up to 500 characters about the ride, the trail or the crew.
3. Tap **Take Photo** or **Add Photo** to add one picture, if you like.
4. Tap **Post**.

Your post shows on your profile and in the feeds of the riders your **Who Sees Your Activity** setting allows (see [Your Home Screen](/help/home-screen)). To delete it, tap **⋯** on the post, then **Delete Post**. Its likes and comments go with it.

Photos are made smaller before they upload: no more than 1,280 pixels on the long side and under 1 MB. Nothing about where you took the photo is added.

## Rider Profiles

Tap a rider's name anywhere in Social to open their profile: their picture, the **PRO** tag if they have OnMyLead Pro, when they joined, their rides, miles and badges, and their posts, rides, badges and trails, newest first. Tap the picture to see it full size.

From a profile you can **Message** a friend, **Add Friend**, or **Report** them. You see a rider's activity only if their **Who Sees Your Activity** setting allows it.

## See a Picture Full Size

Tap any profile picture, in Social, Friends, Messages, chats or Who's Riding, to see it big. Tap a post's photo to see the whole photo. Tap anywhere to close it.

## Share to Facebook, Instagram or X

1. Tap **Share** under one of your own rides, badges or posts, or under a shared trail.
2. Tap **Share Picture** to share a picture card with the miles, badge or trail name, or **Share Text Only**. The picture is a 1080 by 1350 PNG named OnMyLead, about 1 to 2 MB, so Facebook, Instagram and Messages take it right away.
3. Pick Facebook, Instagram, X, Messages or any other app.

Every share links to onmylead.com. Your location is never in a share, and you can't share other riders' rides or posts, or who's out riding right now.

On the website, **Share Picture** opens your browser's share menu. If your browser doesn't have one, the picture downloads and the text is copied so you can paste it into your post.

## Free and Pro

| | Free | Pro |
|---|---|---|
| See Social and every comment | Yes | Yes |
| Like posts | Yes | Yes |
| Comment | No | Yes |
| Post on your profile | No | Yes |
| Share to Facebook, Instagram and X | No | Yes |

:::release 2.1
Liking a comment is free. Replying to a comment is part of commenting, so it needs Pro.
:::

Riders with Pro (or the Pro Trial) show a gold **PRO** tag next to their name. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Keep It Friendly

If a post or comment shouldn't be there, tap **⋯** on the post (or **Report** under a comment) and pick a reason. A post or comment that several riders report is hidden until the OnMyLead team looks at it, and the team removes ones that break the rules. Blocked riders never see your posts or comments, and you never see theirs. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

:::release 2.1
When a comment is hidden, the replies under it are hidden with it.
:::

To stop likes and comments notifications, turn off **Likes and Comments** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).
