articles.summary: See your Starlink dish's live status on its Wi-Fi, keep your plan details handy, and work out how long your batteries will run it.
articles.text:
---
title: Starlink Dish Status and Power Planner
summary: See your Starlink dish's live status on its Wi-Fi, keep your plan details handy, and work out how long your batteries will run it.
category: account
order: 60
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:

keywords: [starlink, dish, satellite internet, mini, roam, battery, power station, solar, watts, runtime, obstruction, latency]
---

The Starlink page shows how your dish is doing, keeps your plan details in one place, and works out how long your batteries will run it.

## Open the Starlink Page

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **On the Trail**, tap **Starlink**.

## See Your Dish's Live Status

1. Join your Starlink's Wi-Fi network on your iPhone.
2. On the Starlink page, tap **Connect to My Dish**.
3. If your iPhone asks to let OnMyLead find devices on your local network, allow it.

While the page is open, **Your Dish** stays live and shows:

- Whether the dish is online, and its current state.
- **Download Now**, **Upload Now** and **Latency**.
- **Sky Blocked**, **Dropped Pings** and **Up For**.
- Any alerts from the dish.
- The last 15 minutes as a bar chart, with dropouts in red.
- Where the dish is facing, GPS, and its software and hardware versions.

After the first time, the page reconnects by itself when you open it. It stops reading the dish when you leave the page.

:::note
This uses your dish's built-in local connection, which SpaceX doesn't officially support. A Starlink update can break it. Everything else on the page keeps working.
:::

### If It Can't Reach Your Dish

If you see **Can't Reach Your Dish**:

- Make sure your iPhone is on your Starlink Wi-Fi.
- Allow local network access in your iPhone's **Settings**, under **OnMyLead**.

The page keeps trying every 10 seconds. Tap **Retry Now** to try straight away. If it says your dish answered but couldn't be read, a Starlink software update may have changed things. Try again later.

Reading the dish only works in the iPhone app, not on the website.

:::release 2.0
## RUS Starlink Mini Mount V2

Below **Your Dish**, the Starlink page shows an ad for the RUS Offroad Starlink Mini Mount V2 (Morelock Series), a Starlink Mini mount that installs on a Milwaukee Packout and also works with magnets. Tap **Shop the Mount** to open its page at rusoffroad.com. The price comes from the RUS Offroad store when it can be reached, and shows $249 when it can't.
:::

## Save Your Plan

Starlink doesn't share plan or usage details with other apps, so you can jot them down here. Check your usage in the Starlink app.

1. If you have machines in your [Garage](/help/garage), pick one under **Setup For**, or **General**. Each one keeps its own setup.
2. Under **My Plan**, fill in **Plan**, **Monthly Cost ($)** and **Data Cap (GB)**.
3. Pick your **Dish** and what it's **Powered By**.
4. Add **Notes** like your mount, cable length or router settings.
5. Tap **Save**.

You need to be signed in to save.

## Plan Your Power

Under **Power Budget**:

1. Enter your **Dish Watts**. If you picked your dish, the typical range is shown.
2. Enter **Hours per Day** you'll run it.
3. Under **Battery Size In**, choose **Watt-Hours** or **Amp-Hours + Volts**, then enter your battery size.
4. Set **Usable %**. Use about 90 for lithium and 50 for lead-acid.
5. If you have solar, enter **Solar Watts** and **Sun Hours** per day.

The page shows your **Battery Runtime**, what the **Dish Uses / Day**, what **Solar Adds / Day**, and your daily balance in green or red.

These are estimates. Snow melt, heat and heavy use draw more power. You can use the power calculator without signing in, but you need to sign in to save it.

articles.summary: Tell the whole group what's happening with one tap, see who got it, and take it back if you tapped by mistake.

title: Send a Status or Quick Reply
summary: Tell the whole group what's happening with one tap, see who got it, and take it back if you tapped by mistake.
category: ride-mode
order: 20
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06

keywords: [status, quick reply, need help, mechanical issue, flat tire, stuck, lost, need fuel, regroup, seen, receipts, cancel, on my way, running late, tablet, custom message, type a message, my quick replies]
screenshots:

---

Ride Mode has big buttons so you can tell the group what's going on without typing. Every rider on the ride sees your tap, and you can see whose phone has it.

![The status buttons in Ride Mode](/help/img/live.webp)

:::warning
Don't use your phone while you're moving. Pull over first, then tap.
:::

:::release 2.0
Typing your own message and saving your own quick replies are Pro features. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, the **Message** button carries a **Pro** tag. The status buttons, Need Help, EMERGENCY and Mechanical Issue stay free.
:::

## Quick Replies

:::until 2.0
The four blue buttons send a short message to the group. They also show in the ride chat.
:::

:::release 2.0
Quick replies send a short message to the group. They also show in the ride chat. **On My Way**, **Need a Minute** and **All Good** sit on the bottom panel. Tap **More** for **Running Late**, **Beverage Break** and every status.
:::

- **On My Way**
- **Running Late**
- **Need a Minute**
- **All Good**
:::release 2.0
- **Beverage Break**
:::

:::release 2.0
## Type Your Own Message

Need to say something the buttons don't cover, like "Gas stop at the next town"? Pull over first, then:

1. Tap **Message** at the top left of the bottom panel (across from **Full Map**).
2. Type your message. It's one line of up to 120 characters, and the counter shows how many are left.
3. Tap **Send to Everyone**, or the send key on your keyboard.

![Message the Group in Ride Mode, with two saved quick replies above the message box](/help/img/ride-message.webp)

It goes out just like a quick reply: the same **Sending** and **Sent to the Group** card with a light for each rider, **Cancel** to take it back, and it waits for signal if you have none. Riders get a notification titled with your name and the message, and it shows in the ride chat in italics.

To put the keyboard away without sending, tap **Done** above it on iPhone and iPad, use the back key on Android, or swipe the sheet down.

### My Quick Replies

Check **Save as One of My Quick Replies** before you send, and the message is kept on this phone or tablet. Next time, tap **Message** and tap it under **My Quick Replies** to send it in one tap. You can keep up to 6; saving a seventh drops the oldest. Tap **Edit**, then a reply, to remove it. Saved replies stay on the device you saved them on.

On a tablet the message sheet opens as a card in the middle of the screen.
:::

## Status Buttons

:::until 2.0
The grid below sets your status for the group:
:::

:::release 2.0
Tap **More** on the bottom panel to open **Tell the Group**. It has every quick reply, then your status, in two groups: **On the Move** (**OK** and **Stopped**) and **Trouble** (**Need Fuel**, **Mechanical Issue**, **Flat Tire**, **Stuck**, **Lost** and **Need Help**). **Regroup Here** (for organizers and leaders) and **EMERGENCY** are at the bottom. Tap one to send it; the sheet closes so you see the **Sending** card. Swipe the sheet down or tap **Done** to close it without sending.

The statuses:
:::

- **OK**
- **Stopped**
- **Need Fuel**
- **Mechanical Issue**
- **Flat Tire**
- **Stuck**
- **Lost**
- **Need Help**
- **EMERGENCY**

**Need Help** sends right away and shows in red for the group. **EMERGENCY** asks you to confirm first. See [Emergencies and Safety](/help/emergency-and-safety).

:::release 2.1
An EMERGENCY also sounds a siren on every other rider's phone until they silence it. See [Hear the Emergency Siren](/help/emergency-siren).
:::

:::release 1.0.3
In [Full Map](/help/ride-mode), the quick replies and status buttons are tucked away and only **EMERGENCY** stays on screen.
:::

:::until 2.0
Tap **Menus ▲** to bring the rest back.
:::

:::release 2.0
Tap **Controls**, or swipe the bar up, to bring the rest back.
:::

## Send a Status

1. In Ride Mode, tap a quick reply or a status button.
2. A card appears above the buttons. It says **Sending**, then **Sent to the Group**.
3. Watch the row of lights on the card, one per rider, with their first initial:
   - A solid green light means that rider's app has it.
   - A blue ring means a notification went to their phone, but their app hasn't shown it yet.
   - An empty light means it hasn't reached them yet.

Under the headline, the card spells it out, for example "Seen by Sam and Alex. 2 notified by push." or "All 5 riders got it." Tap **✕** to hide the card. It also goes away on its own after 10 minutes.

:::release 2.1
A blue ring also means a nearby rider's phone got it over Bluetooth, and the line says **Reached Sam over Bluetooth** until it shows on their screen. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
:::

## Take It Back

Tapped the wrong button? Tap **Cancel** on the card. The status or quick reply is taken back for everyone, the group is told to ignore it, and the notification they got is replaced with one saying you cancelled it.

## With No Signal

If your tap can't go out within a few seconds, the card says **Is Waiting for Signal**. Your tap is saved on your phone and sends by itself when you get service, stamped with the time you tapped it. Tap **Retry Now** to try again right away, or **Cancel** to drop it.

:::release 2.1
While it waits, riders close by on the same ride still get it over Bluetooth, and the card names them: **No signal here. Seen by Sam over Bluetooth.** If one of their phones gets signal first, it sends it for you. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
:::

## Clear Your Status

While your status is anything other than OK, a card on your screen says **Your Status** and what you sent, with a reminder that the group sees it until you mark it resolved. Tap **Resolved, I'm OK** when you're sorted. This sends **OK** to the group.

## Mechanical Issue

**Mechanical Issue** is for a machine that has broken down.

- Your spot shows on the map with an amber wrench, even if you aren't sharing your location. It uses where you were when you tapped.
- The leader, tail gunner and organizers hear it read aloud the moment you tap it, and it stays on their screen until you send another status.
- Your screen shows **Mechanical Issue** with **Fixed, I'm OK**. Tap it once you're rolling again.

**Mechanical Issue** and **EMERGENCY** stay on screen even when you fold the bottom panel away.

## When Another Rider Taps a Status

- A card shows their name, their status and how long ago they tapped it, such as "Sam: Flat Tire, 2 min ago". Tap **Navigate** to get directions to them, or **✕** to hide it on your screen only.
- Calls drop off the list after 30 minutes. A Mechanical Issue stays until that rider sends another status.
- You get a notification on your phone. Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts are always on, even in quiet hours. Other statuses and quick replies follow your **Rider Status** setting. See [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Regroup at My Location

:::until 2.0
Organizers, co-organizers and leaders see a **Regroup at My Location** button above the quick replies. Tap it to set a regroup point where you are.

- Everyone on the ride sees a yellow pin on the map and a yellow banner, **Regroup point set. Tap to navigate**, and hears "Regroup point set."
:::

:::release 2.0
Organizers, co-organizers and leaders see a white **Regroup Here** button at the bottom of the panel, next to **EMERGENCY** (it's also in **More**). Tap it to set a regroup point where you are.

- Everyone on the ride sees a yellow pin on the map and an amber-edged banner, **Regroup point set. Tap to navigate**, and hears "Regroup point set."
:::
- Tapping the banner opens directions to the regroup point.
- Setting a new regroup point replaces the old one.

Leaders can also tap **Regroup** on a separation alert. See [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble).

OnMyLead Pro adds unlimited rides, offline maps, GPX import, saved riding groups and more. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) for the full list.

## Prices

| Plan | US Price |
|---|---|
| **Monthly** | $4.99 a month |
| **Annual** | $29.99 a year, about $2.50 a month. Saves about 50% compared with paying monthly. |

Outside the US, the app shows the price in your local currency.

## Subscribe

:::release 2.0
Invited by a friend, or invited one? When the new rider finishes their first ride, you both get Pro Annual at 50% off for the first year. See [Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro](/help/refer-a-friend).
:::


1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Upgrade to Pro**. During your free trial, this button says **Keep Pro After the Trial**.
3. Choose **Annual** (marked **Best Value**) or **Monthly**.
4. Tap the **Subscribe for** button under the plans, for example **Subscribe for $29.99 a Year**.
5. Confirm the purchase in Apple's window.

On Android, step 5 is Google Play's window instead, and the payment goes to your Google Play account.

When it's done, the app says **You’re on OnMyLead Pro. Thanks for riding with us.** and your plan shows **Pro**.

You can also reach the Pro screen by tapping **See OnMyLead Pro** on any Pro prompt, or **Unlimited With Pro** on the Create a Ride screen.

:::note
You can subscribe in the OnMyLead app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. The website can't sell subscriptions, but Pro you buy in the app also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.
:::

## Already Have Pro From the Other Store?

Pro belongs to your OnMyLead account, so a subscription from the App Store works on Android and one from Google Play works on iPhone and iPad. If you already pay for Pro through one store, the Pro screen on a device that uses the other store says so instead of showing the plans, so you aren't charged twice. To move your subscription to the other store, cancel it in the store you pay now and subscribe on the other device after it ends.

## Billing

- Payment is charged to your Apple Account when you confirm the purchase.
- The subscription renews automatically unless you turn it off at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Renewal is charged within the 24 hours before the period ends.
- You can manage or cancel anytime in your Apple Account settings. See [Manage or Cancel Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).
- On Android, payment is charged to your Google Play account when you confirm. The subscription renews automatically at the end of each period until you cancel it in Google Play, and Pro stays on until the end of the period you paid for.
- The free Pro Trial for new accounts is separate. It needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription on its own.

The Pro screen links to the **Terms of Use** and **Privacy Policy**.

## If Something Goes Wrong

- **"Waiting on Apple to approve the purchase."** This happens with Ask to Buy or when your bank needs to check the payment. Once it's approved, Pro starts on its own.
- **"Waiting on Google Play to approve the purchase."** This happens when you pay with a method Google confirms later, such as cash at a store. Pro starts on its own once the payment goes through.
- **"The purchase didn’t go through. You weren’t charged."** Check your connection and try again.
- **Your plan still says Free after buying.** Make sure you have signal, then close and reopen the app. If it still says Free, tap **Restore Purchases**. See [Restore Purchases](/help/restore-purchases).

title: Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device
summary: Sign in with the same account on your iPhone, iPad, Android phone, tablet or the website, and your settings and Map Mode trails follow you.

keywords: [sync, cloud, backup, two phones, ipad and iphone, new phone, same account, settings, devices, restore trails]
---

Sign in with the same account on every device you use (iPhone, iPad, Android phone or tablet, and onmylead.com) and OnMyLead keeps them in step. Change a setting on your phone and your tablet has it too. Record a trail on your phone and it's in My Trails on your iPad.

Your rides, chats, friends, groups, Garage, trips, Starlink setup, notification settings and profile were always kept with your account. Now your app settings and your own trails are too.

:::release 2.0
Syncing your settings and trails is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, the **Sync** row on the You tab carries a **Pro** tag. Your account, rides, chats, friends and groups are on every device for free.
:::

## What Follows Your Account

**Settings**

- The map style (Satellite or Topo) and the trail layer switch
- **Rider Trails on Maps** and **Follow Me on Maps**
:::release 2.1
- **Zoom In at Intersections**
- **Zoom Out at the Edge**
- **Dot Style** and **Dot Size**
:::
- The **Track Line** switch (the line itself stays on each device, see below)
- **Directions**: which maps app Navigate opens. If you picked Apple Maps, an Android phone asks each time, since it doesn't have Apple Maps.
- **Music Controls**
- **Appearance**: Dark, Light or Match Phone, your theme and Color Blind Mode
- **Language**: the language you picked, or Match Phone (then each device follows its own language)
- **Tilt**: your warning angles, Warn Me, the spoken warnings, the Tilt Meter switch, and Crash Alert (the Zero stays on each device)
- **Voice**: the voice that speaks your alerts. A device that doesn't have that voice uses its best one.
- Your saved quick replies for ride chat
- Which panels you keep open or folded in Ride Mode, Map Mode, Route Builder and Waypoints
- The search distance in Find a Ride and Events
- Announcements you closed, and the Starlink page connecting by itself

**Map Mode trails**

Every trail in **My Trails** (ones you recorded, drew or saved from other riders), with its details, named spots and photos, is backed up privately to your account. Sign in on another device and they're there. Delete a trail on one device and it's deleted on the others too.

The backup is private: only you can see it. Sharing still works exactly as before. A trail only becomes public when you tap **Share with Everyone**.

:::release 2.1
**Map Mode waypoints**

Waypoints you drop in Map Mode on your own (press and hold the map) are backed up privately the same way, so they show on your other devices, and a waypoint you remove on one is removed on the others. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops#press-and-hold-the-map).
:::

**Offline map areas**

The areas you download aren't copied between devices (they're big), but your other devices know about them. Open **Offline Maps** on another phone or tablet and they're listed under **On Your Other Devices**. Tap **Download** to save the same area on this one, or **Hide** to stop seeing it. Downloading is part of Pro, the same as any download.

## What Stays on Each Device

Some things are about one device, so they stay on it:

- **Battery Saver**: it's about this device's battery, and an iPad on the charger may not need it.
- **Track Line**: the line of where you've been is location history, so it never leaves the device.
- The tilt meter's **Zero**: each phone sits differently in its mount.
- A recording in progress (it backs up as soon as you save the trail).
- The downloaded map squares themselves.
- The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement: you agree once on each device you install OnMyLead on.

Your live location is never part of sync. It's only sent while you share it with a ride or with riders you pick, as always. See [Privacy and Your Location](/help/privacy).

## Check or Sync Now

1. Tap **You**.
2. Under **Settings**, **Sync Across Devices** says when this device last synced.
3. Tap it to sync right away.

Devices sync when you open the app, when you sign in, a moment after you change a setting or a trail, and when you tap **Sync Across Devices**. With no signal, your changes wait on the device and go up the next time you're connected.

If you change the same setting on two devices before either syncs, the change you made last wins. Other settings aren't affected.

## Signing In With a Different Account

Each account keeps its own settings and trails. If someone else signs in on your device, they get their own settings, and trails backed up to your account don't show in their My Trails. Trails made on the device before sync existed go to the first account that syncs them.

## Deleting Your Account

Deleting your account deletes the settings and trail backup kept with it. Trails you shared publicly follow the steps in [Delete Your Account](/help/delete-account).

articles.title: Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert
articles.summary: See your vehicle's roll and pitch, get warned before a steep lean, and have OnMyLead alert your group if it detects a crash.
articles.text:
---
title: Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert
summary: See your vehicle's roll and pitch, get warned before a steep lean, and have OnMyLead alert your group if it detects a crash.
category: safety-privacy
order: 52
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/tilt.tsx
  - app/src/components/tilt-gauge.tsx
  - app/src/components/tilt-tile.tsx
  - app/src/components/crash-countdown.tsx
  - app/src/core/tilt.ts
  - app/src/core/crash-detect.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-tilt.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-crash-alert.ts
  - app/src/lib/tilt.ts
  - app/src/lib/motion.ts
related: [emergency-and-safety, ride-mode, navigation-mode]
keywords: [tilt, inclinometer, roll, pitch, angle, side hill, off camber, rollover, crash detection, crash alert, accident, level]
---

The tilt meter shows how far your vehicle leans side to side (**Roll**) and tips nose up or down (**Pitch**), using the motion sensors in your phone or tablet. It works with no signal. Crash Alert uses the same sensors to spot a likely crash in Ride Mode and tell your group if you don't answer.

## See Your Tilt

The **Tilt** tile shows your roll and pitch over the map:

- In **Map Mode**, under your speed and the dash.
- In **Ride Mode**, on the left side of the map above the panel. On a tablet it sits in the map's bottom-left corner. It hides in Full Map and when there isn't room.

The numbers turn amber as you get close to your limit and red at it. Tap the tile to open the full **Tilt** screen, with an axle seen from behind that leans with your roll, two wheels seen from the side that tip with your pitch, and the biggest lean each way under each one. Tap **Reset Max** to clear those (it shows once the meter is calibrated).

You can also open it from the **You** tab: tap **Tilt and Crash Alert**. The screen stays on while it's open, so you can leave it up on your mount.

## Turn the Tilt Meter Off

Don't want it? At the top of the Tilt screen, under the Crash Alert switch, tap **Tilt Meter On** to turn it off. The Tilt tile leaves Map Mode and Ride Mode, the Tilt screen hides the readings, and tilt warnings stop. Crash Alert keeps working on its own switch. Tap **Tilt Meter Off** to bring it back. The switch follows your account to your other devices.

:::release 2.1
The same switch is under **Map Buttons** in **Map Settings**: tap the round **Map Settings** button on Ride Mode's or Map Mode's map and switch **Tilt Meter**.
:::

## Calibrate It for Your Mount

The tilt meter is off until you calibrate it, because your phone probably doesn't sit flat in its mount. Until then the Tilt screen shows **Calibrate** instead of readings, and the tile in Map Mode and Ride Mode says **Calibrate Tilt**. Tilt warnings don't buzz, and Crash Alert only watches for hard hits, not rollovers.

1. Place your phone where it will be mounted, with the vehicle on flat and level ground.
2. Open **Tilt** and press **Calibrate**, then **Calibrate** again to confirm.

That reading becomes level, and the meter turns on. After that the button says **Zero**: press it again whenever you move the phone or switch vehicles. The calibration is kept on this phone only, since each phone sits differently. Tap **Clear Zero** to remove it, which turns the meter off until you calibrate again.

## Tilt Warnings

With **Warn Me** on, your phone buzzes when you lean past your limit for more than a moment, and again every few seconds while you stay past it. Set your own limits with **Roll Limit** and **Pitch Limit** (10° to 45°; they start at 25° roll and 30° pitch). Turn on **Say It Out Loud** to also hear the angle, such as "Roll 28 left".

:::warning
Every vehicle tips at a different angle, and load, tires and ground all change it. The limits are reminders, not a promise you won't roll.
:::

On a motorcycle, turn **Warn Me** off, since leaning into turns is normal. To hide the tile, turn the **Tilt Meter** off at the top of the screen. Your limits and these switches follow your account to your other devices.

## Crash Alert

Crash Alert is on unless you turn it off. To turn it on or off, open the Tilt screen and tap the **Crash Alert On** / **Crash Alert Off** switch at the top. The switch follows your account to your other devices. While Ride Mode is open, it watches for a hard hit or (once you've zeroed the tilt meter) a rollover while you're riding, followed by your vehicle stopping. When it sees one:

1. A full-screen countdown starts at 30 seconds, with vibration and a spoken warning.
2. Tap **I'm OK** to cancel. Nothing is sent.
3. If nobody taps **I'm OK**, your group gets the same **EMERGENCY** alert as the Emergency button, with your location, plus a chat message saying your phone detected a possible crash. Tap **Alert My Group Now** to send it straight away.
4. To cancel and stop Crash Alert for now, tap **I'm OK, Turn Off Crash Alert** under the buttons. Turn it back on from the top of the Tilt screen.

:::release 2.1
If a sheet such as **Map Settings** is open when the countdown starts, it steps aside so the countdown can fill the screen, and comes back once the countdown has gone. The 30 seconds start once the countdown is on screen (it waits at most 2 seconds for the sheet).
:::

Choose how easily it goes off under **Sensitivity** on the Tilt screen: **Low** (only very hard hits and full rollovers, fewer false alarms on rough trails), **Normal** (recommended) or **High** (also smaller hits and steep tips). A hard bump you keep riding through doesn't count, and neither does knocking the phone while parked. Dropping your phone doesn't count either: Crash Alert notices the moment of falling and ignores the landing, and a dropped phone lying at an angle doesn't count as a rollover until it's back in its mount. If something still sets it off by mistake, tap **I'm OK**.

:::warning
Crash Alert tells your group only. It doesn't call 911 or emergency services. It only works while Ride Mode is open and you've joined the ride. With no service the alert waits on your phone and sends as soon as it reconnects, and riders need service to receive it. See [Emergencies and Staying Safe](/help/emergency-and-safety).
:::

## Where It Works

The tilt meter and Crash Alert are in the app on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. They aren't on the website, because a computer has no motion sensors.

articles.summary: Make a packing checklist for a trip, tick things off as they go in the rig, and reset or copy it for next time.
articles.text:
---
title: Plan a Trip and Packing List
summary: Make a packing checklist for a trip, tick things off as they go in the rig, and reset or copy it for next time.
category: account
order: 50
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-05
sources:
  - app/src/app/trips/**
  - app/src/components/trip-form.tsx
  - app/src/core/trips.ts
  - app/src/core/pro.ts
  - app/src/lib/pro.ts
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx
  - app/src/components/app-notices.tsx
related: [garage, free-vs-pro, rus-gear, create-a-ride]
keywords: [trip, packing list, checklist, gear list, what to bring, camping, overnight, template, starter list, tablet]
---

The Trip Planner keeps a packing list for each trip. Tick items off as they go in the rig, and reuse the list next time.

## Open the Trip Planner

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Your Gear**, tap **Trip Planner**.

You need to be signed in.

## Plan a New Trip

1. Tap **Plan a New Trip**.
2. Enter a **Trip Name**, like "Moab long weekend".
3. Add dates if you like: **Starts** and **Ends**, written like 2026-10-12. **Ends** is optional.
4. If you have machines in your [Garage](/help/garage), pick the one you're **Taking**.
5. Tap **Create Trip**.

:::note
Free accounts plan one trip at a time. A trip counts until its last day has passed. Planning several trips at once is part of Pro. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

## Add Items

1. On the trip, tap **Add an Item**.
2. Enter the **Item**, like "Tow strap".
3. Set **How Many** with the number box or the minus and plus buttons.
4. Pick a **Category**, like **Recovery**, **First Aid**, **Camping** or **Food & Water**.
5. Add **Notes** if you like, such as size or where it lives in the rig.
6. Tap **Add**.

Items are grouped by category, each showing how many are packed.

## Start From a Starter List

Tap **Add a Starter List** and pick one, like **Day Ride**, **Overnight / Camping**, **Desert**, **Mountain / Snow**, **Recovery Kit**, **First Aid**, **Tools & Spares** or **Starlink / Power**. One tap adds the items. You can add more than one list, and nothing is added twice.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Tick Items Off

Tap anywhere on an item's row to check it off. Tap again to uncheck it. The bar at the top shows how much is packed. When everything is checked, it turns green and says so, like All 24 packed.

To change or remove an item, tap **Edit** on its row, then tap **Save** or **Remove Item**.

## After the Trip

Under **After the Trip**:

- **Uncheck All** puts every item back to not packed. The list stays.
- **Copy to a New Trip** starts a new trip with the same list. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

:::release 2.0
On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold **Pro** tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags.
:::

## Link a Trip to a Ride

When you create or edit a trip, you can pick a ride you've joined under **For a Ride**. The trip then shows a link to that ride.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Edit or Delete a Trip

1. Open the trip.
2. Tap **Edit Trip** to change the name, dates, machine or ride, then tap **Save**.
3. Or tap **Delete**, then confirm. The trip and all its items are removed.

## Gear Suggestions

A trip's page may show **Gear From RUS Offroad**, with products that fit your list and machine. See [Gear From RUS Offroad](/help/rus-gear).

summary: What to check when riders don't show on the map, alerts don't arrive, a download stops or sign-in fails.

release: "1.0"

related: [accurate-location, faq, ride-mode, location-sharing, offline-maps, notification-settings, contact-support]
keywords: [not working, problem, broken, bug, help, no signal, no service, alerts, download, password, tablet, wrong location, miles away, approximate, precise location]
---

Start here when something doesn't work the way you expect. If your problem isn't listed, [contact us](/help/contact-support).

## A Rider Shows as a Hollow Dot or "Last Seen"

A rider's dot turns hollow when their last position is more than a minute old, and shows **No Signal** with a dashed grey ring after about 3 minutes. A sharing phone checks in at least every 15 seconds while it has service, so this usually means that rider lost service.

:::release 1.0.3
:::until 2.1
A live rider's dot has a bold white ring (the leader's is solid blue). A last-seen rider's dot is a thin grey ring instead.
:::
:::

:::release 2.1
A live rider's dot is a solid disc with a white rim and an arrow inside it (blue for the leader, violet for the tail gunner, graphite for everyone else). A last-seen rider's dot is a thin grey ring with no arrow instead.
:::

If **everyone** suddenly shows as last seen, it's probably your phone. After about 35 seconds without hearing from the server, Ride Mode shows **No Service. Riders Show Where They Were Last Seen**. It doesn't mark the others as lost because of your own dropout.

See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

## A Rider Shows Miles From Where They Are

If a rider right beside you shows up a mile or two away, their phone is giving every app a rough location (Google Maps or Apple Maps on that phone shows the same wrong spot). On that phone, turn on **Precise Location** for OnMyLead and, on Android, **Google Location Accuracy**, then calibrate. Step by step: [Make Your Location Accurate](/help/accurate-location).

## My Group Can't See Me With My Phone Locked

1. Open your iPhone's **Settings > OnMyLead > Location**.
2. Choose **Always**.
3. Open Ride Mode again. If your share is still running, it picks back up.

On Android, check that the **Sharing Your Location** notification is showing while you share. If it isn't, open Ride Mode again to restart it. If your phone has a battery saver that closes apps, set OnMyLead's battery use to **Unrestricted** in **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Battery**.

:::release 1.0.1
If sharing drains your battery too fast on long days, try [Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver). Your group sees you less often, so switch back to **Best Accuracy** when you can charge.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
If Ride Mode shows **Location Is Off**, location is turned off for OnMyLead, so your group can't see you move. Turn it back on in your phone's **Settings**, then open Ride Mode again.
:::

Closing Ride Mode or locking your phone doesn't stop sharing. Sharing ends when your timer runs out, the ride ends, you leave the ride, or you tap **Stop**.

## I Tapped a Status Button With No Signal

It waits on your phone as **Waiting for Signal** and sends by itself as soon as you have service, stamped with the time you tapped it. You can tap **Retry Now** or **Cancel**. See [Status Buttons](/help/status-buttons).

:::release 2.1
## Nearby Riders Don't Show Up Over Bluetooth

Bluetooth Sharing reaches about 30 to 100 meters between phones. Check that Bluetooth is on in the phone's settings, that OnMyLead is allowed to use Bluetooth (iPhone and iPad: **Settings > OnMyLead > Bluetooth**; Android: **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Permissions > Nearby devices**), that **Bluetooth Sharing** is on in the You tab (or the no-service banner in Ride Mode says **Bluetooth On**), and that you opened Ride Mode once with service. On Free, riders' spots and messages over Bluetooth don't show (they're Pro); status taps, including EMERGENCY, Need Help, Crash Alerts and I'm OK, still do. Riders only send their spot while they share with the ride. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
:::

## I'm Not Getting Alerts

1. Check that notifications are allowed for OnMyLead in your iPhone's **Settings > Notifications > OnMyLead**.
2. In the app, open **You** and check your [notification settings](/help/notification-settings), including quiet hours.

On Android, check **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Notifications**, including the **Rider Alerts**, **Ride Chat** and **Ride Updates** categories.

**Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** alerts from your group always come through, even in quiet hours, as long as iPhone notifications are allowed for OnMyLead.

:::release 2.0
## The Spoken Alerts Sound Robotic

Your phone may only have its small standard voice. Open **You** > **Voice** to hear the voices on your phone, and follow the steps there to download a free Premium or Enhanced voice. See [Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts](/help/voice).
:::

## Part of My Route Is a Straight Line

The route builder follows mapped trails. It draws a straight line when no mapped trail joins two points, when the points are very far apart, or when you had no signal and that trail data wasn't saved on your phone. Add a point on the trail or zoom in, or use **Straight Line** for unmapped ground. See [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).

## I Turned On Trails but See No Lines

:::until 1.0.2
Zoom in. Forest Service and BLM lines appear from about zoom level 9 (**Zoom In to See Trails**), and smaller park and local tracks need you to zoom in further (**Zoom In for Park and Local Trails**). The website shows fewer trail layers than the app. See [Map Layers](/help/map-layers).
:::

:::release 1.0.2
Zoom in. Forest Service and BLM lines appear when the map is about 60 miles across a phone screen (**Zoom In to See Trails**), and park and local tracks from OpenStreetMap when it's about 15 miles across (**Zoom In for Park and Local Trails**). The website shows fewer trail layers than the app. See [Map Layers](/help/map-layers).
:::

:::release 2.1
## I Turned On Land but See No Boundaries

Zoom in. National forests, BLM land and parks show once the map is about 60 miles across a phone screen (**Zoom In to See Land Boundaries**), and Texas property lines only when you're zoomed in to a few blocks. Land needs a signal to load. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).
:::

## My Offline Map Download Stopped

Closing the app pauses a running download. Open **You > Offline Maps** and tap **Resume**, or **Finish** if some pieces are missing. If the area says **Too big for one download**, zoom in so the frame covers less. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

:::release 2.1
## The 3D Map Went Flat

With no signal, Ride Mode and Map Mode show 3D Terrain only over an area you saved with **3D Terrain** ticked in Offline Maps. Anywhere else they show the flat downloaded map, so you still have a map. The 3D view comes back with signal. See [3D Terrain](/help/3d-terrain).
:::

## I Don't See a Fuel Check on My Ride

The fuel check needs miles to check against (a saved route or **Route Length (Miles)**) and a machine in your Garage with **Tank (gal)** and **Miles per Gallon** filled in. If you have more than one machine, pick yours under **Bringing** on the ride. See [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range).

## My Password Reset Link Says It Has Expired

Reset links work once and expire. Tap **Back to Sign In**, ask for a new link, and open it on the same iPhone. See [Sign In](/help/sign-in).

## The Starlink Page Can't Reach My Dish

Your iPhone has to be on the Starlink Wi-Fi, and OnMyLead needs Local Network access (**Settings > OnMyLead**). The page tries again every 10 seconds. It doesn't work on the website. See [Starlink](/help/starlink).

articles.title: Use OnMyLead on a Tablet
articles.summary: On an iPad or Android tablet the map fills the screen, with the riders, the ride details and your buttons beside it.
articles.text:
---
title: Use OnMyLead on a Tablet
summary: On an iPad or Android tablet the map fills the screen, with the riders, the ride details and your buttons beside it.
category: getting-started
order: 40
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/e/[code].tsx
  - app/src/core/layout.ts
  - app/src/hooks/use-layout.ts
  - app/src/components/tab-bar.tsx
  - app/src/components/two-pane.tsx
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx
  - app/src/app/(tabs)/find.tsx
  - app/src/app/r/[code].tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/live.tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/route.tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/waypoints.tsx
  - app/src/lib/orientation.ts
  - app/app.json
related: [ride-mode, route-builder, find-a-ride, getting-started]
keywords: [ipad, android tablet, tablet, landscape, split view, sidebar, big screen, rotate, multitasking]
---

OnMyLead works the same on a tablet as on a phone, with the same account, rides and Pro plan. A tablet just gets layouts made for the bigger screen: the map fills it, and the riders, the ride details and your buttons sit beside the map instead of on top of it.

:::release 2.0
Using OnMyLead on a tablet or the website is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, a tablet or the website opens a screen with **Join a Ride**, **Your Rides**, **See OnMyLead Pro** and **Your Account**. Joining a ride, the ride page and Ride Mode always work, so you can follow the leader on any device for free.
:::

## Turn It Either Way

Hold the tablet upright or sideways; every screen works both ways. Phones stay upright.

You can also run OnMyLead next to another app (Split View or Slide Over on an iPad, split screen on Android). The layout follows the size of the window: in a narrow window you get the phone layout, and it switches back as the window grows.

## Getting Around

On a tablet, **Rides**, **Find**, **Groups** and **You** run down the left edge of the screen instead of along the bottom.
:::release 2.0
The blue **Map Mode** button sits under **Find** and opens your offroad map full screen.
:::

:::until 2.0
On **Rides**, with the tablet sideways, **Create a Ride**, **Join a Ride** and **Find a Ride** stay on the left and your rides are listed beside them.
:::

:::release 2.0
On **Rides**, with the tablet sideways, **Join a Ride**, **Create a Ride**, **Find a Ride**, **Events**, **Map Mode**, your toolkit and help stay on the left, and your rides, group, public rides, feed and badges are beside them. Upright, it's one column. See [Your Home Screen](/help/home-screen).
:::

## Ride Mode on a Tablet

The live map fills the screen.

- **Riders** sit in a list on the left with how fresh each rider's location is. Tap the arrow beside a rider to get directions to them. Tap **Hide**, or swipe the list to the left, to see more map; tap **Show Riders** to bring it back. The list starts open with the tablet sideways and folded with it upright.
- **Your buttons** (the route strip, quick replies and status buttons) sit in a panel on the right. Swipe it down or tap **Hide** to fold it, just like on a phone. **Mechanical Issue** and **EMERGENCY** always stay on screen.
- **Directions** and **Add Waypoint** sit just above the buttons panel.
- The ride name, your sharing timer and any announcement stay at the top of the left side.

:::release 2.0
Tap **Message** at the top of the buttons panel to type a message to the group. It opens as a card in the middle of the screen.
:::

:::release 1.0.3
On a tablet, Ride Mode's pop-up cards (Share Your Location, **EMERGENCY**) and sheets close when you swipe them down, just like on a phone.
:::

:::release 1.0.2
The round target button at the bottom of the map, just left of the buttons panel, centers the map on you. See [Use Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

:::release 2.0
**Follow Me** sits just left of that button and keeps the map moving with you as you ride. Drag the map to look around and it pauses; tap **Paused** to follow you again. See [Follow Me on the Map](/help/follow-me).
:::
:::

:::release 1.0.3
Tap **⤢ Full Map** at the top of the buttons panel to hide the riders list, the ride name and the buttons. A slim bar stays at the bottom right with the route line and **EMERGENCY**. See [Use Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).
:::

:::until 2.0
**Menus ▲** in that bar brings everything back.
:::

:::release 2.0
**Controls** in that bar brings everything back (or swipe the bar up). Navigate, Draw a Route, Waypoints and Find a Ride have **Full Map** too; on a tablet their bar sits in the bottom-left corner. See [Full Map](/help/full-map).
:::

## The Ride Page

Once you've joined a ride, the ride and its details stay on the left, and **Map**, **Riders** and **Chat** open on the right. You can read the chat or check the route without losing the meeting time and place.

:::release 2.0
**Leave Ride** is at the bottom of the left side of the ride page, and at the bottom of the **Riders** list in Ride Mode. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).
:::

:::release 2.1
## Scout on a Tablet

In [Scout](/help/scout) (**Find** > **Places to Ride**), the distance slider, the filters and the list of places sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen, sideways or upright. A place's page puts its details on the left and its map beside them.
:::

## Draw a Route and Add Waypoints

With the tablet sideways, the route tools and the waypoint list sit in a panel beside the map. Swipe the panel up or tap **Hide** to fold it. With the tablet upright, the panel floats in the bottom corner of the map; swipe it down to fold it.

:::release 2.1
A long swipe the way the panel folds (up beside the map, down when it floats at the bottom), or a swipe on the folded panel, goes straight to [Full Map](/help/full-map).
:::

## Find a Ride

Search and the list of rides sit on the left, with the map filling the rest of the screen.

:::note
Many tablets have no GPS. A Wi-Fi-only tablet can usually only tell roughly where it is, so share your location from your phone on the trail and use the tablet to follow the group.
:::

:::release 2.0
## Events on a Tablet

Events shows two events per row on a tablet in portrait and three in landscape. An event's page keeps its photo, details and hosts on the left, and the agenda, group rides and who's going on the right. See [Events](/help/events).
:::

articles.title: Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts
articles.summary: Pick the natural-sounding voice that reads Ride Mode alerts out loud, hear each one first, and download a better free voice that works with no service.
articles.text:
---
title: Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts
summary: Pick the natural-sounding voice that reads Ride Mode alerts out loud, hear each one first, and download a better free voice that works with no service.
category: ride-mode
order: 47
release: "2.0"
updated: 2026-11-04
sources:
  - app/src/app/voice.tsx
  - app/src/core/voice.ts
  - app/src/lib/voice.ts
related: [ride-mode, ride-bubble, status-buttons, music-controls, sync-across-devices]
keywords: [voice, speech, spoken alerts, text to speech, robot, robotic, read aloud, out loud, siri, premium voice, enhanced voice, helmet, headset]
---

Ride Mode reads some things out loud so you don't have to look at your phone: announcements from the leader, **Regroup Point Set**, a rider falling behind the group (leader and tail gunner) and a **Mechanical Issue** tap. OnMyLead reads them in the most natural voice on your phone, and you can pick a different one.

Every voice OnMyLead uses is stored on your phone, so spoken alerts keep working with no service.

:::release 2.0
Picking a voice is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, alerts are still read out loud with the **Automatic** voice. If you picked a voice before version 2.0, the app keeps it.
:::

:::release 2.1
Alerts are read in the language the app is in (see [Change the App's Language](/help/language)). If the voice you picked speaks a different language, your phone's own voice for the app's language reads them instead.
:::

## Pick a Voice

1. Go to the **You** tab and tap **Voice**.
2. **Automatic** is on to start. It uses the most natural voice on your phone, and the line under it says which one.
3. Tap **Play** next to any voice to hear it say "Regroup point set. Sam is falling behind."
4. Tap a voice to use it for spoken alerts. Tap **Automatic** to go back.

Voices marked **Premium** sound the most natural, then **Enhanced**, then **Standard**. On Android, voices don't have names, so they're listed by language, such as **US English Voice 1**, with **Natural** or **Standard** under each. If you delete the voice you picked, OnMyLead goes back to Automatic.

Your choice follows your account to every device you sign in on. A phone or tablet that doesn't have that voice uses its best one. See [Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device](/help/sync-across-devices).

## Get a More Natural Voice

Phones come with small standard voices, which can sound robotic. Better voices are a free download, and once downloaded they work with no service. If your phone has only standard voices, the Voice screen shows how to get one.

**iPhone and iPad:**

1. Open **Settings** > **Accessibility** > **Read & Speak** (**Spoken Content** on older iOS) > **Voices** > **English**.
2. Download a **Premium** or **Enhanced** voice, such as Zoe, Ava or Evan. You can play a sample there first. Premium voices are a few hundred MB, so download them on Wi-Fi.
3. Go back to OnMyLead's **Voice** screen and tap **Check Again**. Automatic picks the new voice.

Siri's own voice can't be used by apps.

**Android phones and tablets:**

1. Open **Settings** and search for **Text-to-speech**.
2. Choose **Speech Services by Google**, then **Install Voice Data**, and download your language.
3. Go back to OnMyLead's **Voice** screen and tap **Check Again**.

Voices that need an internet connection are never used, so alerts don't go quiet when you lose service.

**Website:** your browser decides which voices onmylead.com can use.

## Tips

- Spoken alerts play through whatever your phone is connected to: the speaker, earbuds or helmet comms.
- Spoken alerts still pause while your own phone has no service and other riders look quiet. See [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble).

articles.title: Waypoints and Planned Stops
articles.summary: Mark camp, fuel, water, a gate or a hazard on a ride's map, and let the leader plan numbered stops for the whole group.
articles.text:
---
title: Waypoints and Planned Stops
summary: Mark camp, fuel, water, a gate or a hazard on a ride's map, and let the leader plan numbered stops for the whole group.
category: routes-maps
order: 30
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-11-06
sources:
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/waypoints.tsx
  - supabase/migrations/20261105060000_release_fixes_pass2.sql
  - app/src/app/r/[code].tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/live.tsx
  - app/src/components/waypoint-sheet.tsx
  - app/src/components/time-picker.tsx
  - app/src/components/waypoint-row.tsx
  - app/src/components/waypoint-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/waypoint-mapbox-map.tsx
  - app/src/components/waypoint-map.web.tsx
  - app/src/components/map-search.tsx
  - app/src/hooks/use-ride-waypoints.ts
  - app/src/core/waypoints.ts
  - app/src/core/waypoint-symbols.ts
  - app/src/components/waypoint-blaze.tsx
  - app/src/lib/waypoints.ts
  - supabase/migrations/20261018500000_ride_waypoints.sql
  - supabase/migrations/20261019200000_planned_stops.sql
  - supabase/migrations/20261103400000_waypoint_symbols.sql
  - supabase/migrations/20261104150000_waypoint_alerts.sql
  - app/src/app/nav/index.tsx
  - app/src/hooks/use-map-mode-ride.ts
  - app/src/core/map-waypoints.ts
  - app/src/lib/map-waypoints.ts
  - supabase/functions/notify-ride-message/index.ts
related: [route-builder, leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner, ride-mode, navigation-mode, notification-settings, directions, privacy]
keywords: [press and hold, long press, tap and hold, waypoint alert, new waypoint notification, map mode waypoint, search, find a place, waypoint, pin, marker, symbol, icon, camp, fuel stop, lunch stop, hazard, viewpoint, parking, gate, trailhead, water crossing, food, restroom, first aid, repair, photo spot, color blind, planned stop, stops]
screenshots:
  - file: waypoints.webp
    shows: app/src/app/ride/[id]/waypoints.tsx
---

Waypoints are named spots you drop on a ride's map, such as camp, fuel, water, a viewpoint, a hazard or parking. Your own waypoints are only for you. The ride's leader can also share waypoints with everyone on the ride, and plan numbered stops the whole group will make.

![Planned stops and waypoints on a ride](/help/img/waypoints.webp)

Waypoints are never public. Shared ones and planned stops show only to riders on that ride.

:::release 2.0
Adding waypoints and planned stops is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free account, **Add Waypoint**, **Add a Waypoint**, **Add a Planned Stop** and **Add at My Location** carry a **Pro** tag. Seeing the leader's waypoints and stops on a ride, and following them in Ride Mode, stay free.
:::

## Who Sees What

- **Your waypoints**: only you see them, unless you can share (below).
- **Shared waypoints**: the leader or an organizer can share a waypoint with everyone on the ride.
- **Planned stops**: always shared. Every rider sees them numbered on the map, in order.

The leader is the rider with the Leader role, or the organizer when nobody has it. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

You need to have joined the ride to add or see its waypoints.

## Add a Waypoint

1. Open the ride and tap the **Map** tab.
2. Under **Waypoints**, tap **Add a Waypoint** (or **Open Waypoints Map** if there are some already).
3. Press and hold the map where you want it (click it on onmylead.com). To mark where you're standing, tap **Add at My Location** instead.
:::until 2.0
4. Pick what it is: **Spot**, **Camp**, **Fuel**, **Water**, **Viewpoint**, **Hazard** or **Parking**. The name fills in for you.
:::
:::release 2.0
4. Pick its symbol. The name fills in for you. See [Waypoint Symbols](#waypoint-symbols) below.
:::
5. Change the **Name** if you like, and add a **Note (Optional)**.
6. If you're the leader or an organizer, choose who it's for under **What It Is** (see below).
7. Tap **Save Waypoint**.

:::release 1.0.3
Changed your mind? Swipe the sheet down, or tap **Cancel**, to close it without saving.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
To find a spot by name, tap **Search** at the top of the waypoints map and type a park, trailhead, town or address, such as "Hidden Falls Adventure Park". Pick a result and the map moves there and labels it. Then press and hold (or click) the map at that spot to drop the waypoint. Search only moves the map; nothing is added until you drop it. See [Search for a Place](/help/place-search).
:::

In Ride Mode, tap **Add Waypoint** to drop one where you are, or press and hold the map. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

:::release 2.1
## Press and Hold the Map

In Ride Mode and Map Mode, press and hold anywhere on the map. The **New Waypoint** sheet opens for that spot: pick a symbol, change the name if you like, add a note and tap **Save Waypoint**. On onmylead.com, right-click the map in Map Mode instead (or press and hold on a touch screen).

- **On a group ride** (Ride Mode, or Map Mode while you're sharing your location with a live ride): the waypoint goes on that ride. If you're the leader or an organizer it starts as **Everyone on the Ride**, so the whole group sees it. Other riders' waypoints are just for them.
- **In Map Mode on your own**: the waypoint is yours and saved on your phone, so it works with no signal. With [Sync Across Devices](/help/sync-across-devices) (Pro) it also shows on your other devices.

While the **Draw** tab is open in Map Mode, taps add points to the line, so press and hold doesn't drop waypoints until you switch tabs.

To change one later, tap it on the map, then tap **Edit** (name, symbol, note) or **Remove**.

## New Waypoint Alerts

When the leader or an organizer shares a waypoint or a planned stop while the ride is live, everyone else on the ride gets a notification with a sound, like "Lou added a new waypoint: Fuel Stop". Tap it to open Ride Mode with that waypoint showing. It also goes into your [Notifications](/help/notifications-inbox).

- It goes out once per waypoint: when it's added for everyone, or when a **Just Me** waypoint is switched to **Everyone on the Ride**. Editing it afterwards, or switching it to **Just Me** and back, doesn't send another.
- Waypoints set up before the ride starts don't send alerts. They're on the map when riders open Ride Mode.
- New waypoint alerts follow the **Announcements** switch in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings) and your quiet hours.
:::

Names can be up to 60 characters and notes up to 280.

:::release 2.0
## Waypoint Symbols

Every waypoint has a symbol, so you can tell what it is at a glance on the map. There are 15:

| Symbol | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| **Spot** | Anything else |
| **Camp** | A campsite or where you'll stay the night |
| **Fuel** | A gas station or fuel cache |
| **Water** | Drinking water or a refill |
| **Food** | Lunch, a restaurant or a snack stop |
| **Viewpoint** | A scenic overlook |
| **Photo Spot** | A good place for group photos |
| **Hazard** | A washout, drop-off or anything to watch for |
| **Water Crossing** | A creek or river crossing |
| **Gate** | A gate to open and close behind the group |
| **Trailhead** | Where a trail starts |
| **Parking** | Trailer or vehicle parking |
| **Restroom** | A toilet or outhouse |
| **First Aid** | A first aid kit, clinic or help point |
| **Repair** | A shop, or a good place to work on a vehicle |

Each symbol has its own drawing, so they're easy to tell apart without relying on color, including for color-blind riders. **Hazard** and **Water Crossing** sit on a triangle instead of a diamond, so warnings stand out by shape. Shared waypoints are blue and your own are white.

A planned stop shows its symbol on a small white tag at the corner of its numbered stop sign, so everyone sees whether the stop is for fuel, food or camp.

To change a symbol, tap the waypoint, tap **Edit**, and pick another one.

The symbols show on the phone, the tablet and onmylead.com. Riders who haven't updated the app yet see the newer symbols as the closest older one (a **Gate** shows as a **Spot**, a **Water Crossing** as a **Hazard**) until they update.
:::

### Sharing a Waypoint (Leader and Organizers)

When the leader or an organizer adds a waypoint, they choose:

- **Planned Stop**: the whole ride stops here. Numbered on every rider's map.
- **Everyone on the Ride**: shows on every rider's map.
- **Just Me**: only you see it.

New waypoints from the leader or an organizer start as **Everyone on the Ride**, and you can switch to **Just Me**.

## Plan the Ride's Stops

Planned stops tell everyone where the group will stop for fuel, lunch or camp, and in what order.

1. Open the ride and tap the **Map** tab.
2. Under **Planned Stops**, tap **Add a Planned Stop**.
3. Press and hold the map where the group will stop.
4. Pick what it is and give it a name.
:::until 1.0.3
5. Add a **Planned Time (Optional)**, like "12:30 pm".
:::
:::release 1.0.3
5. To add a **Planned Time (Optional)**, tap **Add**, then tap **AM** or **PM**, the hour and the minute. It starts at 12:00 PM. Tap **Clear** to remove it.
:::
6. Tap **Save Planned Stop**.

Stops are numbered in the order you add them. To change the order:

1. Tap a planned stop on the map or in the list.
2. Tap **Move Earlier** or **Move Later**.

The leader or an organizer can edit any planned stop on the ride, even ones someone else added, so the plan carries on if the leader changes.

## View, Navigate, Edit or Remove

Tap a waypoint on the map or in the list to open it. You'll see its symbol, who it's from, the note and its coordinates.

- **Navigate**: get directions in your maps app. See [Directions](/help/directions).
- **Edit**: change it. You can edit your own waypoints. The leader or an organizer can also edit planned stops.
- **Remove**: take it off the map. You can remove your own. The leader or an organizer can also remove shared ones. When a shared waypoint is removed, everyone stops seeing it.

## On the Website

The waypoints map works on onmylead.com too. Click the map to drop a waypoint, and click a waypoint to open it.

:::release 2.1
From 2.1 the waypoints map is drawn by Mapbox on every device, so it looks the same on the phone and the website, and Ride Mode on the website has a live map where you can press and hold too. On the website, right-click a trail line to see its card. If the Mapbox map isn't available there, Ride Mode on the website shows the route sketch instead, so add ride waypoints from the ride's waypoints map.
:::

On a tablet held sideways, the waypoint list sits beside the map; swipe it up or tap **Hide** to fold it.

:::release 2.0
For the whole screen, tap **Full Map** on the panel's grab bar. Press and hold the map to drop waypoints as usual, and tap **Controls** (or swipe the bar up) to bring the list back. See [Full Map](/help/full-map).
:::

## No Signal

The waypoints you can see are saved on your phone, so they stay on the map without signal. The panel shows **Saved on This Phone** when that's what you're seeing.

## Limits

Each rider can add up to 100 waypoints on a ride. If you reach that, remove one to add another.

:::release 2.1
In Map Mode you can keep up to 2,000 waypoints of your own.
:::

:::note
Waypoints are different from the numbered points you tap when drawing a route. Route points shape the line; waypoints mark places along the way.
:::

OnMyLead 2.0 is the biggest update yet. It works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. Here are the big changes, with the guide for each. The full list is on the [Release Notes](/help/release-notes) page.

## The Big Changes

- **A new Home.** Join a Ride sits at the top with a box for the invite code, with Create a Ride and Find a Ride under it, then your next ride, your riding group, public rides near you and a Feed of your friends' rides. See [Your Home Screen](/help/home-screen).
- **Map Mode** (it was called Navigate). Your offroad map for when it's just you: speed, elevation, heading and trip, custom trails you draw yourself, Track Line of where you've been and named spots like water crossings. See [Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails](/help/navigation-mode).
- **Tilt Meter and Crash Alert.** See your roll and pitch over the map and get a warning before a steep lean. In Ride Mode, a hard hit or a rollover starts an I'm OK countdown, and if you don't answer, your group gets an EMERGENCY alert. It never calls 911. See [Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert](/help/tilt-and-crash-alert).
- **Events.** Rallies, poker runs and ride weekends on one page with the agenda and the group rides to join. See [Events](/help/events).
- **Social.** Like and comment on your friends' rides, badges and trails, and post ride reports with a photo. See [Like, Comment and Post in Social](/help/social).
- **Badges.** Earn Bronze, Silver and Gold and climb from Rookie to Legend, plus the OnMyLead Founder and Brand Ambassador badges. See [Earn Badges and Ranks](/help/badges-and-ranks).
- **Light mode and themes.** Dark, Light or Match Phone, four themes and Color Blind Mode. See [Change the Look](/help/appearance).
- **12 languages.** See [Change the App's Language](/help/language).
- **Sync across devices.** Your trails and settings follow you to every phone, tablet and the website you sign in on. See [Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device](/help/sync-across-devices).
- **A smoother Ride Mode,** with the leader line in order from the leader to the tail gunner, your own typed messages, Full Map, Follow Me and Music Controls. See [Use Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).
- **Invite Friends.** When a rider you invite finishes their first ride, you both save 50% on your first year of Pro Annual. See [Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro](/help/refer-a-friend).
- **New Free and Pro plans.** Joining rides, following the leader, Ride Mode and every safety feature stay free, and Map Mode is free for 8 hours a month. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Get the Update

Open the App Store on iPhone or iPad, or Google Play on Android, and update OnMyLead. Everything you had before, your rides, groups, garage and trails, is still there.

---

OnMyLead 2.1 keeps your group talking where the signal ends. It works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets, except CarPlay, which is iPhone only. Here are the big changes, with the guide for each. The full list is on the [Release Notes](/help/release-notes) page.

## The Big Changes

- **Bluetooth Sharing with no service.** When there's no cell service, phones on the same ride pass spots, status taps, messages and EMERGENCY to each other over Bluetooth, about 100 to 300 feet between phones, and every phone passes them along the group. Seeing riders and sharing your spot, taps and messages over Bluetooth is Pro. On every plan your phone passes everything along, and EMERGENCY, Need Help and Crash Alerts go out over Bluetooth. It isn't a satellite messenger and can't reach 911. See [Share With Nearby Riders With No Service](/help/bluetooth-sharing).
- **Emergency Siren.** When another rider on your ride sends EMERGENCY, or their Crash Alert goes out, your phone sounds a loud siren on a full-screen alert until you tap Silence Siren or Show Me Where. See [Hear the Emergency Siren](/help/emergency-siren).
- **Map Settings.** One round button in the top-left corner of every riding map opens everything about the map: the map style, roads, trails and land boundaries, how the map follows you, and your own dot. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).
- **A smoother map that keeps you on screen.** The map moves smoothly while you ride, your dot stays on screen, and the map zooms in at intersections so you see the turn. See [Follow Me on the Map](/help/follow-me).
- **A new rider dot.** Every live rider is a glossy dot with an arrow pointing the way they're heading: the leader in blue, the tail gunner in violet. With Pro you pick your own dot's style and size in Map Settings. See [Use Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).
- **Group Spread and Leader Trackline.** A measuring line under the rider line shows how far the last rider is behind the leader, and a blue line behind the leader shows exactly which way they went. See [Follow the Leader's Trackline](/help/leader-trackline).
- **3D Terrain.** Satellite on the real shape of the land in Ride Mode and Map Mode, and you can save it in Offline Maps. See [3D Terrain](/help/3d-terrain).
- **Badge Leaderboard.** See where you rank in your state, your country or everywhere, by the badges you earned riding. See [See the Badge Leaderboard](/help/badge-leaderboard).
- **Group Photos.** Give your riding group a photo of the crew. Everyone sees it; adding one is Pro. See [Create and Manage a Riding Group](/help/riding-groups).
- **CarPlay (Pro, iPhone).** Your ride on the car screen, with big buttons for status taps and EMERGENCY. See [Use OnMyLead on CarPlay](/help/carplay).
- **Edit Ride Details,** drop a waypoint by holding the map, Scout for places to ride and offroad park trails on every map. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride), [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops), [Find Places to Ride With Scout](/help/scout) and [Offroad Park Trails](/help/park-trails).
- **Always call 911.** The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement (version 2) says plainly that OnMyLead's alerts only reach riders on your ride. After you update, the Before You Ride screen shows once more so you can read it and tap I Agree. See [The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement](/help/rider-safety-agreement).
- **See your version.** The bottom of Home shows which version you have, like Version 2.1 (10).

## A Fresh Pro Trial

Bluetooth Sharing, CarPlay, customizing your dot and adding group photos are part of OnMyLead Pro from 2.1. So nobody loses anything the day 2.1 arrives, every rider who doesn't have Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial, and Home shows the date it ends. Safety stays free on every plan. See [Your Free 30-Day Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Get the Update

Open the App Store on iPhone or iPad, or Google Play on Android, and update OnMyLead. Everything you had before, your rides, groups, garage and trails, is still there.

The You tab's Help menu gained a Help Center link. Nothing these guides describe changed, so only the updated date moved.

In 2.0 the Create a Ride card is now dark like Find a Ride (red flag icon instead of a red background), and both cards fill and line up evenly. The guide now names the card by its look. Events now sits right under Join, Create and Find, above Map Mode (Chris asked to move it up). Other guides that describe the home screen were checked; only the tablet guide's list changed.
Fixed the Events database update so it installs on the live server (it called a random-code function by the wrong name). Events work the same; nothing riders see changed.

Chris supplied the product photo for the Starlink Mini Mount V2 ad; the app now always shows it, so only the price comes from the store. The ad's description now says it installs on a Milwaukee Packout and also works with magnets (Chris's wording). The ad shows $249 when the store can't be reached. Gear From RUS Offroad works the same (rus-match.ts only gained the ad's fixed details).
The website showcase's Map Mode picture now says Map Mode in its description (it said Navigate). Nothing riders do on the website changed.

Chris named the next release 2.0 instead of 1.0.4. Guides written for it now say 2.0 and publish when the stores release 2.0. Battery Saver and Fix Common Problems cite lib/location.ts, where only a code comment changed; riders see no difference.
Version bump to 1.0.4 (iOS build 8, Android versionCode 8). These guides cite app/app.json; nothing riders do changed, so the text stays. 1.0.4's new guides publish once the stores release it.
Chris asked for an ad for the RUS Starlink Mini Mount V2 (Morelock Series) on the Starlink page. The Starlink guide says where it shows and what Shop the Mount does, in a 2.0 release block.

Checked after the Starlink mount ad added an Admin switch (app-settings.ts) and product-lookup helpers (rus-match.ts, lib/rus.ts). Getting started and Gear From RUS Offroad work the same for riders, so no text changed.

Server-cost work, no rider-visible change: Ride Mode now listens only to its own riders' live positions, and the ride track uploads every 2 minutes instead of on every fix (the live dot still updates on every fix; stopping sharing sends the rest). Articles checked against the code; nothing they say changed.
Create an Event (Pro since the Events change) now carries the gold Pro tag on Free too; Events and Free and Pro say so.

Free riders now see a small gold Pro tag on every button that needs Pro (Chris: show a little Pro mark next to Pro features to encourage upgrading). The article lists where the tags appear, says tapping one opens the same Pro prompt, and that Pro Trial and Pro accounts never see them. Written in a 2.0 release block.
Each Pro feature's article now says the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold Pro tag on the Free plan and none during the Pro Trial or on Pro. Written in 2.0 release blocks.

Checked after the Pro tags change touched shared screens and components (Button, groups, route builder, trips, offline map buttons, entitlements, showcase). The only change riders see is the Pro tag, covered in Free and Pro and each Pro feature's article; these articles need no text change, so only their review dates moved. Home's gold now reads the shared Colors.gold (same colour), so Your Home Screen looks the same.

Chris asked for an Events area on the home screen where Pro riders post events with photos, details, dates and a place, an agenda (concerts, raffles, poker runs) and several group rides with other riders assigned to manage them. New Events article; the Events card on the home screen, Create Events in Free and Pro, and Report an Event, all for 2.0.

Events (2.0) touched shared files these articles list (the ride page gained a Part of [event] link, the Pro list gained Create Events, Create a Ride can link to an event). Nothing these articles describe changed for riders; dates bumped after checking.

Reviewed for the Social change. Shared code they list changed (Pro comparison rows and the new social_posts feature, the Likes and Comments notification setting, profile pictures that open full size in rider lists, chats, Friends and Out Riding, new Social routes, the Friends & Social toolkit tile). Their steps read the same; the new behavior is described in Social, Free vs Pro, Notification Settings, Profile Picture, Home Screen and Friends (2.0 blocks).

Chris asked for likes, comments and interaction on every feed item, a Social area with friends, activity and comments, posts on your profile, big profile pictures with small files, sharing to Facebook, Instagram and X, a PRO tag, and comment/post/share for Pro only. New Social article; Feed, Free vs Pro, Likes and Comments notifications, reporting posts and comments, privacy of posts and photos, and full-size profile pictures added in 2.0 release blocks. The unreleased Instagram rule now only flags Instagram sign-in, since sharing to Instagram is real.

Chris asked for a place to report a rider for abuse or harassment, with an email to the admin, timed suspensions or bans, and the admin able to read the conversation. Added You > Report a Rider, the Threats reason, what happens after a report (messages saved for the OnMyLead team only, 1 to 90 day suspensions or a ban), the suspended sign-in message, and a Reports section in Privacy. Written in 2.0 release blocks.

Checked after the abuse report change touched shared files (the You tab menu, the ride page, Going list, chats, direct messages, Out Riding, sign-in, report reasons in core/pro.ts and the app layout). Only reporting changed for riders, which is in Report or Block a Rider and Privacy; these articles' steps are the same, so no text changed.

2.0 redesigns Ride Mode and the map panels: a back button and sharing line under the ride name, glass panels, three quick replies plus More (a Tell the Group sheet with every status), Regroup Here beside EMERGENCY, amber-edged announcement and regroup banners, Map Style pictures for Satellite and Topo, and riders that glide instead of jumping. New text is in 2.0 release blocks; the old steps stay until 2.0 is live.

Checked against the 2.0 Ride Mode and map redesign: these screens changed color and spacing only (glass panels and buttons, smoother rider dots and Follow Me), so the steps and labels in these articles are unchanged. The onmylead.com home page gained one sentence about the smoother Ride Mode; nothing in the website or getting-started steps changed.

Coming in 2.0: the redesigned home screen. Join a Ride first with the code box, Create a Ride with rides left this month, Find a Ride, the Map Mode card, Your Group, Public Rides Near You with a distance you pick, a Feed you can customize (whose posts, which kinds, who sees yours), badges, a toolkit and Help & Support.

Coming in 2.0: these articles point to the new home screen (Join card with Join button, rides-left label on Create, Public Rides Near You and its distance, Plan a Group Ride from the group card, the two-column tablet layout, and who sees your Feed). Old steps stay in until-2.0 blocks.

Coming in 2.0: Navigate is renamed Map Mode. Measure becomes Draw with Map a Custom Trail and a How Custom Trails Work sheet (the take-down rule from the Admin Dashboard), Track Line draws where you've been in a colour per day, Mark a Spot names obstacles on drawn and recorded trails, and shared trails now show in full with an optional Hide My Start on recordings.

Checked after the 2.0 home screen change: their code changed only in code comments (Navigation Mode renamed Map Mode), the shared bottom sheet, the You tab's Map Mode label, or a Track Line hook in the location code that riders don't see unless they turn Track Line on. The steps in these articles are unchanged.

Coming in 2.0: every rider agrees to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement on a Before You Ride screen at first launch (and on onmylead.com after signing in), and again when it changes. New article explains what it says, how to agree, where to read it again (You tab > Safety Agreement, onmylead.com/rider-agreement) and the permanent record that's saved; the related guides point to it. Written in 2.0 release blocks.

Checked after the rider agreement change touched the You tab (a Safety Agreement link next to Terms and Privacy), the app's root layout, the website footer (a Rider Safety Agreement link) and the admin rider page. Nothing these guides describe changed for riders; the agreement itself is in its own article.

Fixed: a 4 mile test ride showed about 60 miles on the ride summary. Distance now leaves out rough locations, GPS bounces, jumps while the phone says it is standing still, and gaps with location off, and points from an earlier ride no longer join the next one. The articles say what counts; written in 1.0.4 release blocks.

Checked after the ride miles fix changed how lib/location.ts saves the ride track (per ride, with each fix's accuracy, skipping fixes rougher than 100 m). Sharing, Ride Mode and Battery Saver work the same for riders, so no text changed; what counts toward distance is in Ride Summary and Ride Again.

Coming in 1.0.4: a Music button in Ride Mode and Navigate (and the Full Map bar) to play, pause, skip and change the volume of the music on the phone. Android controls any music app; iPhone and iPad control Apple Music, plus volume for any app, because Apple allows no more. Riders can hide it. New article plus 1.0.4 release blocks in the related articles.
The You tab's On the Trail section gets a Music Controls switch in 1.0.4, which shows or hides the new Music button.
